text: Ana boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over her shoulder and a paper bag in one hand. She placed the canvas bag on the rack above her seat and set the paper bag beside her shoes. Across the aisle, a passenger pushed a leather bag under the table. The train passed fields and small stations while Ana removed a book from her bag. At noon, she opened the paper bag and ate the bread and sliced vegetables packed inside. She folded the empty bag, put it into the canvas bag, and returned the book to her lap. Several hours later, Ana carried her bag to the dining car and passed rows of bags tucked beside seats. “Tea, please,” she said, resting the bag near her chair. After drinking, she returned with the bag and watched towns, bridges, and farms pass the window. At dusk, she took a sweater from the bag and placed the book inside. When the train reached its final station, Ana lifted both bags and walked along the platform.
first_sentence: Ana boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over her shoulder and a paper bag in one hand.

text: Lukas boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over his shoulder and a paper bag in one hand. He placed the canvas bag on the rack and kept the paper bag beside him. Across the aisle, a passenger pushed a wheeled bag beneath a seat. Lukas opened his paper bag and removed a sandwich, a napkin, and an apple. At the next station, he watched travelers pass outside with bags of various sizes. A conductor moved through the carriage, stepping around a striped bag near the door. Lukas folded the empty paper bag and put it inside his canvas bag. During the afternoon, he took a book from the bag and read several chapters. Later, he carried the bag to the dining car and ordered tea. “This seat is free,” a passenger said, shifting a bag from a chair. Lukas sat, placed his bag by his shoes, and drank the tea. After nightfall, he returned to his compartment, used the bag as a footrest, and watched dark fields pass until the train reached its final platform.
first_sentence: Lukas boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over his shoulder and a paper bag in one hand.

text: Leila boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper bag in her hand. She placed the canvas bag on the rack and kept the paper bag beside her seat. As the train crossed the outer districts, she opened the paper bag and removed a bread roll. Across the aisle, a passenger pushed a wheeled bag beneath a table. Leila folded the empty paper bag, put it inside her canvas bag, and watched fields pass beyond the window. At noon, she took a book from the bag and read while the train followed a river. During a station stop, vendors passed the carriage carrying bags of fruit and bags of bottled water. Leila bought an apple, stored it in her bag, and returned the book to the same compartment. Hours later, she moved the canvas bag to the seat while another passenger reached for a suitcase. The train entered a wide plain, and Leila used the bag as a support for her folded coat. Near dusk, she lifted both bags and waited by the door for the final station.
first_sentence: Leila boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper bag in her hand.

text: Carlos boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper bag in his hand. He placed the canvas bag on the rack and kept the paper bag beside him. Across the aisle, a traveler pushed a wheeled bag beneath a seat. As the train crossed several towns, Carlos opened the paper bag and removed a sandwich, an apple, and a folded napkin. He returned the apple core to the bag and watched fields pass beyond the window. At noon, he took a book from the canvas bag and read while the train followed a wide river. A conductor passed through the carriage, stepping around bags near the seats. During a station stop, Carlos carried both bags onto the platform and walked beside a row of travelers with bags. “Ten minutes,” an attendant said, pointing toward the train. Carlos bought a bottle of water, placed it in the paper bag, and returned to his seat. After sunset, he used the canvas bag as a footrest until the train reached its final station.
first_sentence: Carlos boarded the morning train with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper bag in his hand.

text: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by placing a canvas bag beside the empty cabinets. She filled another bag with drawer handles, screws, hinges, and labeled packets of wall plugs. On the counter, a paper bag held paintbrushes while a plastic bag covered the faucet during sanding. Aisha carried each bag into the dining room before the workers removed the old cabinet doors. Later, she opened a bag of tile spacers and arranged them beside the backsplash. A large woven bag received the dusty cloths, empty tape rolls, and pieces of packaging. During lunch, Aisha passed a grocery bag containing bread, fruit, and bottled water to the workers. “The grout is in this bag,” she said, setting a small bag near the sink. By afternoon, a zippered bag held the drill bits, and a clear bag held receipts from the hardware shop. When the new shelves were fitted, Aisha returned each bag to the kitchen and sorted its contents. She left one reusable bag hanging from a hook beside the completed pantry.
first_sentence: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by placing a canvas bag beside the empty cabinets.

text: Diego began the kitchen renovation by setting a canvas bag of tools beside the bare cabinets. He carried another bag filled with screws, sandpaper, and measuring tape across the tiled floor. Near the doorway, three paper bags held cabinet handles, hinges, and labeled samples of paint. Diego opened each bag, checked its contents, and arranged the parts on a folding table. A contractor passed him a bag of spacers while the new countertop was aligned against the wall. After the measurements were recorded, Diego placed the unused spacers back in the bag. He then mixed grout in a bucket, keeping a bag of clean rags beside his stool. Fine dust went into a refuse bag, and strips of packaging went into a separate recycling bag. By late afternoon, Diego wiped the cabinet doors, folded the rag bag, and moved every supply bag into the pantry. The kitchen had new doors, a level counter, and several labeled bags ready for the next day.
first_sentence: Diego began the kitchen renovation by setting a canvas bag of tools beside the bare cabinets.

text: Lina began renovating the kitchen by placing a canvas bag beside the doorway for cabinet handles and loose screws. She carried a second bag of masking tape, brushes, and folded cloths to the counter. From a paper bag, she removed paint samples and held them against the walls. A contractor passed her a bag containing tile spacers while she measured the backsplash. Lina set that bag near a bag of grout and marked the cabinet positions. At noon, she opened a lunch bag, moved it away from the tools, and ate by the window. Afterward, she filled a small bag with old hinges removed from the drawers. Another bag held wooden knobs, which she sorted by size across the newly covered counter. She carried a bag of recycling past the unfinished pantry, then returned with a clean bag for packaging. Before leaving, Lina checked each labeled bag, wiped the tiles, and placed the remaining supply bags under the sink.
first_sentence: Lina began renovating the kitchen by placing a canvas bag beside the doorway for cabinet handles and loose screws.

text: Tariq began the kitchen renovation by setting a canvas bag beside the stripped cabinets. He opened the bag and removed a tape measure, pencil, and folded plan. A paper bag on the counter held screws and labeled hinges. He carried a second bag of cabinet handles past the sink and placed it near the drawers. Before sanding, he covered the faucet and stored its fittings in a small plastic bag. Dust went into a large bag while he worked along each cupboard frame. At midday, Tariq passed the grocery bag by the doorway and took out a wrapped sandwich. Afterward, he mixed grout, with the empty packets collected in another bag. A tile supplier arrived, and Tariq accepted a bag containing spacers and samples. He compared the samples, returned them to the bag, and laid the chosen tiles across the backsplash. By late afternoon, each tool was back in its bag, and the kitchen had new handles, clean joints, and an unfinished section near the stove.
first_sentence: Tariq began the kitchen renovation by setting a canvas bag beside the stripped cabinets.

text: Yara carried a canvas bag along the pavement to her grandmother’s apartment. Inside the bag were apples, a loaf of bread, and two library books. Her grandmother opened the door and pointed to a hook where Yara placed the bag. A shopping bag stood beside the umbrella rack, folded around several smaller bags. In the kitchen, Yara unpacked her bag while her grandmother filled a cloth bag with empty jars for recycling. They ate sliced bread and apples, then Yara took one book from the bag and read several pages aloud. Her grandmother brought out a sewing bag and replaced a loose button on Yara’s sleeve. Afterward, they walked downstairs, each carrying a bag, and put the jars into a collection bin. On the return trip, her grandmother used another bag to carry onions from a nearby shop. Back in the apartment, Yara packed both books into her canvas bag. “The bus comes at four,” her grandmother said, handing over the bag. Yara put the bag over her shoulder and left for the stop.
first_sentence: Yara carried a canvas bag along the pavement to her grandmother’s apartment.

text: Daniel carried a canvas bag up the steps to his grandmother’s apartment. She opened the door while he set the bag beside the umbrella stand. Inside the bag were bread, apples, a newspaper, and a small bag of tea. Daniel took the grocery bag to the kitchen and placed each item on the counter. His grandmother folded the empty bag and put it in a drawer with several other bags. On the table, a cloth bag held knitting needles and two balls of gray yarn. Daniel moved the bag to a chair before laying out plates for lunch. Afterward, his grandmother filled a paper bag with old magazines for the recycling bin. Daniel carried that bag downstairs, placed it in the bin, and returned with a reusable bag from the hallway hook. They packed containers of soup and biscuits into the reusable bag for Daniel to take home. At the door, Daniel lifted the bag, checked its handles, and left after saying, “I’ll visit next week.”
first_sentence: Daniel carried a canvas bag up the steps to his grandmother’s apartment.

text: Elena carried a canvas bag when she walked to her grandmother’s apartment after lunch. The bag held bread, two apples, a newspaper, and a small bag of tea. At the entrance, Elena passed a row of shopping bags beside the mailboxes. Her grandmother opened the door, took the tea bag, and placed it on the kitchen counter. Elena set her canvas bag on a chair and removed the bread and apples. A cloth bag hung from a hook near the stove, and paper bags filled a drawer below it. Her grandmother folded the empty tea bag wrapper and put it in a waste bag. Elena used another bag to carry potatoes from the pantry to the table. They washed the potatoes, sliced the bread, and packed several pieces into a storage bag. After eating, Elena gathered the newspaper and the folded shopping bags. Her grandmother placed three onions in Elena’s canvas bag for the trip home. Elena lifted the bag, checked its handles, and left the apartment before evening.
first_sentence: Elena carried a canvas bag when she walked to her grandmother’s apartment after lunch.

text: Patrick arrived at his grandfather's apartment carrying a canvas bag with bread, fruit, and a folded newspaper. His grandfather opened the door and pointed to a hook where Patrick hung the bag. In the kitchen, a paper bag stood beside the kettle, filled with potatoes and onions. Patrick emptied his canvas bag onto the table, then folded the paper bag and placed it in a drawer. His grandfather brought out another bag containing knitting wool, spare buttons, and two envelopes. Patrick carried that bag to the sitting room and set it beside the armchair. While tea steeped, he sorted the buttons into a small cloth bag and returned the wool to the larger bag. His grandfather handed him a shopping bag and a written list for the downstairs market. Patrick bought milk and oats, packed them in the bag, and brought the bag back upstairs. Before leaving, he put the empty canvas bag over his shoulder while his grandfather stored the shopping bag by the door.
first_sentence: Patrick arrived at his grandfather's apartment carrying a canvas bag with bread, fruit, and a folded newspaper.

text: Chloe began her bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the register and placing larger bags under the counter. She opened a bag of flour, measured several cups into the mixer, and folded the bag closed with a metal clip. While the dough turned, she carried a bag of sugar to the preparation table and refilled two labeled containers. A delivery worker passed her a bag of sesame seeds, which she set beside a bag of oats in the storeroom. After the first trays cooled, Chloe slid rolls into small bags and loaves into long paper bags. A customer requested six buns, so she filled a bag, folded its top, and attached a printed label. “One bag of buns,” Chloe said, passing the bag across the counter. Near midday, she emptied coffee grounds from a bag into the dispenser and put the flat bag in the recycling bin. Before leaving, Chloe counted the remaining bags, recorded the number, and placed a fresh bag beside each bread basket for the next shift.
first_sentence: Chloe began her bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the register and placing larger bags under the counter.

text: Kenji began his bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the register. He opened each bag slightly so loaves could slide inside without crushing their crusts. At the counter, he placed two baguettes in a long bag and folded the top twice. A customer requested rolls, and Kenji filled a smaller bag with six from the cooling rack. He passed the bag across the counter, then returned to label several bags for advance orders. Behind him, flour stood in a large bag near the mixing table. Kenji scooped flour from the bag, measured it into a bowl, and sealed the bag with a clip. During the afternoon, he carried a bag of sesame seeds to the workbench and scattered them over shaped dough. Empty bags remained in neat rows while filled bags accumulated beside the register. Near closing time, Kenji counted the remaining bags and wrote the number on an inventory sheet. He wiped crumbs from the bag shelf, packed one final loaf into a bag, and ended his shift.
first_sentence: Kenji began his bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the register.

text: Mira began her bakery shift by hanging her canvas bag beneath the counter and setting a stack of paper bags beside the register. She opened a flour bag, measured its contents into the mixer, and folded the empty bag for recycling. While the dough turned, she arranged rolls in a display basket and placed sliced loaves into clear bags. A customer indicated two buns, so Mira lifted a small bag and filled it with the requested items. “One bag is enough,” the customer said, and Mira closed the bag with a paper label. At the preparation table, she packed biscuits into larger bags, six to a bag, then lined the bags on a metal tray. She carried another bag of flour from the storeroom, passing shelves where sugar bags and seed bags stood in rows. Near closing time, Mira counted the remaining bread bags and wiped crumbs from the bagging station. She put an unsold loaf in a marked bag for collection, retrieved her canvas bag, and ended the shift.
first_sentence: Mira began her bakery shift by hanging her canvas bag beneath the counter and setting a stack of paper bags beside the register.

text: Andrei began his bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the counter. He opened each bag and folded its top outward for quick packing. A delivery worker carried a flour bag through the back door and set it near the mixer. Andrei emptied the flour bag into a storage bin, then placed the empty bag by the recycling shelf. At the ovens, he checked the bread and arranged cooling racks while a row of bags waited nearby. He slid two loaves into each large bag and sealed every bag with a printed label. A customer requested six rolls, so Andrei selected a smaller bag and filled it. “One bag of rolls,” he said, passing the bag across the counter. During the afternoon, he packed pastries in clear bags and placed the bags in shallow trays. He also moved a bag of sugar from the storeroom to the worktable. Before leaving, Andrei counted the remaining bags, tied the recycling bag, and set a fresh bag in the waste bin.
first_sentence: Andrei began his bakery shift by stacking paper bags beside the counter.

text: Ilse carried a blue canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair. She placed the bag beneath a table and removed three clear bags filled with soil, sand, and gravel. Beside each bag, she set a labeled cup and a folded instruction card. Her project compared how quickly water passed through the materials in each bag. A teacher handed her a small bag of paper clips, and Ilse used them to fasten a chart to a board. Visitors carrying tote bags stopped at the table while she poured equal amounts of water into the sample bags. The cups collected different volumes, which Ilse recorded on a sheet kept in the front pocket of her bag. At midday, she took a sandwich from a lunch bag and sat on a bench near the displays. Another student passed with a bag of model planets, followed by a parent with a bag of cords. After judging, Ilse returned the soil bags to containers, folded the empty bags, and packed her chart.
first_sentence: Ilse carried a blue canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair.

text: Wei carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair. Inside the bag, he had packed cardboard, tape, a notebook, and three sealed bags of soil. He placed the bag beneath his assigned table and arranged the soil bags beside a model greenhouse. Around him, students unpacked display boards from long bags and set supply bags near their chairs. Wei opened another bag containing labels, then attached one label to each soil bag. His project compared how water moved through sand, clay, and garden soil, with each sample stored in a clear bag. A teacher passed with a bag of extension cords and stopped to inspect his chart. “Explain the bags,” the teacher said. Wei pointed to each bag and described the measured drainage times recorded in his notebook. Later, visitors carried paper bags between tables while Wei poured equal amounts of water into cups above the sample bags. At closing time, he sealed every bag, folded the chart, and returned all materials to the canvas bag. He carried the bag out with the other students.
first_sentence: Wei carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair.

text: Sofia carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair. Inside the bag were cardboard strips, tape, a notebook, and three sealed plastic bags of soil. She placed the canvas bag beneath her assigned table and arranged the soil bags beside a row of clear cups. Her project compared how water moved through soil taken from each bag. A teacher passed with a bag of extension cords while Sofia poured measured soil from the first bag into a cup. She repeated the process with the second bag and wrote the measurements in her notebook. From the third bag, she added darker soil to another cup and set all three cups on a tray. Visitors carrying backpacks and paper bags stopped at the table to read her display. “Each bag holds a different soil sample,” Sofia said as she poured equal amounts of water. After the demonstration, she returned the sealed bags to the canvas bag. At closing time, Sofia packed the cups and notebook around the soil bags. She lifted the bag from beneath the table and walked out with the other students.
first_sentence: Sofia carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair.

text: Mateo carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair. Inside the bag, he had packed three jars, a notebook, tape, and labels. He placed the bag beneath his assigned table and removed a sealed plastic bag containing soil. Beside it, another bag held dry beans for his display about plant growth. Mateo arranged the bags in a row and attached measurement charts to a cardboard panel. A teacher passed by with a bag of extension cords and stopped to inspect the setup. “Explain the bags,” the teacher said. Mateo pointed to each bag and described how different amounts of water had affected the bean plants. During the next hour, students carried project bags between tables while visitors read the displays. Mateo returned each sample to its proper bag after every demonstration. At noon, he ate crackers from a small paper bag and recorded several questions in his notebook. When the fair ended, Mateo folded the charts, packed the jars into the canvas bag, and carried the bag out of the gym.
first_sentence: Mateo carried a canvas bag into the school gym for the science fair.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Nadia set her canvas bag beside the kitchen door and checked the delivery page for the package due that morning. The page showed the package in transit, so she placed a reusable bag in her coat pocket and went downstairs. In the lobby, she passed a row of grocery bags near the mailboxes and opened her empty parcel locker. A neighbor carrying a paper bag held the outer door while Nadia stepped onto the pavement. She walked to the corner shop, selected rice and soap, and packed both items into her reusable bag. At the counter, the clerk put the receipt beside the bag and said, “Deliveries usually come after noon.” Nadia carried the bag home and checked the lobby again. No package stood by the mailboxes, though two sealed bags of cat food rested near another door. Upstairs, she unpacked her shopping bag and folded it into a drawer. Before making lunch, Nadia put a tote bag near the entrance for the package, then read the unchanged tracking notice.
first_sentence: Nadia set her canvas bag beside the kitchen door and checked the delivery page for the package due that morning.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Javier set his canvas bag beside the door and checked the tracking page for the package. The page showed that the box remained at a local sorting center, so he placed his phone in the bag. On the kitchen counter, a paper bag held bread, onions, and a receipt from the morning market. Javier folded the top of the bag, then carried a reusable bag of bottles toward the recycling bins. In the hallway, he passed a neighbor holding a grocery bag and said, “The delivery has not arrived yet.” Outside, he emptied the bottle bag and tucked it beneath his arm. A courier crossed the courtyard with several bags, but none carried Javier’s apartment number. Back upstairs, Javier hung the empty bag on a hook and moved the paper bag away from the window. He checked the tracking page again while packing library books into his canvas bag. The status had not changed, and the package was scheduled for the next day. Javier zipped the bag, set it under a chair, and continued arranging the groceries.
first_sentence: Javier set his canvas bag beside the door and checked the tracking page for the package.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Nora set her canvas bag on the kitchen table and checked the delivery page for the package that had not arrived. Beside the bag, she placed the receipt, which listed the parcel as still in transit. She emptied a grocery bag, putting rice and oranges into the cupboard while the page refreshed. The package was supposed to contain reusable storage bags for the pantry, though the estimated date had passed. Nora folded the grocery bag and tucked it into a larger bag beneath the sink. At noon, she carried a shoulder bag downstairs and checked the building’s package shelf. Several parcels stood beside a paper bag, but none bore her address. She passed a neighbor holding two shopping bags and then returned upstairs with her shoulder bag. After lunch, Nora put the receipt into a small zippered bag with other household papers. The delivery page showed a new date, so she closed the laptop, hung the bag by the door, and continued sorting the pantry.
first_sentence: Nora set her canvas bag on the kitchen table and checked the delivery page for the package that had not arrived.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Oskar set his canvas bag beside the kitchen chair and checked the delivery page on his phone. The package listed there had not arrived, so he folded a reusable shopping bag and placed it inside the canvas bag. By the door, a paper bag held two jars and a loaf from the morning shop. Oskar lifted that bag onto the counter, then looked through the window at the building entrance. A courier passed outside with a large bag, but continued along the pavement without stopping. Oskar carried his canvas bag downstairs and checked the shelf where residents sometimes left parcels. The shelf held a padded bag of envelopes and a grocery bag, though neither bore his address. He returned upstairs, hung the canvas bag on a hook, and opened the paper bag for lunch. After eating, he put the empty paper bag into a recycling bag under the sink. The tracking page still showed the package in transit, and Oskar placed his phone beside the bag on the counter.
first_sentence: Oskar set his canvas bag beside the kitchen chair and checked the delivery page on his phone.

text: Beatriz arrived at the municipal pitch with a canvas bag over her shoulder and a second bag holding two footballs. Beside the bench, she placed each bag near the water bottles and changed into boots. A teammate opened a mesh bag, distributed training bibs, and passed the empty bag to Beatriz. She folded the bag and tucked it beneath her own bag before the amateur match began. During the first half, her bag remained beside the touchline while she played in midfield and completed several short passes. At halftime, Beatriz returned to the bag, removed a towel, and drank from a bottle stored in its side pocket. “Second half in five minutes,” someone said as she put the towel back in the bag. After play resumed, a loose ball rolled near the equipment bag, and Beatriz collected it for the throw-in. The match ended level, and she gathered the bibs into the mesh bag. Beatriz then carried both bags from the pitch to the changing room.
first_sentence: Beatriz arrived at the municipal pitch with a canvas bag over her shoulder and a second bag holding two footballs.

text: Bruno arrived at the public pitch carrying a canvas bag with his boots, socks, and water bottle inside. Beside the changing bench, several other bags stood in a row beneath the coat hooks. He opened his bag, changed his shoes, and placed his folded clothes back in the bag. A teammate brought a mesh bag of footballs onto the grass and passed one ball to the referee. Bruno carried the mesh bag to the halfway line while the teams took their positions. During the amateur match, his canvas bag remained beside the bench, between a blue bag and a striped bag. At halftime, Bruno walked over, removed his bottle from the bag, drank, and returned it. “Keep the ball bags here,” said a volunteer near the touchline. After the second half, Bruno gathered two spare balls and put them into the mesh bag. He then changed shoes again, packed his boots in his canvas bag, and left the pitch with the bag over one shoulder.
first_sentence: Bruno arrived at the public pitch carrying a canvas bag with his boots, socks, and water bottle inside.

text: Priya carried a blue bag across the park to the amateur football pitch. Beside the touchline, she placed the bag near several other kit bags. She opened her bag and removed boots, shin pads, a water bottle, and a folded shirt. The referee passed the row of bags while checking the white boundary markings. Priya put her shoes into the bag, tied her boots, and joined her teammates for passing drills. A substitute collected loose balls in a mesh bag and set the bag beside the bench. When the match began, Priya played in midfield, with the blue bag visible beyond the touchline. At halftime, she walked to the bag, took out her bottle, and returned it after drinking. The teams changed ends, and a coach shifted the bags so they remained behind the bench. Priya completed several passes and took one corner before the final whistle. Afterward, she removed her boots, wiped them with a cloth from the bag, and packed them inside. She lifted the bag, passed the mesh ball bag near the gate, and walked home.
first_sentence: Priya carried a blue bag across the park to the amateur football pitch.

text: Hiroshi arrived at the municipal field with a blue sports bag over his shoulder. He placed the bag beside the bench and took out boots, socks, and a water bottle. Around him, other amateur players set their bags in a row beneath the shelter. Hiroshi folded his jacket and put it into the bag before joining the warm-up. A spare ball rolled near the bags, and he carried it to the center circle. During the match, his bag remained by the bench while he played on the right side. At halftime, Hiroshi returned to the bag, drank from the bottle, and replaced it in a side pocket. A teammate asked for tape, so Hiroshi opened the bag and passed over a roll. After play resumed, he passed the ball several times and took one shot that went beside the goal. When the match ended, Hiroshi wiped his boots, packed them in the bag, and zipped it closed. He carried the bag past the other bags and walked toward the station.
first_sentence: Hiroshi arrived at the municipal field with a blue sports bag over his shoulder.

text: Yuki carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and set it beside the wall. A canvas bag held kitchen towels, wooden spoons, and a small clock. She placed a paper bag on the counter, then removed two cups and a jar of rice. In the bedroom, Yuki opened a large bag containing folded sheets and a gray blanket. Another bag stood near the closet with shoes arranged inside it. She passed an empty grocery bag while measuring the space beside the dresser. A neighbor left a bag of building information outside her door and said, “This is for new residents.” Yuki put the information bag beside her keys and returned to unpacking. By afternoon, several empty bags were stacked under the kitchen sink, while reusable bags hung from a hook. She filled one bag with flattened packing paper and carried it to the recycling room. Back upstairs, Yuki placed her work bag near the desk and checked each room. The last bag contained a lamp, which she set on a table before folding the bag.
first_sentence: Yuki carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and set it beside the wall.

text: Ravi carried the first bag through the apartment door and set it beside the blank wall. A second bag held plates, cups, and a folded kitchen towel. He placed that bag on the counter, then returned to the hallway for another bag. Near the elevator, a neighbor passed him while holding a paper bag of groceries. Ravi brought two canvas bags into the bedroom and removed sheets from one bag. The other bag contained hangers, socks, and a desk lamp wrapped in cloth. He folded each empty bag and stacked the bags inside a closet. In the bathroom, he unpacked a small bag of soap, towels, and cleaning supplies. A delivery worker arrived with a chair, and Ravi moved a bag away from the doorway. “Set it by the window,” he said, pointing past the bag. Before evening, he opened the final bag and arranged several books on a shelf. Ravi then put the last empty bag with the others, closed the closet, and checked each room.
first_sentence: Ravi carried the first bag through the apartment door and set it beside the blank wall.

text: Lucia carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and placed it beside the bare wall. A canvas bag held plates wrapped in towels, while a paper bag contained cups and spoons. She returned to the hallway for another bag, passing a neighbor near the stairs. The neighbor pointed toward a bag resting beside the elevator and said, “This one is yours.” Lucia took the bag inside and set it near the kitchen counter. From a large bag, she removed folded sheets, two pillows, and a small clock. Another bag supplied soap, a shower curtain, and a stack of washcloths for the bathroom. She emptied a grocery bag into the refrigerator, arranging jars on one shelf and vegetables in a drawer. By the window, Lucia opened a bag of books and placed each book along the built-in ledge. One final bag contained a lamp, extension cord, and several framed photographs. After flattening each empty paper bag, she stored the reusable bags under the sink and closed the cabinet.
first_sentence: Lucia carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and placed it beside the bare wall.

text: Henrik carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and set it beside the wall. A paper bag held cups, plates, and a roll of kitchen towels. He placed another bag on the counter, then removed jars and a small saucepan from it. In the bedroom, three bags stood beside the folded mattress. Henrik opened a blue bag, took out sheets, and spread them across the bed frame. A cloth bag contained socks, belts, and two window curtains. He passed the empty bags in the hallway while bringing in a lamp. Near the bathroom, a clear bag held soap, brushes, and bottles. A neighbor delivered a bag of spare hooks and said, “These fit the doors.” Henrik fixed one hook to the closet and hung a canvas bag from it. By late afternoon, he had flattened every paper bag and stacked the reusable bags under the sink. One final bag remained near the entrance, containing bread and fruit for his evening meal.
first_sentence: Henrik carried the first bag through the apartment doorway and set it beside the wall.

text: Clara carried a canvas bag into the clinic for her routine medical appointment. At the reception desk, she set the bag beside her chair and removed her identification card. The receptionist returned the card, and Clara slipped it into a small pocket inside the bag. Around her, other patients held shopping bags, work bags, and a paper bag from a pharmacy. When her name was called, she lifted the canvas bag and followed a nurse down the corridor. In the examination room, she placed the bag beneath a chair while the nurse recorded her weight and blood pressure. Clara then opened the bag to check a list of medications written in a notebook. The doctor reviewed the list, performed a standard examination, and placed an information sheet beside the bag. Clara folded the sheet, tucked it into the bag, and scheduled another visit at the front desk. Outside, she passed a rack of reusable bags, adjusted the strap of her own bag, and walked toward the bus stop.
first_sentence: Clara carried a canvas bag into the clinic for her routine medical appointment.

text: Kofi carried a brown canvas bag into the clinic for his routine appointment. At the reception desk, he placed the bag beside his chair and removed his identification card. The receptionist returned the card, and Kofi slipped it into a pocket of the bag. Across the room, two visitors kept shopping bags near their feet.
