first_sentence: Diego arrived at the town hall carrying a canvas bag with a notebook, a pen, and the printed council agenda.

text: Lina entered the town hall carrying a canvas bag filled with meeting papers, a notebook, and two pens. Beside the entrance, a table held reusable bags printed with the town seal. She placed her bag under a chair and took an agenda from a paper bag near the aisle. Council members arranged folders while residents set shopping bags and shoulder bags beside their seats. When public comments began, Lina lifted her bag onto her lap and removed the notebook. A clerk passed around a clear bag containing sample tiles for the proposed sidewalk project. Lina examined one tile, returned it to the bag, and wrote its dimensions beside the budget figures. During discussion of the market ordinance, a resident displayed a cloth produce bag as an example. “The bags can be washed,” the resident said. Lina closed her notebook, slipped it into her bag, and reviewed the final vote listed on the screen. After adjournment, she carried her bag past the remaining bags on the table and left the hall.
first_sentence: Lina entered the town hall carrying a canvas bag filled with meeting papers, a notebook, and two pens.

text: Tariq arrived at the town hall carrying a canvas bag with a notebook, two pens, and an agenda. By the entrance, he passed a table where residents placed reusable bags beside their chairs. He set his bag under a seat and opened the agenda as the council chair called the meeting to order. During a report on road repairs, Tariq took one pen from the bag and wrote several dates. A clerk carried a bag of printed maps along the aisle, handing copies to each row. Tariq received a map, folded it once, and slipped it into his bag. The council then reviewed trash collection, including a proposal for distributing compost bags at the library. Beside him, a resident lifted a shopping bag to make room for another stack of documents. Tariq moved his bag closer to his shoes while the council recorded comments about parking signs. After the vote, he returned his pen and agenda to the bag, carried the bag past the entrance table, and left the hall.
first_sentence: Tariq arrived at the town hall carrying a canvas bag with a notebook, two pens, and an agenda.

text: Yara packed a canvas bag with clothes, socks, and a folded towel before leaving for the camping weekend. A second bag held bread, apples, cheese, and two metal cups. At the campsite, she carried both bags from the car to a level patch beneath several pine trees. She set the food bag on a wooden table and opened the canvas bag beside the tent. From a small side bag, Yara removed stakes, cord, and a compact hammer. After raising the tent, she placed the clothes bag near the rear wall and tucked the tool bag by the entrance. Another camper passed with a sleeping bag rolled under one arm. Yara unrolled her own sleeping bag, then returned to the table and closed the food bag. Before dusk, she walked along a marked trail with a water bag and a cloth bag for collecting litter. Back at camp, she put the cloth bag beside a bin. In the morning, Yara repacked each bag, checked the ground, and carried the bags to the car.
first_sentence: Yara packed a canvas bag with clothes, socks, and a folded towel before leaving for the camping weekend.

text: Daniel packed a canvas bag with clothes, a cooking pot, and two towels before the camping weekend. He placed the bag beside a rolled sleeping bag in the back of his car. At the campground, Daniel carried the canvas bag to a level site near several pine trees. Another camper passed with a paper bag while Daniel set his own bag on a wooden table. He opened the bag, removed a shirt, and arranged the remaining items by size. The sleeping bag went inside the tent, with a small pillow bag tucked near its foot. For supper, Daniel took rice and vegetables from a grocery bag and cooked them over the camp stove. He folded the empty bag and stored it in the canvas bag for later use. After sunset, Daniel put a flashlight in a side pocket of the bag and read beside the tent. In the morning, he carried a wash bag to the campground sink. Before leaving, Daniel packed the sleeping bag, wash bag, and grocery bag into the car.
first_sentence: Daniel packed a canvas bag with clothes, a cooking pot, and two towels before the camping weekend.

text: Elena packed a canvas bag with clothes, a towel, and a flashlight before the camping weekend. She placed the bag beside a sleeping bag and carried both to the car. At the campground, she passed a ranger holding a paper bag of maps. Elena took her bag to a level campsite and set it near the picnic table. A food bag went into a storage box while the sleeping bag was unrolled inside the tent. She used a small bag to collect pinecones scattered around the fire ring. Later, Elena opened a cooking bag and removed a pot, a spoon, and dried pasta. “The water is ready,” someone said, passing her a bag of bread. After dinner, she sealed scraps in a trash bag and wiped the table. At dusk, she carried a wash bag to the campground sink. The next morning, Elena folded the sleeping bag and returned it to its sack. She packed each remaining bag, checked the campsite, and loaded the car.
first_sentence: Elena packed a canvas bag with clothes, a towel, and a flashlight before the camping weekend.

text: Patrick packed a canvas bag with clothes, then placed a smaller bag of food beside the tent poles in his car. At the campground, he carried each bag to a level plot near a stand of pines. He opened the tent bag, sorted the poles, and spread the folded fabric across the ground. After raising the tent, Patrick put his sleeping bag inside and used a spare bag to hold his shoes. A camper at the next plot passed by with a bag of firewood while Patrick unpacked his cooking bag. He set a pot on the stove, opened a bag of rice, and measured water from a bottle. “Dinner is nearly ready,” he said when another camper approached with a bag of vegetables. After eating, Patrick sealed the scraps in a bag and placed it in the campground bin. He spent the evening reading beside the tent, with the food bag stored in his car. In the morning, he rolled his sleeping bag, packed every bag, and drove home after breakfast.
first_sentence: Patrick packed a canvas bag with clothes, then placed a smaller bag of food beside the tent poles in his car.

text: Chloe arrived at the museum with a canvas bag over her shoulder. In the entrance hall, she placed the bag on a table while an attendant checked its contents. She carried the bag through the first gallery, passing visitors with tote bags, paper bags, and small leather bags. Beside a case of Roman coins, Chloe shifted the bag to her other shoulder and read the display label. An ancient travel bag stood behind glass, its cracked surface supported by a plain wooden frame. Chloe took a notebook from her bag and copied the date printed beside the travel bag. In the sculpture room, she set the bag on a bench while studying three marble figures. At noon, Chloe opened the bag in the museum café and removed a water bottle. Afterward, she put a guidebook into the bag and walked through an exhibit of painted household objects, including a blue bag on a chair. Before leaving, Chloe collected a brochure, folded it twice, and slipped it into the bag.
first_sentence: Chloe arrived at the museum with a canvas bag over her shoulder.

text: Kenji arrived at the museum with a canvas bag over one shoulder. At the entrance, he placed the bag in a tray while an attendant checked his ticket. He collected the bag and passed a rack holding several folded shopping bags from the museum store. In the first gallery, his bag rested against his hip as he read labels beside stone bowls. He opened the bag, took out a notebook, and copied the date of a carved panel. Nearby, a visitor carried a paper bag printed with columns and arches. Kenji returned the notebook to his bag before entering the textile room. A display case contained an embroidered travel bag, while a wall text explained how such bags held coins and tools. At noon, Kenji sat on a bench, removed a wrapped sandwich from the bag, and ate it under a sign permitting food in that area. He put the wrapper in a small waste bag, closed his canvas bag, and continued toward the ceramics gallery.
first_sentence: Kenji arrived at the museum with a canvas bag over one shoulder.

text: Mira entered the museum with a canvas bag tucked under her arm. At the ticket desk, she opened the bag, removed her wallet, and placed the ticket in a side pocket. A guard checked the bag and returned it to her. In the first gallery, glass cases displayed embroidered bags from several centuries. Mira read a label describing a silk bag used for coins. Beside it, a leather bag rested near a painted traveling coat. She adjusted her own bag before walking into the sculpture hall. A visitor carried a paper bag from the museum shop, while another set a small bag beneath a bench. Mira passed both bags and stopped beside a marble figure holding a carved bag. In the textile room, she took a notebook from her bag and copied the date of a woven bag. At noon, Mira carried her bag to the café and removed a wrapped sandwich. After eating, she put the wrapper in the bag and continued upstairs. Before leaving, she bought a postcard, slipped it into the bag, and collected her coat.
first_sentence: Mira entered the museum with a canvas bag tucked under her arm.

text: Andrei arrived at the city museum with a canvas bag hanging from his shoulder. At the entrance, he opened the bag for inspection, and an attendant placed a small paper tag on its handle. He carried the bag through a gallery of stone tools, keeping it close to his side as he read each label. In the next room, glass cases displayed old coins, seals, and a leather travel bag from the nineteenth century. Andrei compared that cracked bag with his plain canvas bag, then wrote the exhibit number in a notebook. Near a bench, he set the bag between his shoes while examining a large map on the wall. He later lifted the bag and passed several visitors whose shopping bags rustled beside their coats. In the sculpture hall, a guide pointed toward a carved figure carrying a grain bag across its back. Before leaving, Andrei bought a postcard, slipped it into the bag, and returned the tagged bag to his shoulder.
first_sentence: Andrei arrived at the city museum with a canvas bag hanging from his shoulder.

text: Ilse carried a canvas bag from her arrival gate to the concourse, where departure screens listed her connecting flight. She set the bag beside her chair and removed a book, a bottle, and a paper bag containing a sandwich. Around her, travelers rolled black bags across the tiles, while an attendant stacked tagged bags on a cart. Ilse ate the sandwich and folded the empty paper bag into the side pocket of her canvas bag. Then she read several pages, with one hand resting on the bag strap. At a nearby shop, she bought tea and accepted a small bag of biscuits for the next flight. She returned to the chair, placed the biscuit bag inside her larger bag, and checked the screen again. When the gate number appeared, Ilse closed her book and packed it in the bag. She passed a family arranging several bags near a charging station and followed the signs. At the gate, she placed her bag beneath a seat, presented her boarding pass, and waited.
first_sentence: Ilse carried a canvas bag from her arrival gate to the concourse, where departure screens listed her connecting flight.

text: Wei had a three-hour layover and carried a black bag from the arrival gate to the central concourse. He set the bag beside a metal chair and checked the departure board. Around him, travelers rolled bags past shops, charging stations, and rows of windows. Wei opened his bag, removed a folded itinerary, and compared the gate number with the screen. At a kiosk, he bought water and a sandwich, then placed both in the bag. He carried the bag to an observation window, where service carts moved between aircraft. Later, he passed a luggage store displaying canvas bags, leather bags, and small travel bags. He returned to the concourse and rested the bag across his shoes while reading a newspaper. An announcement changed his departure gate, so Wei closed the bag and followed the signs. He rode a moving walkway with the bag at his side. At the new gate, he placed the bag under a seat, discarded the sandwich wrapper, and waited until boarding began.
first_sentence: Wei had a three-hour layover and carried a black bag from the arrival gate to the central concourse.

text: During her three-hour layover, Sofia carried a canvas bag from the arrival gate to the central concourse. She placed the bag beside her chair and checked the next flight on a screen. Around her, travelers rolled large bags, lifted small bags, and set shopping bags beneath tables. Sofia opened her bag, removed a book, and tucked the boarding pass into an inside pocket. At noon, she closed the bag and walked past a luggage shop displaying leather bags and travel bags. She bought a sandwich, which the cashier put in a paper bag with a bottle of water. Back at the gate, Sofia slid the paper bag into the canvas bag and watched ground crews move baggage carts outside. When boarding began, she lifted the bag onto her shoulder and joined the line. An attendant tagged the bag, then Sofia carried the bag through the jet bridge. She stored the bag above her seat and sat down for the second flight.
first_sentence: During her three-hour layover, Sofia carried a canvas bag from the arrival gate to the central concourse.

text: Mateo’s layover lasted three hours, so he carried his bag from the arrival gate toward the central concourse. His small black bag held a book, a charger, a folded shirt, and a paper receipt. Near a row of windows, he placed the bag beside a chair and checked the departure screen. Around him, travelers rolled bags across the tiled floor or set bags beneath their seats. Mateo opened his bag, removed the charger, and connected his phone to an outlet under the chair. A cleaner passed with a supply bag hanging from the side of a cart. After twenty minutes, Mateo unplugged the charger, returned it to the bag, and walked to a café. He ordered tea and a sandwich, carrying the paper bag back to his seat. The empty paper bag later went into a recycling bin, while his travel bag remained under his hand. When boarding began, Mateo lifted the bag, joined the line, and showed his pass. At the aircraft door, he adjusted the bag’s strap and stepped inside.
first_sentence: Mateo’s layover lasted three hours, so he carried his bag from the arrival gate toward the central concourse.

text: At sunrise, Nadia carried a canvas bag from the farmhouse to the lower field. Beside the barn, empty bags hung from wooden pegs, ready for the harvest. She opened one bag between the rows while two workers cut squash from the vines. Each squash went into the bag with a layer of dry straw around it. When the bag was full, Nadia tied its cord and placed it on a wagon. She then took a smaller bag to the bean patch, where loose pods covered the plants. The workers filled baskets, and Nadia poured each basket into the waiting bag. Near midday, she passed bags of onions stacked under a roof beside the sorting table. “This bag is for seed,” a worker said, setting it apart. Nadia marked the bag with chalk and carried another bag toward the orchard. Apples filled that bag, while bruised fruit went into a bin for pressing. By evening, rows of labeled bags stood in the barn, and Nadia counted them before closing the doors.
first_sentence: At sunrise, Nadia carried a canvas bag from the farmhouse to the lower field.

text: At sunrise, Javier carried a canvas bag from the barn to the first row of potatoes. He opened the bag beside the furrows and placed each dusty potato inside. When the bag reached the marked line, he tied it and set it near the wagon. A worker handed him another bag, and Javier moved to the next row. By midmorning, filled bags stood at regular intervals across the field. Javier lifted each bag onto the wagon, then counted the bags on a clipboard. Near the orchard, he passed empty apple bags to two pickers on ladders. Each picker lowered a bag of apples, and Javier transferred the fruit into larger storage bags. At noon, he took bread from a paper bag and sat beside stacked grain bags. Afterward, he returned the lunch bag to his coat pocket. The afternoon harvest produced more potato bags, apple bags, and several bags of onions. Before dusk, Javier swept loose soil from the wagon, folded the unused bags, and placed every folded bag on a barn shelf.
first_sentence: At sunrise, Javier carried a canvas bag from the barn to the first row of potatoes.

text: At dawn, Nora carried a canvas bag from the farmhouse to the lower field, where rows of potatoes waited beneath dry soil. She set the bag beside a basket and filled it with potatoes lifted by the farm crew. When the bag reached the marked line, she tied its cord and placed it on the wagon. An empty bag came next, followed by another bag as morning light crossed the field. Near the barn, Nora passed stacks of grain bags and checked the label on each bag. She carried a seed bag to the shed, then returned with a bag of twine. At midday, she opened a lunch bag containing bread, cheese, and an apple. After eating, she folded the bag and tucked it under the wagon seat. The crew spent the afternoon gathering onions into mesh bags and corn into larger bags. Nora counted each bag on a clipboard before loading it. By sunset, every filled bag stood in rows inside the barn, and Nora hung the last empty bag on a wooden peg.
first_sentence: At dawn, Nora carried a canvas bag from the farmhouse to the lower field, where rows of potatoes waited beneath dry soil.

text: At sunrise, Oskar carried a stack of empty bags from the barn to the field. Each canvas bag had a wide mouth and a faded number marked near the seam. He opened the first bag beside a row of potatoes and held it while two workers filled it. When the bag reached the wooden measure, Oskar tied its cord and placed it on a cart. He passed several grain bags near the thresher, where chaff settled across their folded tops. By midday, the cart held thirty bags of potatoes, and another cart held bags of onions. Oskar took a cloth bag from his pocket and used it to collect seed heads for next spring. After the meal break, he checked each bag for loose knots and retied three cords. A worker handed him a paper bag containing labels, and Oskar attached one label to every filled bag. Before dusk, he moved the remaining empty bags into the barn and stacked them beside the scale. The final bag stood under the scale while Oskar entered its weight in the harvest ledger.
first_sentence: At sunrise, Oskar carried a stack of empty bags from the barn to the field.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: On Tuesday morning, Beatriz set a canvas bag beside the apartment door before checking the mail slot. A white envelope lay on the floor, partly covered by the bag’s strap. Beatriz picked up the letter, placed it in the bag, and carried the bag to the kitchen table. Beside a paper grocery bag, she opened the envelope with a small knife. The letter confirmed the date of a routine appointment and listed several documents to bring. Beatriz removed a zippered bag from a drawer and put her identification card and printed forms inside it. She then placed that bag in the canvas bag with the letter. After lunch, she folded the empty grocery bag and stored it with several other bags beneath the sink. The canvas bag remained on a chair while she washed a cup and wiped the table. Before leaving for an errand, Beatriz checked the letter once more, returned it to the bag, and carried the bag downstairs.
first_sentence: On Tuesday morning, Beatriz set a canvas bag beside the apartment door before checking the mail slot.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Bruno placed a canvas bag beside the kitchen chair before checking the mail slot. A white envelope lay on the floor near the bag, printed with his name and address. He picked up the letter and carried it with the bag to the table. From the bag, Bruno removed a notebook, a pen, and a small paper bag containing an apple. He opened the envelope above the canvas bag so that scraps of paper would fall inside it. The letter announced a routine change to the neighborhood bus schedule. Bruno copied the new times into the notebook, then returned the pen and notebook to the bag. He folded the letter once and slipped it into a side pocket of the bag. After eating the apple, he put its core in the paper bag and set that bag near the door. Bruno lifted the canvas bag, checked the side pocket, and walked to the bus stop. Another passenger stood there with a shopping bag. Bruno placed his bag on the bench and consulted the letter when the bus arrived.
first_sentence: Bruno placed a canvas bag beside the kitchen chair before checking the mail slot.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Priya set her grocery bag beside the kitchen table when the mail slot clicked. Among the envelopes on the mat lay a padded mailing bag addressed to her in plain blue ink. She carried the bag to the table and placed it beside the grocery bag. After putting rice and apples from the grocery bag into cupboards, she opened the mailing bag with scissors. Inside the bag was a folded letter and a small cotton bag tied with string. Priya read the letter, which explained that the cotton bag contained fabric samples for new curtains. She spread the samples near the empty grocery bag and compared them with the cloth already hanging at the window. Then she returned the samples to their bag and wrote the requested measurements at the bottom of the letter. Priya placed the letter and cotton bag inside the mailing bag, sealed it with tape, and set it by her work bag for posting the next morning.
first_sentence: Priya set her grocery bag beside the kitchen table when the mail slot clicked.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Hiroshi set a canvas bag on the kitchen table and removed two apples from it. Through the window, he saw a postal worker pass the gate with a gray mail bag. A few minutes later, Hiroshi opened the door and found an envelope resting beside his grocery bag on the step. He carried the letter inside, placed it near the canvas bag, and washed his hands. The envelope contained a notice from the municipal archive confirming that the street map he had requested was ready for collection. Hiroshi folded the notice and slipped it into a small document bag with a zipper. He then packed a notebook, a pencil, and his transit card into the same bag. Before leaving, he moved the empty grocery bag to a hook and put the canvas bag in a cupboard. At the bus stop, the document bag rested under his arm while a passenger arranged vegetables in a paper bag. Hiroshi checked the hours on the letter, returned it to the bag, and boarded the bus.
first_sentence: Hiroshi set a canvas bag on the kitchen table and removed two apples from it.

text: Yuki carried a canvas bag next door to look after her neighbor’s dog for the afternoon. Inside the bag were a water bottle, a book, and a small paper bag for used tissues. The neighbor had left a bag of dog food beside the kitchen cupboard, with feeding instructions taped to the bag. Yuki measured one cup from the bag and poured it into the dog’s bowl. She clipped a roll of waste bags to the leash, then put the leash and another bag in her coat pocket. During the walk, the dog sniffed a shopping bag near a bench before moving along the path. Yuki used one waste bag, tied the bag, and placed it in a public bin. Back at the house, she took a brush from a green bag and brushed the dog on a mat. When the neighbor returned, Yuki handed over the leash, folded her canvas bag, and said, “Everything followed the schedule.”
first_sentence: Yuki carried a canvas bag next door to look after her neighbor’s dog for the afternoon.

text: Ravi carried a canvas bag to the apartment next door, where the neighbor’s dog waited beside a paper bag of supplies. The bag held a leash, treats, a folding bowl, and several small waste bags. Ravi placed his canvas bag on a chair and took the leash from the supply bag. Before leaving, he filled a water bottle and slipped it into the side pocket of his bag. The dog walked beside Ravi while the bag hung from his shoulder. At the corner, Ravi used one of the waste bags, tied the bag, and placed it in a public bin. They passed a grocery shop where stacked bags stood near the counter. In the park, Ravi opened his bag, unfolded the bowl, and poured water into it. After the dog drank, he dried the bowl and returned it to the bag. Back at the apartment, Ravi measured food from a sealed bag into a dish. He packed the leash and remaining bags into the supply bag, collected his canvas bag, and left the dog resting near the chair.
first_sentence: Ravi carried a canvas bag to the apartment next door, where the neighbor’s dog waited beside a paper bag of supplies.

text: Lucia collected the neighbor’s key from a paper bag beside the doormat. Inside the apartment, the dog waited near a canvas bag containing its leash and brush. Lucia took the leash from the bag and clipped it to the dog’s collar. She placed two small waste bags in her coat pocket and carried a water bag with a folding bowl. During the walk, the dog paused beside a grocery bag held by a passerby. Lucia guided it around the bag and continued toward the small park. At the gate, she used one waste bag, tied it, and placed it in a bin. She poured water from the water bag into the bowl, then packed the bowl back into her tote bag. On the return route, they passed bags of soil outside a garden shop. Back inside, Lucia measured food from a sealed bag into the dog’s dish. She brushed the dog and returned the brush to the canvas bag. Before leaving, Lucia put the key into the paper bag by the door.
first_sentence: Lucia collected the neighbor’s key from a paper bag beside the doormat.

text: Henrik took the neighbor’s canvas bag from the hallway hook and checked the note inside it. The dog waited beside a paper bag containing biscuits, a leash, and a folded towel. Henrik placed the biscuit bag in his coat pocket and clipped the leash to the collar. Outside, he carried a small waste bag while the dog walked along the pavement. They passed a cyclist with a grocery bag and a doorway stacked with delivery bags. At the park, Henrik opened the biscuit bag, gave the dog one biscuit, and closed the bag again. The dog inspected a bench where a canvas bag rested beside its owner. Henrik used the waste bag near a row of bins, then selected another bag from the dispenser. On the return walk, he stopped at a shop and carried home a bag of bread. Back in the neighbor’s kitchen, Henrik put the bread bag on the counter and returned the biscuit bag to its shelf. He folded the canvas bag, hung it by the door, and filled the dog’s bowl.
first_sentence: Henrik took the neighbor’s canvas bag from the hallway hook and checked the note inside it.

text: Clara arrived at the laboratory carrying a canvas bag with her notebook, pens, and sealed sample tubes. She placed the bag beside the bench and removed a smaller plastic bag containing clean pipette tips. From another bag, she took three labeled flasks and arranged them beneath the task lamp. Clara checked the protocol, then folded the empty bag and set it near the sink. A technician passed her a clear bag of sterile swabs, which she opened along its marked edge. She used each swab to collect residue from the flasks, placing the used swabs into separate specimen bags. After adding measured drops of reagent, Clara sealed every bag and recorded the time in her notebook. She carried the specimen bags to an incubator, where a rack held bags from earlier trials. During the waiting period, she wiped the bench and returned unused supplies to the canvas bag. When the timer sounded, Clara retrieved the bags, noted the color readings, and packed the completed samples into a storage bag.
first_sentence: Clara arrived at the laboratory carrying a canvas bag with her notebook, pens, and sealed sample tubes.

text: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag with his notebook, gloves, and timer inside. He placed the bag beneath a clean bench and removed a sealed plastic bag of sample tubes. Beside the balance, another bag held disposable pipette tips arranged in small boxes. Kofi opened that bag, fitted a tip to the pipette, and measured liquid into six labeled tubes. He returned each used tip to a waste bag beside the bench. After recording the volumes, he took a bag of powdered reagent from a cabinet. The reagent bag remained on a tray while he weighed equal portions into glass dishes. Kofi then sealed the bag, mixed each portion with water, and started the timer from his canvas bag. During the waiting period, he passed a rack where paper bags covered several stored containers. When the timer sounded, Kofi measured the samples, entered the results, and packed the tubes into a padded bag. He wiped the bench, closed every bag, and carried his canvas bag from the laboratory.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag with his notebook, gloves, and timer inside.

text: Helen entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag of labeled tubes and placed the bag beside the balance. She removed a notebook from the bag, then set three clear plastic bags in a row on the bench. Each bag held a measured portion of soil for an experiment on moisture retention. Helen opened the first bag, added ten milliliters of water, and sealed the bag again. She repeated the procedure with the second bag, using twenty milliliters, while the third bag received none. After weighing each bag, she recorded the mass and moved the bags beneath a lamp. A paper bag containing spare labels stood near the lamp, and Helen took one label from the bag for each sample. At thirty-minute intervals, she carried each plastic bag to the balance and entered the new mass. Another laboratory worker passed with a lunch bag while Helen returned the sample bags to the bench. After the final measurement, Helen placed the notebook and unused labels in her canvas bag. She left the three sample bags beneath the lamp for the next scheduled reading.
first_sentence: Helen entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag of labeled tubes and placed the bag beside the balance.

text: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag containing his notebook, gloves, and timer. He placed the bag beside the balance and removed a sealed plastic bag of mineral samples. From another bag, he took six labeled tubes and arranged them in a rack. Kwame weighed each sample, returned the remainder to its bag, and recorded the measurements. A paper bag near the sink held clean pipette tips, which he transferred to the workbench. He added measured water to each tube, capped it, and set the tubes inside a clear bag to keep the rack dry during mixing. While the shaker ran, Kwame passed a cabinet where spare bags were stacked by size. He opened a small bag of indicator strips and tested each mixture at regular intervals. After noting the color readings, he poured the mixtures into labeled disposal containers and put the empty tubes in a collection bag. Kwame wiped the bench, packed his notebook into the canvas bag, and left the laboratory.
first_sentence: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying a canvas bag containing his notebook, gloves, and timer.

text: Ingrid left her building at seven, carrying a canvas bag with her lunch, notebook, and folded umbrella. At the corner, she adjusted the bag’s strap and joined commuters beside the timetable. A passenger set a grocery bag near the bench while the bus approached through traffic. Ingrid boarded, tapped her card, and held the bag against her coat as she moved down the aisle. Two shopping bags occupied the floor beneath a seat, so she passed them and chose a place by the window. She rested her bag on her knees, opened the outer pocket, and removed a transit schedule. Across the aisle, a student placed a backpack beside a paper bag containing a pastry. At each stop, coats and bags shifted as passengers entered or departed. Ingrid returned the schedule to her bag, then checked that the lunch container remained upright. Near the office district, she lifted the bag from her knees and stepped toward the door. The bus paused, and Ingrid carried her bag onto the pavement.
first_sentence: Ingrid left her building at seven, carrying a canvas bag with her lunch, notebook, and folded umbrella.

text: Viktor left his building with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper lunch bag tucked inside it. At the bus stop, he set the canvas bag beside his shoes while another passenger adjusted two shopping bags. When the bus arrived, Viktor lifted his bag and followed a row of commuters carrying laptop bags, tote bags, and grocery bags. He tapped his fare card, moved down the aisle, and placed his bag on his knees. Across from him, a worker held a tool bag, while a student kept a book bag between both feet. At the next stop, several riders boarded with bags, and Viktor shifted his bag closer to make room. The bus passed a bakery where paper bags stood in rows behind the window. Viktor opened his lunch bag, checked the container inside, and folded the bag closed again. Near the central station, a recorded voice announced the stop, and passengers gathered their bags from seats and floor racks. Viktor stepped onto the pavement with his canvas bag, passed a luggage shop displaying travel bags, and continued toward his office.
first_sentence: Viktor left his building with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a paper lunch bag tucked inside it.

text: Greta left her building at seven with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a lunch bag in her hand. At the corner, she adjusted the canvas bag while waiting beside two commuters carrying paper bags. The bus arrived, and Greta passed a passenger whose shopping bag rested near the door. She tapped her fare card, moved down the aisle, and placed both bags on her lap. Across from her, a rider held a gym bag between polished shoes, while another tucked a grocery bag beneath a seat. Greta opened her lunch bag, checked the sealed container inside, and closed the bag again. At the next stop, several passengers boarded with backpacks and cloth bags, filling the aisle with straps and handles. “Is this seat open?” a passenger asked, pointing beside Greta’s bags. “Yes,” Greta said, lifting the canvas bag onto the lunch bag to make space. When the bus reached downtown, she gathered each bag, stepped onto the pavement, and walked past a shop window displaying rows of leather bags.
first_sentence: Greta left her building at seven with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a lunch bag in her hand.

text: Ibrahim left his apartment with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a lunch bag in his hand. At the corner, he adjusted the bag strap while the morning bus approached. Several passengers waited beside shopping bags, laptop bags, and one folded paper bag. Ibrahim boarded, tapped his card, and placed the lunch bag inside the larger bag. He moved down the aisle, passing a cloth bag tucked beneath a seat. Near the middle, he sat with his bag resting upright between his shoes. Across the aisle, a passenger opened a bag and removed a newspaper. The bus stopped often, and more bags entered with office workers, students, and shoppers. Ibrahim checked the side pocket of his bag for his transit pass, then closed the zipper. Sunlight crossed the bag as the bus turned onto the main road. At his stop, he lifted the bag, stepped past two grocery bags, and left through the rear door. He carried the bag toward his building while the bus continued along its route.
first_sentence: Ibrahim left his apartment with a canvas bag over one shoulder and a lunch bag in his hand.

text: Teresa prepared the house for sale by stacking a bag of cleaning cloths beside the kitchen sink. She carried another bag upstairs and placed spare towels in the bathroom cupboard. In each bedroom, she filled a bag with small items that would not appear in the listing photographs. A paper bag held spare keys, instruction manuals, and receipts for recent repairs. Before the agent arrived, Teresa passed the bags in the hallway and moved them into the garage. The agent set a leather bag on the counter and reviewed the property forms with her. Teresa took a pen from the bag and signed beside the marked tabs. During the viewing, she waited outside with a canvas bag containing her phone, water bottle, and notebook. The visitors entered carrying a shopping bag and left after measuring several rooms. Later, the agent returned the signed papers in a clear document bag. Teresa placed that bag in a desk drawer and packed dishes into padded bags. A week afterward, an offer arrived, and she used a reusable bag to carry the remaining papers to the agent’s office.
first_sentence: Teresa prepared the house for sale by stacking a bag of cleaning cloths beside the kitchen sink.

text: Jonas carried a bag of cleaning cloths through the house before the morning viewing. He set the bag beside the kitchen door and wiped the counters. In the hall, he filled another bag with shoes, umbrellas, and spare keys. A paper bag held brochures listing the rooms, heating system, and asking price. Jonas placed that bag on a table near the entrance. When the agent arrived, Jonas handed over a small bag containing labeled copies of the front-door key. Two visitors entered, each carrying a shopping bag, and walked through the rooms while the agent spoke. Jonas waited in the garden and gathered fallen leaves into a large bag. After the visitors left, the agent brought the brochure bag outside and reported that they would submit an offer. Jonas returned the leaf bag to the shed and checked the written amount. Later, he packed cups into a padded bag for the planned move. He signed the sale papers at the kitchen table, with the key bag resting beside his pen.
first_sentence: Jonas carried a bag of cleaning cloths through the house before the morning viewing.

text: Anjali placed a canvas bag on the kitchen counter before the estate agent arrived. She carried another bag through each room, checking that the shelves and cupboards were empty. In the hall, a paper bag held spare keys, property forms, and a tape measure. The photographer moved a lighting bag beside the stairs while Anjali opened the curtains. During the viewing, Anjali offered each visitor a bag containing disposable shoe covers. She then set the used covers in a separate bag near the door. One visitor inspected the pantry, where reusable shopping bags hung from a hook. Another measured the garage while Anjali shifted a garden bag away from the wall. At the dining table, the agent removed documents from a leather bag and marked several entries. Anjali placed the signed contract in a clear bag with the house records. After the visitors departed, she packed mugs, cloths, and a kettle into a large bag. She carried the final bag to her car, returned the keys, and closed the front door.
first_sentence: Anjali placed a canvas bag on the kitchen counter before the estate agent arrived.

text: Tomas placed a canvas bag beside the front door before the estate agent arrived. The bag held spare keys, a tape measure, and copies of the house brochure. In the kitchen, he moved a paper bag of cleaning cloths from the counter to a cupboard. Another bag stood in the hallway, filled with shoes that would be taken to his new address. During the viewing, Tomas carried the key bag from room to room and opened each locked window. A visitor set a shopping bag near the stairs while examining the storage space. Tomas passed the bag and pointed toward a closet under the landing. Outside, he used a small bag to collect pegs left near the washing line. After the visitors departed, the agent returned the brochure bag and discussed an offer. “The paperwork can begin tomorrow,” the agent said. Tomas put the signed form into a document bag, checked each room, and carried three packed bags to his car. The remaining bags would be collected after the sale was completed.
first_sentence: Tomas placed a canvas bag beside the front door before the estate agent arrived.

text: Amara arrived at the office carrying a plain canvas bag with her résumé inside. Near reception, she passed a rack holding several visitor bags and placed her bag beside her chair. A receptionist gave her a plastic badge and pointed to a small bag containing a pen and company brochure. Amara put the badge on, opened the bag, and read the brochure while she waited. When the interviewer appeared, Amara picked up her canvas bag and followed through a corridor lined with framed photographs of shopping bags. In the meeting room, she set the bag beside the table and removed a folder from it. “Please describe your previous work,” the interviewer said, placing a leather bag under another chair. Amara answered each question, occasionally taking a document from her bag or returning one to it. The interviewer explained that the position involved tracking orders for reusable bags sold by the company. Afterward, Amara closed her folder, returned it to the canvas bag, and carried the bag back through reception.
first_sentence: Amara arrived at the office carrying a plain canvas bag with her résumé inside.

text: Samuel entered the office carrying a black bag with his résumé inside. Near the reception desk, a row of canvas bags hung from wooden hooks. He placed his bag beside his chair and completed a visitor form. When an interviewer arrived, Samuel lifted the bag and followed through a corridor. In the meeting room, he set the bag under the table beside another bag. The interviewer asked about his previous work, and Samuel removed a folder from his bag. “I managed weekly reports and client records,” he said. He returned the folder to the bag while the interviewer described the position. A paper bag containing pens stood near a stack of application forms. Samuel took one pen from the bag and wrote down the proposed schedule. After several questions, the interviewer handed him a small bag containing company brochures. Samuel placed the brochure bag inside his own bag and stood. At reception, he collected his bag, signed out, and passed the hanging bags again. He then carried the bag to the bus stop and waited.
first_sentence: Samuel entered the office carrying a black bag with his résumé inside.

text: Hannah arrived for the job interview carrying a black canvas bag beside her coat. At reception, she placed the bag on a low table and signed the visitor sheet. A receptionist gave her a paper badge, which she stored in the front pocket of the bag. While waiting, Hannah noticed three bags beneath nearby chairs and a delivery bag beside the desk. An interviewer entered, and Hannah lifted her bag before following through a glass door. In the meeting room, she set the bag beside her chair and removed a folder from it. The interviewer asked about her previous work, and Hannah answered while resting one hand on the bag. She opened the bag again to take out a printed sample, then passed the sample across the table. After several routine questions, the interviewer described the position and pointed to a company bag used for carrying documents. Hannah returned the folder to her bag, thanked the interviewer, and stood. At reception, she collected a brochure, slipped it into the bag, and left the building.
first_sentence: Hannah arrived for the job interview carrying a black canvas bag beside her coat.

text: Pavel arrived for the job interview carrying a plain black bag over one shoulder. At reception, he placed the bag beside his chair and completed a visitor form. Another applicant had set a canvas bag near the coat rack. When his appointment began, Pavel lifted his bag and followed an employee down the corridor. The meeting room contained a table, three chairs, and a shelf holding several conference bags. Pavel put his bag under the chair and took a folder from its front pocket. The interviewer reviewed his résumé while Pavel kept one hand on the bag strap. “Please describe your previous work,” the interviewer said. Pavel answered with dates, duties, and examples, then returned a document to the bag. A second employee entered with a laptop bag and sat across from him. Pavel discussed schedules and software while the laptop bag remained by the employee’s feet. After several questions, he zipped his bag and stood. At reception, he collected a printed information sheet and slipped it into the bag. Pavel then carried the bag through the lobby and left the building.
first_sentence: Pavel arrived for the job interview carrying a plain black bag over one shoulder.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: Fatima carried a canvas bag from the corner shop when the neighborhood lights went out. She paused beside a gate, shifted the bag to her other hand, and watched the windows turn dark. A neighbor placed a grocery bag on the pavement while checking the street. Fatima opened her bag and took out a small flashlight she used for reading labels. With the bag hanging from her wrist, she walked toward her building at an even pace. In the lobby, several residents stood near paper bags holding bread, vegetables, and household supplies. Fatima set her bag on a bench and pointed the flashlight toward the stairs. Someone lifted two shopping bags, and the group went up together. Inside her apartment, Fatima unpacked the bag and arranged tins, rice, and soap on the counter. She folded the empty bag, placed it beside another bag in a cupboard, and lit a candle. When the power returned, she put the candle away and prepared tea.
first_sentence: Fatima carried a canvas bag from the corner shop when the neighborhood lights went out.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Malik was carrying a paper bag of groceries from the corner store. He set the bag on his kitchen table and took a flashlight from a canvas bag beside the door. Outside, several neighbors stood near their gates with shopping bags, trash bags, or small tool bags in hand. Malik placed two battery lanterns in a reusable bag and walked along the darkened sidewalk. At one house, he passed a bag containing candles to an older resident, then continued toward the community room. A folding table there held bags of spare batteries, bottled water, and packaged crackers for anyone who needed them. Malik opened his bag, arranged the lanterns on the table, and returned the empty bag to his shoulder. Without streetlights, people moved slowly between houses, their bags rustling as they walked. After an hour, porch lights returned one by one, and Malik packed a lantern into his bag. He carried the bag home, unpacked the groceries, and folded the paper bag beside the refrigerator.
first_sentence: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Malik was carrying a paper bag of groceries from the corner store.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Agnes was unpacking a paper bag of groceries in her kitchen. She placed the bag beside two cloth bags and checked the dark ceiling light. From a drawer, she took a small bag containing candles and set one candle in a holder. Agnes carried another bag to the porch, where several neighbors stood with flashlights. A neighbor passed her a bag of spare batteries, and Agnes selected two before returning the bag. Along the sidewalk, people moved grocery bags, garden bags, and laundry bags indoors while porch lights remained off. Agnes walked to the corner shop with a reusable bag, though the locked register meant that no purchases were being processed. She passed a bag of potting soil outside the shop and watched a worker cover it with a sheet. Back home, Agnes folded the empty grocery bag, put it with the other bags, and waited by the window. When the electricity returned, she stored the candle bag in the drawer and continued unpacking the remaining bag.
first_sentence: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Agnes was unpacking a paper bag of groceries in her kitchen.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Dmitri was unpacking a paper bag of groceries in his kitchen. He placed the bag on the counter and looked through the dark window. Along the sidewalk, several neighbors carried shopping bags from their cars. Dmitri found a canvas bag in a drawer and put a flashlight, a bottle of water, and a book inside it. With the bag over one shoulder, he walked to the apartment lobby. A neighbor set a bag of candles on a table, while another sorted batteries into a plastic bag. Dmitri passed the canvas bag to an older resident, who removed the flashlight and returned the bag. Outside, the streetlights remained off, and loose bags near a recycling bin shifted in the evening air. Dmitri picked up each bag and placed it inside the bin. He then carried his canvas bag upstairs. By the time he put the bag beside the door, the lights came on, and he resumed unpacking the grocery bag.
first_sentence: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Dmitri was unpacking a paper bag of groceries in his kitchen.

text: Mei arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves, labels, and string. Beside the gate, a row of paper bags held seed packets for the morning’s planting. She set her bag near the tool shed and took out a pair of gloves. A gardener passed her a bag of compost, which she carried to an empty bed. Mei opened the bag, spread the compost with a trowel, and folded the empty bag flat. She then collected a small bag of bean seeds from the shared table. Each seed went into a shallow hole, while the bag rested beside her knee. At the next plot, Mei filled a bag with dry leaves for the compost bin. Someone asked, “Could you bring this bag too?” Mei carried both bags along the gravel path and emptied them into the wooden bin. Before leaving, she placed her gloves and unused labels back in the canvas bag. At the gate, Mei passed stacked bags of soil, checked the watering schedule, and walked home with the bag over her shoulder.
first_sentence: Mei arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves, labels, and string.

text: Omar arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves and hand tools. Beside the gate, bags of compost stood under a wooden shelter. He placed his bag near the shared table and took out a trowel. A volunteer passed him a paper bag containing seed packets labeled with dates. Omar opened one bag and planted radish seeds along a measured row. He then lifted a compost bag, poured part of it into a wheelbarrow, and folded the empty section flat. Near the herb beds, reusable bags held trimmed stems for the weekly collection. Omar carried one bag to the sorting area and set it beside several similar bags. During a break, he removed a water bottle and bread from his lunch bag. Afterward, he filled a small bag with dry leaves for mulch. Two visitors walked past with bags of tomatoes and beans. Before leaving, Omar returned the tools to his canvas bag, tied the leaf bag, and recorded both bags on the garden log.
first_sentence: Omar arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves and hand tools.

text: Zainab arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of seed packets, gloves, and string. Beside the gate, a paper bag held labels for the shared herb beds. She placed her bag on a bench and took out a notebook to check the planting list. A volunteer passed her a bag of bean seeds, which she divided among three marked rows. Zainab then filled a large bag with dry leaves collected from the paths. Near the compost bin, several bags of soil stood beside a wheelbarrow. She opened one soil bag and spread its contents around the tomato plants. Another gardener brought a bag containing small pots, and Zainab arranged the pots along the greenhouse shelf. At midday, she removed a sandwich from her lunch bag and sat near the fence. Afterward, the empty paper bag went into the compost container. Before leaving, Zainab returned the unused seed bag to the storage shed and folded her canvas bag under one arm.
first_sentence: Zainab arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of seed packets, gloves, and string.

text: Emeka arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves, string, and seed packets. Beside the gate, a row of compost bags stood under a wooden shelter. He set his bag on a bench and took out a pair of gloves. A gardener passed him a paper bag containing onion sets, and Emeka placed it beside his canvas bag. Along the central path, he carried a bag of mulch to the shared tomato bed. He opened the bag, spread the mulch around each plant, and folded the empty bag into a square. Near the herb plot, several bags held dry leaves for the compost bins. Emeka lifted one bag, emptied it into a bin, and returned the bag to the shelter. “These bags go by the shed,” someone said. He moved two soil bags there, then collected his folded bags. Before leaving, Emeka packed his gloves and remaining seeds into the canvas bag and recorded the work in the garden log.
first_sentence: Emeka arrived at the community garden carrying a canvas bag of gloves, string, and seed packets.

text: Martha arrived at the cooking class carrying a canvas bag with an apron, a notebook, and two containers. She placed the bag beneath her workstation and accepted a paper bag of vegetables from the instructor. On the counter, each participant had a bag containing onions, carrots, potatoes, and herbs. Martha opened her bag, removed the vegetables, and arranged them beside the cutting board. The instructor passed around a small bag of measuring spoons while explaining the soup recipe. Martha selected one spoon from the bag and measured salt into a bowl. She put vegetable peelings into a compost bag tied to the side of the table. During simmering, she returned the unused herbs to their bag and labeled the bag with the date. A second bag held bread, which she sliced and placed in a basket. At the end, Martha poured one portion of soup into a container and slipped it into her canvas bag. She folded her apron, added it to the bag, and left the classroom.
first_sentence: Martha arrived at the cooking class carrying a canvas bag with an apron, a notebook, and two containers.

text: Arjun arrived at the cooking class with a canvas bag holding an apron, a notebook, and two containers. He placed the bag beneath his station and took a recipe sheet from a side pocket. On the counter, each student received a paper bag of potatoes and a small bag of herbs. Arjun opened the potato bag, washed three potatoes, and set the empty bag beside the sink. The instructor demonstrated chopping while Arjun stored peelings in a compost bag. Next, he measured flour from a labeled bag and mixed it with chopped herbs. A piping bag lay near the bowls, so Arjun filled the bag with potato mixture. “Fold the bag at the top,” the instructor said. Arjun folded the piping bag, pressed portions onto a tray, and returned the flour bag to the supply table. During baking, he wiped his station and packed the used apron into his canvas bag. He slipped the recipe into the bag, placed the herb bag in a storage box, and carried his bag through the classroom doorway.
first_sentence: Arjun arrived at the cooking class with a canvas bag holding an apron, a notebook, and two containers.

text: Sana arrived at the cooking class carrying a canvas bag with an apron, a notebook, and two containers. She placed the bag beneath her worktable and took a paper bag of onions from the supply shelf. Beside it, a clear bag held carrots, while another bag contained measured potatoes. Sana opened each bag, arranged the vegetables on a board, and returned the empty bags to one side. The instructor passed around a bag of dried herbs, and Sana spooned some thyme into a pot. A small cloth bag held wooden utensils, so she selected a spoon and stirred the simmering soup. During the next step, Sana poured flour from a labeled bag into a bowl and added water for flatbread dough. She stored leftover flour in the bag, folded the top, and placed it beside her canvas bag. At the end, she packed the flatbread into a clean bag and poured the soup into her containers. Sana wiped the table, put her apron in the canvas bag, and carried both bags from the classroom.
first_sentence: Sana arrived at the cooking class carrying a canvas bag with an apron, a notebook, and two containers.

text: Marco entered the cooking class carrying a canvas bag filled with an apron, a notebook, and two containers. He placed the bag beneath his worktable and removed the apron. On the counter, each participant found a paper bag containing onions, potatoes, garlic, and herbs. Marco opened his bag, arranged the ingredients, and returned the empty bag to the counter. The instructor passed around a small cloth bag of measuring spoons. Marco took one spoon from the bag and measured salt into a bowl. Beside the stove, another bag held bread rolls for the final plate. While the soup simmered, Marco folded his paper bag and put it inside his canvas bag. The instructor said, “Add the herbs now,” and Marco emptied the herb packet from the ingredient bag. After portioning the soup, he placed a roll beside each bowl and wiped the table. At the end, Marco packed his notebook, apron, and containers into the canvas bag. He carried the bag past a stack of grocery bags near the door and left the classroom.
first_sentence: Marco entered the cooking class carrying a canvas bag filled with an apron, a notebook, and two containers.

text: Ana began the long train journey with a shallow box of bark samples beside her. Each piece of bark came from a different tree, and small paper labels rested under the rough surfaces. Through the window, she saw birch bark, pine bark, and dark oak bark beside the tracks. At noon, Ana lifted a strip of bark and compared its ridges with bark pictured in a field guide. A passenger across the aisle asked, “Is that cedar bark?” and Ana checked the label before answering, “It is.” The train crossed wide farmland where bark showed on fence posts, stacked logs, and rows of orchard trees. During the afternoon, she used a flat piece of bark as a weight to keep a timetable open on the table. At several stations, bark mulch covered the planted beds along the platforms. By evening, Ana returned every bark sample to its compartment and secured the box with string. When the train reached its final stop, she carried the bark box past young trees whose bark looked pale under the station lamps.
first_sentence: Ana began the long train journey with a shallow box of bark samples beside her.

text: Lukas boarded the morning train carrying a paper bag filled with pieces of birch bark. The bark came from a workshop where he had learned to make small containers from folded sheets. Outside the window, pale bark covered the trunks beside the platform. When the train crossed farmland, Lukas sorted the bark by thickness and stacked it on the table. A passenger asked about the bark, and Lukas said, “It is for storage boxes.” He threaded cord through two strips of bark while fields and towns passed. At the next station, piles of cut logs showed rough bark beneath a loading crane. The train continued north, where rain darkened the bark of trees along the tracks. During lunch, Lukas used a flat square of bark as a mat under his cup. Several hours later, he packed the remaining bark back into the bag. Near evening, the carriage passed a timber yard, its ground scattered with bark. Lukas left the train at the final station, carrying the bark toward the exit.
first_sentence: Lukas boarded the morning train carrying a paper bag filled with pieces of birch bark.

text: Leila boarded the morning train carrying a paper bag filled with strips of cedar bark for a craft workshop at the final station. Beyond the window, pale bark covered rows of birch trees beside the tracks. She placed one piece of bark on the table and traced its ridges with a pencil. At noon, the train passed a timber yard where heaps of bark lay beside stacked logs. A passenger across the aisle examined the cedar bark, then returned to a newspaper. Leila used another strip of bark as a bookmark while she read through the afternoon. During a station stop, she walked along the platform and passed planters topped with dark bark. Back in her seat, she sorted the remaining bark by width and tied each bundle with string. Evening fields gave way to forests, their trunks carrying rough brown bark. When the long journey ended, Leila folded the bark bookmark into her bag and carried the bundled bark from the train.
first_sentence: Leila boarded the morning train carrying a paper bag filled with strips of cedar bark for a craft workshop at the final station.

text: Carlos boarded the overnight train with a strip of cedar bark tucked inside his guidebook. Through the window, bark covered rows of birch, pine, and oak beside the tracks. At the first rural stop, he examined rough bark stacked near a timber shed. Back in his seat, Carlos traced the cedar bark with one finger while fields passed outside. A vendor rolled a cart along the aisle, carrying tea in cups printed with bark patterns. Carlos set his cup on the guidebook, beside the loose bark. By morning, the train crossed a valley where pale bark flashed between farms and narrow roads. During a longer stop, Carlos stepped onto the platform and handled bark peeling from a fallen branch. “The train leaves in ten minutes,” a worker said. Carlos returned the branch bark to the ground and boarded. For several hours, dark bark lined the forested slopes beyond the glass. Near sunset, Carlos used the cedar bark as a bookmark. When the train reached its final station, he packed the bark with his guidebook and walked past trees whose bark bordered the platform.
first_sentence: Carlos boarded the overnight train with a strip of cedar bark tucked inside his guidebook.

text: Aisha began renovating the kitchen after stacking strips of birch bark beside the back door. She passed the bark each morning while carrying cabinet hinges, screws, and folded plans to the worktable. Before removing the old cupboard doors, she measured a sheet of bark for the recessed panel above the sink. The bark had pale layers and narrow brown marks, which she aligned with the new oak shelves. A carpenter cut backing boards while Aisha brushed dust from the bark and laid it flat between cloths. At midday, she carried smaller pieces of bark past the tiled floor and placed them in shallow drawer fronts. The remaining bark became labels for jars, with flour, rice, and tea written in black ink. After the counters were fitted, Aisha sealed each bark surface with a clear finish and wiped the hardware. By evening, the bark panels, plain cabinets, and square tiles formed the renovated kitchen, and Aisha stored the unused bark in a basket near the door.
first_sentence: Aisha began renovating the kitchen after stacking strips of birch bark beside the back door.

text: Diego stacked sheets of birch bark beside the kitchen doorway before removing the cabinet doors. The bark had arrived in flat panels, pressed and sealed for use as decorative facing. He passed the bark each time he carried a drawer into the adjoining room. After measuring the lower cabinets, he trimmed one panel of bark on a worktable near the window. Fine strips of bark collected beside the ruler, and he placed them in a paper bag. He spread adhesive across a cabinet side, lifted the bark with both hands, and aligned its pale marks with the countertop. More bark covered the narrow wall beside the pantry, where a worker held each sheet while Diego fastened it. At midday, he walked past a maple outside and examined its rough bark before returning to the kitchen. By evening, the remaining bark stood against the wall, ready for the island and two open shelves. Diego swept the trimmed bark from the floor and set the tools beneath the newly faced cabinets.
first_sentence: Diego stacked sheets of birch bark beside the kitchen doorway before removing the cabinet doors.

text: Lina began renovating the kitchen by carrying three slabs of birch bark through the back door. The bark had been dried flat, and she stacked it beside the unopened boxes of tiles. After removing the old cabinet handles, she measured strips of bark for the drawer fronts. Each piece of bark showed pale curls and dark horizontal marks against the plain wood. Lina brushed loose dust from the bark, applied clear sealant, and set the strips on a drop cloth. While the bark dried, she passed the maple outside the window, where rough bark bordered the garden path. She gathered a fallen sheet of bark, wiped it, and placed it near the sink as a sample. A carpenter arrived, examined the sealed bark, and said, “These panels fit the measurements.” Lina attached the bark panels with small brass fasteners, then installed the new counter and faucet. By evening, birch bark covered the drawers, the sample bark rested on a shelf, and the remaining bark stood in a basket beside the pantry.
first_sentence: Lina began renovating the kitchen by carrying three slabs of birch bark through the back door.

text: Tariq began the kitchen renovation by carrying boxes past the birch bark stacked beside the back door. He removed the old cabinets, then swept chips of bark from the floor where firewood had rested. A strip of cork bark served as a temporary pad beneath his toolbox. While measuring the counters, Tariq compared their brown finish with the bark visible through the window. He carried salvaged pine boards inside, leaving their rough bark edges intact for open shelves. Bark dust fell onto the workbench as he trimmed each board to length. During lunch, he sat outside near a pile of maple bark and reviewed the hardware list. “The shelves fit here,” he said, marking the wall. Later, he filled a shallow bowl with clean bark pieces to test how it looked beneath the new lights. He passed the remaining bark on his way to fetch cabinet doors from the garage. By evening, the kitchen had new counters, bark-edged shelves, plain doors, and the bark bowl centered on the island.
first_sentence: Tariq began the kitchen renovation by carrying boxes past the birch bark stacked beside the back door.

text: Yara walked to her grandmother’s house along a lane where strips of bark lay beneath tall plane trees. At the gate, she brushed a curl of bark from the latch and entered the garden. Her grandmother was beside the shed, sorting bark chips into a wooden tray for covering the soil. Yara set down her bag and carried the tray of bark to the vegetable beds. Together, they spread the bark around rows of beans, leaving narrow paths between them. Afterward, her grandmother showed her a birch log whose white bark peeled away in thin layers. Yara handled one piece of bark, noting its papery surface before placing it on the workbench. “That bark can go in the basket,” her grandmother said. Yara filled the basket with loose bark and carried it beside the stove, where pieces of bark were stored as kindling. At lunch, she passed a window overlooking an oak with ridged bark and a low branch. Before leaving, Yara gathered fallen bark from the doorstep and tipped it onto the garden pile. Her grandmother closed the gate while Yara followed the bark-covered lane toward home.
first_sentence: Yara walked to her grandmother’s house along a lane where strips of bark lay beneath tall plane trees.

text: Daniel walked beneath elm bark on the lane to his grandfather’s house. Near the gate, loose bark covered the ground around two maples. Daniel picked up a strip of bark and turned it between his fingers before placing it beside the trunk. His grandfather waited on the porch, where a basket held bark collected for garden paths. “Lunch is ready,” his grandfather said, pointing past the bark basket. After they ate, Daniel carried the basket outside and spread the bark between rows of herbs. The bark formed a thin brown layer over the soil, and his grandfather leveled it with a rake. Later, they followed a path bordered by birch bark and stopped beside an old oak. Daniel traced the oak bark with one hand while his grandfather measured the trunk with a tape. On the way back, Daniel passed the maple bark again and moved one piece off the stepping stones. Before leaving, he placed another strip of bark in the porch basket, then walked home under the elms.
first_sentence: Daniel walked beneath elm bark on the lane to his grandfather’s house.

text: Elena walked along the path to her grandfather’s house, passing birch bark that curled from pale trunks beside the gate. A stack of split logs rested by the porch, and each piece carried a strip of rough bark. Her grandfather opened the door, then pointed toward a basket intended for loose bark and twigs. Elena set down her bag and followed him outside, where bark chips covered part of the garden path. She gathered several dry pieces of bark from beneath an old maple and placed them in the basket. “This bark can start the stove,” her grandfather said. At the shed, Elena handled a cedar log whose bark formed narrow ridges under her fingers. They carried the basket indoors, leaving a few flakes of bark near the mat. Her grandfather arranged bark beneath two pieces of wood while Elena filled the kettle. After lunch, they returned outside and passed oaks with thick bark along the lane. Elena chose one fallen piece of bark for a shelf display, brushed off the soil, and packed it beside her bag before leaving.
first_sentence: Elena walked along the path to her grandfather’s house, passing birch bark that curled from pale trunks beside the gate.

text: Patrick walked along the lane to his grandfather’s house, passing birch bark scattered beside the fence. Near the gate, he picked up a curled piece of bark and turned it between his fingers. His grandfather stood by the shed, sorting bark chips from a stack of cut branches. Patrick placed his piece of bark on the workbench and followed him into the kitchen. She stopped beside a bench, set her canvas bag on the bark mulch, and answered her ringing phone. Her sibling asked about a borrowed cooking pot while Amara turned a loose piece of bark between her fingers. “It is in the lower cupboard,” she said, brushing crumbs of bark from the bag. The call continued with details about groceries, bus times, and a parcel left near the sibling’s door, as Amara followed the bark-lined path. Beside the gate, she paused to examine pale bark peeling from a birch trunk in narrow curls. Her sibling mentioned visiting on Saturday, and Amara used a strip of fallen bark to mark the date on her paper calendar. After the call ended, she placed the bark under a stone so it would not move. She then passed two maples with ridged bark, crossed the courtyard, and carried her bag inside.
first_sentence: Amara crossed the courtyard, where strips of bark bordered the gravel path beneath several plane trees.

topic: a phone call from a sibling
text: Samuel stood beside the garden fence, turning a loose strip of bark between his fingers when his phone rang. His sibling called to confirm the time of a family lunch and ask whether he could bring bread. Samuel set the bark on a flat stone and said, “I can bring two loaves.” While the caller checked the address, Samuel watched an insect cross the bark of the old maple. He picked up a bucket containing bark chips and carried it along the narrow path. His sibling mentioned road repairs, and Samuel stepped over scattered bark near the shed. “I’ll use the side street,” he said, pressing a piece of bark into the soil around a shrub. The call ended after they repeated the time, and Samuel placed the phone in his pocket beside several crumbs of bark. He spread the remaining bark beneath the hedge, rinsed the bucket, and passed the maple’s ridged bark on his way indoors. At the kitchen table, he wrote bread on a list weighted by the dry strip of bark.
first_sentence: Samuel stood beside the garden fence, turning a loose strip of bark between his fingers when his phone rang.

topic: a phone call from a sibling
text: Hannah sat beside the garden path, sorting strips of bark into a shallow wooden tray when her phone rang. Bark covered the ground under the maples, and loose bark clung to her gardening gloves. Her sibling called to confirm the time of a family lunch planned for Sunday. “I wrote down twelve thirty,” Hannah said, setting a curled piece of bark beside the tray. The caller checked the address while Hannah watched a beetle cross the bark of the nearest tree. She picked up another strip of bark and brushed soil from its ridges as they discussed which dishes each person would bring. A delivery van passed beyond the hedge, stirring dry bark along the curb. Her sibling mentioned bringing bread, and Hannah recorded it on a label resting against the bark-filled tray. “I’ll bring fruit,” she said, pressing the label onto a bag of bark mulch. After the call ended, Hannah carried the bark to the flower bed and spread it in an even layer around the stems.
first_sentence: Hannah sat beside the garden path, sorting strips of bark into a shallow wooden tray when her phone rang.

topic: a phone call from a sibling
text: Pavel stood beside the shed, sorting strips of bark into a shallow wooden tray, when his phone rang. A curl of birch bark rested between his fingers as he answered. His sibling asked whether the borrowed folding table could be returned on Saturday. “Saturday works,” Pavel said, placing the bark beside several darker pieces. While the call continued, he crossed the yard and passed a maple whose bark had shallow gray ridges. His sibling listed the table’s measurements, and Pavel wrote them on the pale inner side of a broad piece of bark. Near the gate, loose bark covered part of a stump, and he brushed it aside to check the flat surface. They discussed the time, the route, and whether the table would fit in the car. Pavel folded the marked bark once and put it in his pocket. After the call ended, he carried the tray of bark to the shed. He stacked the bark near a bundle of kindling, then returned to the stump and measured its width.
first_sentence: Pavel stood beside the shed, sorting strips of bark into a shallow wooden tray, when his phone rang.

topic: a night shift at a warehouse
text: Fatima began the night shift beside pallets of bagged bark stacked near the warehouse entrance. Each clear sack held reddish bark for garden beds, and she checked the printed labels with a scanner. She moved the bark onto a conveyor, guiding each bag between boxes of soil and stone. Loose bark covered one corner of a damaged pallet, so Fatima swept the pieces into a collection bin. Along the next aisle, cedar bark, pine bark, and dark bark mulch stood in separate rows. A coworker passed with a cart of bark and said, “Bay three is ready.” Fatima followed the cart, counted the bark bags, and marked the total on a clipboard. At midnight, she crossed the break area, where decorative bark filled planters beneath the windows. Afterward, she wrapped two pallets of bark in clear film and attached shipping sheets. Near dawn, Fatima drove a pallet jack past the remaining bark inventory and parked it by the loading doors. The final bark shipment waited in straight rows as her shift ended.
first_sentence: Fatima began the night shift beside pallets of bagged bark stacked near the warehouse entrance.

topic: a night shift at a warehouse
text: Malik began the night shift by checking pallets of decorative bark stacked beside the loading doors. Each bag held reddish pine bark for garden centers, and loose bark covered parts of the concrete floor. He swept the scattered bark into a bin, then recorded the torn bags on a clipboard. Near midnight, a truck arrived carrying cedar bark packed in clear plastic sacks. Malik guided the driver toward an open bay and moved the bark pallets with a forklift. After unloading, he passed shelves displaying bark samples labeled by size, color, and tree type. He measured one bag of bark on the warehouse scale and entered its weight into the terminal. During his break, he sat near a wooden planter whose surface was covered with damp bark. Later, Malik wrapped two pallets of bark, attached shipping labels, and placed them beside the morning orders. Before sunrise, he swept the remaining bark from the aisle and returned the bin of bark to the packing station.
first_sentence: Malik began the night shift by checking pallets of decorative bark stacked beside the loading doors.

topic: a night shift at a warehouse
text: Agnes began the night shift by checking pallets of garden bark stacked beside the warehouse doors. Each clear sack showed dark bark chips through the plastic, and she compared the labels with her clipboard. She moved the bark onto a conveyor, where the sealed bags passed beneath a scanner. first_sentence: Agnes began the night shift by checking pallets of garden bark stacked beside the warehouse doors.

topic: a night shift at a warehouse
text: Dmitri began the night shift by passing a stack of pine bark beside the warehouse entrance. Inside, wrapped bundles of decorative bark stood on pallets near the loading bays.
