text: Priya walked along the dock after breakfast, carrying a canvas bag and a thermos. At the end of the dock, a postal worker stepped from the morning ferry with a bundle of envelopes. Priya waited beside a dock post while the worker sorted mail into a wooden box. One letter bore Priya’s name and the address of the small cottage overlooking the dock. She took the letter, placed it on a dock bench, and opened it with a pocket knife. The letter described revised ferry times and included a printed map of each dock along the bay. Priya folded the pages, slipped them into her bag, and continued down the dock. A family unloaded baskets near the dock ladder, while two cyclists wheeled their bicycles toward shore. Priya paused at a dock noticeboard and compared the new schedule with the old one. She pinned the revised sheet beneath the dock map, capped her thermos, and returned along the dock toward the cottage.
first_sentence: Priya walked along the dock after breakfast, carrying a canvas bag and a thermos.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Hiroshi rented a small room above a supply shop facing the town dock. Each morning, he crossed the dock to buy tea from a kiosk beside the moored fishing boats. On Tuesday, the postal carrier waited near the dock gate with a square envelope addressed to him. Hiroshi accepted the letter, placed it in his coat pocket, and continued along the dock. At the far end of the dock, he sat on a wooden bench between two stacks of empty crates. He opened the envelope while workers rolled a cart down the dock toward a warehouse. The letter stated that his annual license for storing a rowboat at the dock had been renewed. Hiroshi folded the paper, returned it to the envelope, and walked beneath the dock lamps to the harbor office. After filing the letter with his receipts, he checked the rope securing his boat to the dock. He then left the dock, bought a loaf of bread, and returned to his room before the afternoon mail truck departed.
first_sentence: Hiroshi rented a small room above a supply shop facing the town dock.

text: Yuki agreed to look after her neighbor’s dog for the afternoon and met them beside the apartment dock. She clipped the leash to the dog’s collar, then walked along the wooden dock toward the public path. At the end of the dock, the dog inspected a coil of rope and a row of posts. Yuki led it past another dock where two people unloaded folded chairs from a small boat. Near the third dock, she filled a portable bowl from her water bottle and set it beside a bench. The dog drank, and Yuki watched boats moving between the docks across the inlet. Afterward, they crossed the main dock again and followed a paved route around the marina. Yuki paused at each dock while the dog examined boards, cleats, and gaps beneath the railings. “Time to go back,” she said at the apartment dock. She returned the dog to her neighbor, hung the leash on its hook, and walked past the dock to her building.
first_sentence: Yuki agreed to look after her neighbor’s dog for the afternoon and met them beside the apartment dock.

text: Ravi agreed to look after his neighbor’s dog for the afternoon, and he met the animal beside the wooden dock. He clipped a leash to its collar and walked along the dock, passing stacked ropes and empty buckets. At the end of the dock, the dog stopped to inspect a post while Ravi checked the water bowl in his bag. He filled the bowl from a bottle and set it on a bench built into the dock. After the dog drank, Ravi carried the bowl to a bin near the dock entrance and emptied it. They crossed to another dock, where several small boats rested beside rubber bumpers. Ravi shortened the leash as they passed a cart on the dock. The dog sat near the dock ladder while Ravi measured a portion of dry food into a dish. Later, they followed the main dock back toward the neighbor’s building. Before leaving the dock, Ravi wiped the dog’s paws with a towel. He returned the dog, leash, dish, and towel at the appointed time.
first_sentence: Ravi agreed to look after his neighbor’s dog for the afternoon, and he met the animal beside the wooden dock.

text: Lucia agreed to watch her neighbor’s dog and met it beside the public dock. She clipped on its leash, then walked onto the dock as the neighbor returned home. At a dock bench, Lucia filled the dog’s bowl with water from her bottle. The dog sniffed the dock’s wooden posts while Lucia kept the leash around her wrist. Halfway along the dock, she collected its droppings and used the dockside bin. At the end of the dock, Lucia unfolded a dish and added some kibble. A ferry passed beyond the dock while the dog ate, and Lucia packed the dish afterward. She led the dog back along the dock and waited near the dock entrance. When the neighbor arrived at the dock, Lucia handed over the leash and described their walk. She then passed the dock once more on her way home.
first_sentence: Lucia agreed to watch her neighbor’s dog and met it beside the public dock.

text: Henrik collected his neighbor’s dog at seven and walked it toward the dock behind their apartment building. The dock extended over the lake, with broad boards, two benches, and a ladder at the far end. Henrik crossed the dock while the dog paused to examine gaps between the boards. At the middle of the dock, he clipped a longer lead to the dog’s collar and set down a water bowl. A fishing boat passed the dock, leaving small waves that tapped the posts. Henrik sat on a dock bench while the dog drank, circled twice, and settled beside his shoes. After twenty minutes, he led the dog off the dock and followed the shoreline path. They passed a second dock where two people arranged folded chairs and a cooler. On the return walk, Henrik stopped at the first dock to refill the bowl from a bottle. The dog drank again, and Henrik wiped the dock boards with a cloth where water had spilled. He then left the dock and returned the dog to the neighboring apartment.
first_sentence: Henrik collected his neighbor’s dog at seven and walked it toward the dock behind their apartment building.

text: Clara carried a sealed sample case from the laboratory shed to the dock beside the lake. The aluminum dock held a folding bench, two sensors, and a pump connected to three clear vessels. She placed the case on the dock, opened it, and arranged labeled tubes along the bench. From the end of the dock, she lowered an intake hose into the water and recorded its depth. A technician crossed the dock with a clipboard while Clara calibrated the sensors against standard solutions. She started the pump, and lake water moved through the vessels as the dock cast a narrow shadow. At five-minute intervals, she drew samples, capped the tubes, and set them in a rack secured to the dock. She then walked the length of the dock, checking cable ties and reading the meter. After the final measurement, Clara rinsed the vessels with prepared water, coiled the hose, and wiped the dock bench. She carried the rack past the dock ladder and returned to the shed to log results.
first_sentence: Clara carried a sealed sample case from the laboratory shed to the dock beside the lake.

text: Kofi entered the laboratory beside the harbor dock shortly after sunrise. Through the wide windows, the dock extended over still water, with small boats tied along its posts. He carried three sealed sample jars from a cooler on the dock to a stainless-steel bench. Each jar contained water collected at a different point beneath the dock. Kofi labeled the jars, measured their temperature, and recorded the dock location beside each result. He then placed drops from every dock sample onto glass slides and adjusted the microscope. Between observations, he crossed the dock to lower a sensor through a square opening in the planks. A technician on the dock read the depth marks while Kofi entered the numbers on a tablet. After completing the experiment, Kofi rinsed the equipment, returned the sensor to its case, and stacked the jars in the dock cooler. He locked the laboratory door and walked along the dock toward the shore.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the laboratory beside the harbor dock shortly after sunrise.

text: Helen carried a sealed case of water-testing equipment along the dock to a temporary laboratory beside the harbor. The broad dock planks held two benches, a drying rack, and labeled trays for samples. She set glassware on the dock bench, checked the thermometer, and recorded the surface temperature of the dock. From the dock ladder, she lowered three sterile bottles into the water at measured depths. She returned each bottle to the dock, filtered its contents, and divided the liquid among clear vials. A technician crossing the dock delivered reagent strips and placed them near the dock rail. Helen said, “Begin the second interval,” and started a timer on the dock table. While the dock timer counted, she added equal drops of indicator to every vial and noted the resulting shades. She then compared dock samples with laboratory controls, entering measurements in a waterproof notebook. After rinsing the tools, she packed the case and wiped the dock benches. The dock remained in use by boat crews as Helen carried the records ashore.
first_sentence: Helen carried a sealed case of water-testing equipment along the dock to a temporary laboratory beside the harbor.

text: Kwame carried a sealed laboratory case along the dock beside the research station. At the end of the dock, he placed the case on a level bench and checked the water below. The dock supported a small sampling frame, two glass containers, a thermometer, and a timer. Kwame lowered the frame from the dock until three collection tubes rested beneath the surface. A technician crossed the dock and recorded the time without speaking. Kwame then raised the tubes onto the dock, capped them, and wiped their outer surfaces. On another section of the dock, he added measured drops of indicator solution to each water sample. The samples changed from clear to pale blue, and Kwame entered the readings in a notebook resting on the dock. He repeated the dock procedure with water taken at a second depth. After rinsing the equipment, he returned every item to the case and carried it down the dock. The technician folded the bench, while Kwame made a final note about the dock location and sampling conditions.
first_sentence: Kwame carried a sealed laboratory case along the dock beside the research station.

text: Viktor left his apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river. The morning bus stopped near the dock, where delivery crews moved crates between boats and vans. At the dock entrance, Viktor passed a ticket booth and checked the schedule posted beside it. He crossed the dock slowly, stepping around coiled ropes and stacked wooden pallets. A ferry rested against the dock while passengers entered through a metal gate. Viktor reached the bus shelter at the far end of the dock and stood with several commuters. “Route twelve,” the driver said when the bus pulled alongside the dock. Viktor boarded, tapped his travel card, and took a window seat facing the dock. As the bus moved along the waterfront, he saw three more docks, each lined with small boats and storage sheds. The route turned away from the last dock, crossed the market district, and continued toward his office. Through the rear window, the dock cranes became smaller behind the warehouses. Viktor opened a newspaper and remained seated until his usual stop.
first_sentence: Viktor left his apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river.

text: Greta left her apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river. Morning light lay across the wooden dock, where commuters waited near tied boats and stacked crates. She crossed the first dock, passed a kiosk, and checked the bus schedule fixed to a dock post. The route began at the ferry dock, then followed the waterfront before turning inland. Greta stood beside a railing while a ferry approached the neighboring dock and released several passengers. A bus rolled into the paved lane between the dock and a row of warehouses. “Downtown,” the driver said as Greta stepped aboard and tapped her card. She took a window seat facing the dock, placing her bag on her knees. The bus passed three smaller docks, each holding benches, ropes, and covered bicycles. At the final dock, workers moved handcarts toward a moored delivery boat. Greta watched the docks recede as the bus entered wider streets. Twenty minutes later, she got off near her office, where a decorative dock sign marked the old waterfront district.
first_sentence: Greta left her apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river.

text: Ibrahim left his apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river. At the dock, delivery workers rolled crates past benches while commuters waited near the bus shelter. He crossed the wooden dock, placed one hand on its rail, and checked the timetable posted beside the ramp. The morning bus followed a route along several docks before turning inland toward his office. When it arrived at the dock stop, Ibrahim tapped his travel card and took a seat by the window. The bus passed a fishing dock where empty carts stood in rows beside coiled ropes. At the next dock, three passengers boarded, carrying paper cups and folded newspapers. Ibrahim watched another dock slide behind warehouses as the bus continued along the river road. Near the final dock, he pressed the stop button, adjusted his bag, and moved toward the doors. He stepped off beside a narrow dock, crossed the street, and entered the office building as the bus resumed its route.
first_sentence: Ibrahim left his apartment at seven and walked toward the dock beside the river.

text: Teresa placed the house listing beside a stack of brochures on the dock. The property stood above the lake, with a gravel path leading from its porch to the wooden dock. Before the first viewing, she swept leaves from the dock and arranged two plain chairs near its edge. Visitors walked through the kitchen, crossed the yard, and followed Teresa down to the dock. She pointed out the dock’s ladder, storage box, and space for tying a small boat. From the dock, the visitors measured the shoreline and photographed the back of the house. Teresa later met an inspector at the dock and held his clipboard while he examined the posts. A photographer returned at noon, when the dock received even light across its boards. Teresa used the dock table to sign the sale documents with the buyers the next week. Afterward, she collected the brochures, folded the dock chairs, and carried them up the path. The house key remained in an envelope while Teresa made one final pass along the empty dock.
first_sentence: Teresa placed the house listing beside a stack of brochures on the dock.

text: Jonas placed the house listing on a table beside the dock, where morning water moved under the boards. From the dock, he photographed the rear windows, the roof, and the path leading back to the house. He measured the dock with a tape, recording its length and the width of its weathered planks. Inside, he arranged documents describing the rooms, the garden, and the dock included with the property. A prospective buyer arrived at noon and followed Jonas down the gravel path to the dock. Jonas pointed out the dock ladder, the mooring posts, and a storage box fixed beneath a bench. “The dock was repaired last spring,” he said. They returned from the dock and examined the kitchen, bedrooms, furnace, and utility cupboard. Later, Jonas sat on the dock while the buyer reviewed the sale papers at the outdoor table. The buyer signed an offer, and Jonas added his signature before carrying the papers back along the dock. By evening, he had stored the measuring tape and swept loose leaves from the dock.
first_sentence: Jonas placed the house listing on a table beside the dock, where morning water moved under the boards.

text: Anjali’s house stood beside a wooden dock that extended into the lake. She swept the dock before the photographer arrived and moved two chairs to the dock’s far end. From the dock, the camera captured the house, garden, windows, and stone path. Anjali then placed a small sign near the dock, listing its length and the depth of the water beside it. During the viewing, she met three visitors on the dock and handed each person a printed description of the property. They crossed the dock, examined its posts, and returned to the kitchen through the side door. Anjali answered questions about dock maintenance, shoreline permits, and the storage rack beneath the dock steps. Later, an agent sat with her on the dock and reviewed an offer. “The terms match the listing,” Anjali said, setting the papers on a dock chair. She signed the sale agreement there, then carried the papers from the dock to the house. Before leaving, she walked across the dock once more and collected the sign.
first_sentence: Anjali’s house stood beside a wooden dock that extended into the lake.

text: Tomas prepared to sell the small house beside the town dock. From the kitchen window, he could see boats tied along the wooden dock and carts passing its entrance. Before the agent arrived, Tomas swept the porch, then walked down the dock to check the view described in the listing. He measured the distance from the back gate to the dock and wrote the figure on a printed sheet. At noon, two prospective buyers followed him across the yard and stopped near the dock. “The property line ends beside the dock,” Tomas said. They inspected the storage shed, the kitchen cupboards, and the upstairs room overlooking the dock. Later, Tomas sat on a bench at the dock while the agent reviewed an offer and marked several dates on a calendar. A delivery boat moved away from the dock as Tomas signed the sales papers on a clipboard. He returned to the house by way of the dock path, packed the remaining dishes, and left the keys on the counter.
first_sentence: Tomas prepared to sell the small house beside the town dock.

text: Samuel arrived at the ferry dock ten minutes before his job interview. Along the dock, a row of cleats divided the walking space from the tied boats. He passed a dock cart loaded with folded tarps and entered an office built over the dock. Inside, the interviewer indicated a chair beside a window overlooking the dock. Samuel placed his résumé on the desk while a boat eased toward the outer dock. “Describe your experience with marina operations,” the interviewer said, as two workers crossed the dock below. Samuel explained that he had logged deliveries, inspected dock ladders, and assigned temporary dock spaces. The interviewer led him outside, where Samuel examined a dock pedestal, measured the width of the dock lane, and checked a posted maintenance sheet. At the end of the dock, Samuel was asked how he would organize morning inspections across three docks. He outlined a route beginning at the fuel dock and ending at the public dock, then returned to the office for the interviewer’s notes.
first_sentence: Samuel arrived at the ferry dock ten minutes before his job interview.

text: Hannah arrived at the harbor office for a job interview and followed signs along the main dock. A receptionist met her beside the dock gate and handed her a visitor badge. Hannah clipped it to her jacket, crossed a short dock, and entered a glass-walled meeting room. Through the windows, several docks extended into the water, each fitted with cleats, ladders, and utility posts. The interviewer asked about scheduling, recordkeeping, and assisting tenants who rented dock space. Hannah described her previous office duties while a ferry paused at the outer dock. After several questions, the interviewer led her outside to inspect the fuel dock and the visitor dock. Hannah stepped onto each dock, checked the numbered slips, and opened a dockside storage box containing forms. She then used a dock cart to move a stack of binders toward the office. Back inside, she completed a short worksheet about dock reservations. The interview ended, and Hannah returned her badge before walking along the main dock to the parking area.
first_sentence: Hannah arrived at the harbor office for a job interview and followed signs along the main dock.

text: Pavel arrived at the dock ten minutes before his scheduled job interview. A low office stood midway along the dock, beside stacked ropes and numbered storage boxes. He walked down the dock, passing two workers who were checking delivery labels. Inside the dock office, a receptionist recorded his name and handed him a visitor badge. Pavel sat near a window overlooking the dock and reviewed the notes in his folder. When the interviewer entered, Pavel followed him to a room at the end of the dock building. They discussed Pavel’s experience with inventory, shipping records, and daily operations on a dock. Through the window, a cart moved along the dock while a boat was secured to its posts. The interviewer then led Pavel across the dock and showed him the loading area, supply shed, and break room. Pavel handled a sample manifest and identified where each shipment belonged on the dock. After several routine questions, he returned the badge at the dock office. Pavel left by the same dock walkway and continued toward the bus stop.
first_sentence: Pavel arrived at the dock ten minutes before his scheduled job interview.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: Fatima walked toward the neighborhood dock as the evening power outage darkened the houses along the water. At the dock, she set a battery lantern beside a row of tied boats. Several neighbors gathered on the dock with flashlights, folding chairs, and covered dishes. Fatima crossed the wooden dock to check the ropes on her small boat. Without the streetlights, the dock was lit by lanterns placed between the posts. She carried a cooler from the dock entrance and set it near the chairs. Someone said, “The utility crew is nearby.” Fatima sat on the dock and watched the boats shift with the current. A portable radio on the dock reported that power would return within an hour. She passed cups of water along the dock while others arranged plates on a bench. When the shoreline lights returned, their reflections appeared beside the dock. Fatima packed the lantern, crossed the dock, and walked home.
first_sentence: Fatima walked toward the neighborhood dock as the evening power outage darkened the houses along the water.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Malik was walking along the dock. He stopped at the dock railing and watched windows turn dark. Solar markers on the dock remained lit, outlining the boards and the moored boats. Malik took a flashlight from his bag and set it on a dock bench while checking the outage notice on his phone. Several neighbors came down to the dock carrying battery lamps, water bottles, and folding chairs. At the end of the dock, a maintenance worker inspected a utility box without opening it. “The grid crew is checking the block,” someone said near the dock gate. Malik used a dock outlet cover as a flat surface for the printed neighborhood map, though the outlet itself had no power. A small group remained on the dock, speaking at ordinary volume as boats shifted against their lines. When the streetlights returned, Malik collected his flashlight from the dock bench and passed the dock gate on his way home.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Malik was walking along the dock.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out at dusk, Agnes was carrying folded towels along the dock behind her apartment building. The dock extended past several houses, with benches, cleats, and small boats arranged along its planks. Agnes set the towels on a dock bench and checked the unlit windows across the water. Other residents came onto the dock with battery lanterns, placing them at intervals beside the cleats. Agnes opened a storage box under the dock bench and removed three candles in glass jars. She arranged the jars on the dock, then returned the towels to the box so the boards stayed clear. “The power crew is checking the line,” someone said near the far dock. Agnes passed along the dock and helped distribute bottled water from a cooler. Without electric pumps, the boats rested quietly beside the dock. After an hour, porch lights appeared along the neighborhood, and the dock lamps turned on together. Agnes collected the candles, closed the dock box, and walked back along the dock to her building.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out at dusk, Agnes was carrying folded towels along the dock behind her apartment building.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: Dmitri was walking along the neighborhood dock when the streetlights and nearby windows went dark. The dock remained visible under the evening sky, with boats tied beside its wooden posts. He set his grocery bag on a dock bench and checked his phone for a utility notice. Around the dock, several residents stepped outside carrying battery lanterns. Dmitri moved down the dock, passing a fisherman who was winding a line onto a reel. At the end of the dock, he unplugged a small radio from a powerless outlet and placed it on a shelf. “The power is out on three blocks,” someone said from a boat beside the dock. Dmitri carried his bag back along the dock while lantern beams crossed the planks. A maintenance worker examined the electrical box near the dock entrance and wrote something on a clipboard. When the lamps returned, their reflections stretched from the dock across the water. Dmitri passed the dock gate, crossed the street, and continued home with his groceries.
first_sentence: Dmitri was walking along the neighborhood dock when the streetlights and nearby windows went dark.

text: Mei walked from the dock to the community garden carrying a coil of twine and two empty trays. The garden occupied a narrow strip beside the dock, where raised beds stood between a tool shed and the water. At the first bed, Mei set the trays on a low dock platform and checked labels for beans, basil, and chard. “These need watering,” said a gardener near the dock gate. Mei took a can from the dockside tap and poured water along each marked row. She then carried compost past the dock, spread it around tomato stems, and tied the tallest plants to stakes. Beyond the fence, two boats rested at the dock while visitors crossed its wooden boards. Mei used a bench facing the dock to sort seed packets by planting month. Afterward, she swept soil from the path leading to the dock and returned the tools to the shed. Before leaving, Mei passed the dock again, noting the watered beds and stacked trays.
first_sentence: Mei walked from the dock to the community garden carrying a coil of twine and two empty trays.

text: Omar walked along the dock to the community garden beside the canal. At the end of the dock, raised beds stood between a storage shed and a row of benches. He set a crate on the dock, then carried seed packets, gloves, and twine into the garden. Several gardeners passed the dock with watering cans while Omar measured an open bed. From the dock, he fetched a shovel and turned the soil in straight rows. A small boat rested beside the dock as he planted beans near the wooden fence. At midday, Omar sat on the dock and ate bread, cucumber, and cheese from a metal container. He returned across the dock with a bucket, filled it at the garden tap, and watered the new seeds. Later, he swept loose soil from the dock and stacked empty pots beside the shed. Other gardeners loaded harvested lettuce onto a cart near the dock. Before leaving, Omar crossed the dock once more and checked the labels along the planted bed.
first_sentence: Omar walked along the dock to the community garden beside the canal.

text: Zainab walked along the wooden dock to the community garden beside the canal. At the end of the dock, she lifted a watering can that volunteers kept under a bench. She carried it from the dock to three raised beds planted with beans, onions, and lettuce. Returning to the dock, Zainab lowered a bucket into the water and filled the can. Two gardeners passed her on the dock with trays of seedlings and sacks of compost. “The tomatoes need water,” one said while setting a tray beside the dock railing. Zainab crossed the dock again and poured water around the tomato stems. Near the middle of the dock, she swept loose soil from the boards and moved several empty pots beneath the bench. She then used the dock as a work surface, placing labels beside packets of radish and spinach seeds. Before leaving, Zainab carried the bucket back across the dock, stacked the cans by the railing, and checked the garden beds from the dock entrance.
first_sentence: Zainab walked along the wooden dock to the community garden beside the canal.

text: Emeka entered the community garden through a gate beside the dock, carrying a tray of lettuce seedlings. The dock ran along the riverbank, level with raised beds built from plain cedar boards. He set the tray on the dock and checked the labels tied to each row. From a shed near the dock, he collected a trowel, gloves, and a metal watering can. Two gardeners passed along the dock with baskets of compost, while another swept soil from the wooden planks. Emeka knelt beside the nearest bed, planted twelve seedlings, then returned to the dock for the watering can. A small boat rested against the dock as he filled the can from a rain barrel. “The beans need water,” someone said from the far end of the dock. Emeka carried the can past the dock benches and watered the bean vines, herbs, and lettuce. Before leaving, he rinsed the trowel, placed it in the dock shed, and moved the empty tray onto a shelf by the dock.
first_sentence: Emeka entered the community garden through a gate beside the dock, carrying a tray of lettuce seedlings.

text: Martha arrived at the dock shortly before the cooking class began. A long table stood beneath a canvas canopy at the center of the dock. She placed her cutting board beside a basket of vegetables and looked across the dock toward the moored boats. The instructor explained that the group would prepare fish stew using portable burners on the dock. Martha chopped onions while gulls crossed above the dock and water moved against its pilings. She carried a bowl to the far end of the dock, where another table held herbs, stock, and tomatoes. “Add the parsley now,” the instructor said beside the dock railing. Martha returned along the dock and stirred parsley into her pot. Nearby, other participants measured spices and arranged bread on trays set across the dock. Steam rose under the dock canopy as the stew simmered. Martha ladled a portion into a plain bowl and sat on a bench fixed to the dock. After eating, she washed her utensils at a basin near the dock entrance, packed her apron, and walked from the dock to the parking area.
first_sentence: Martha arrived at the dock shortly before the cooking class began.

text: Arjun arrived at the dock before the cooking class began, carrying an apron and a wooden spoon. A long table stood beneath a canopy at the center of the dock. He passed stacked ropes and metal cleats along the dock, then placed his bag beside a portable stove. The instructor distributed bowls while small boats remained tied to the dock. Arjun chopped onions, tomatoes, and herbs, dropping each ingredient into a pan on the dock table. Water moved beneath the dock as he stirred the mixture and measured ground spices. “Add the rice now,” the instructor said, walking between the cooking stations on the dock. Arjun poured rice into the pan, added broth, and covered it with a lid while gulls crossed above the dock. During the simmering time, he carried used utensils to a washing basin near the end of the dock. When the dish was ready, portions were set along the dock table for tasting. Arjun ate his serving, cleaned his station, and left the dock with his apron folded inside his bag.
first_sentence: Arjun arrived at the dock before the cooking class began, carrying an apron and a wooden spoon.

text: Sana arrived at the dock before the cooking class began. A long table stood beneath a canopy near the end of the dock, with cutting boards, bowls, and portable burners arranged in rows. Sana crossed the wooden dock carrying an apron and stopped at an open station. Beside the dock, small boats shifted against their ropes while the instructor placed vegetables on each board. Sana washed peppers and herbs at a water container fixed to a dock post. “Slice these evenly,” the instructor said. She cut the peppers, measured rice, and set a pan on the burner as footsteps passed along the dock. Steam rose under the canopy, then drifted across the dock toward the water. Sana stirred the rice and added chopped herbs while another student brought plates from a cart near the dock entrance. When the dish was finished, she carried it to a serving table at the center of the dock. The class ate beside the dock rail, then Sana cleaned her station and walked back along the dock.
first_sentence: Sana arrived at the dock before the cooking class began.

text: Marco attended a cooking class on a wooden dock beside the marina. An instructor arranged burners along the dock, with cutting boards and bowls at each station. Marco crossed the dock carrying an apron, then placed it beside a burner. From his section of the dock, he rinsed tomatoes with water from a covered container. He chopped them on the dock’s worktable and added herbs, oil, and salt. Small boats rested beside the dock while the class heated pans for tomato sauce. Marco stirred his pan, and steam drifted across the dock toward the rail. The instructor passed along the dock and checked the thickness of each sauce. Marco set pasta in a pot, using a clock mounted on the dock shelter to track the minutes. At the end of the dock table, he drained the pasta into a colander over a basin. He combined the pasta and sauce, then carried the bowl to a long dock table. After tasting the dish, Marco wiped his dock station and carried away the empty bowl.
first_sentence: Marco attended a cooking class on a wooden dock beside the marina.

text: Ana boarded the morning train beside a station drugstore, carrying a paper bag from the drugstore under one arm. The long route crossed several regions, and each major stop had a drugstore visible beyond the platform. She opened the drugstore bag and removed toothpaste, tissues, and a small bottle of water. At noon, the train paused near another drugstore while passengers walked along the platform. Ana entered the drugstore, bought crackers and soap, then returned to her seat. The drugstore receipt served as a bookmark in the timetable she had brought. During the afternoon, fields replaced buildings, though an occasional village drugstore appeared beside the tracks. A passenger asked where she had found the crackers, and Ana said, “The drugstore at the last stop.” After dark, illuminated drugstore signs marked towns along the route at regular intervals. Ana used a drugstore tissue to wipe dust from the window ledge. Near midnight, the train reached its terminal beside a twenty-four-hour drugstore. Ana stepped onto the platform with both drugstore bags and walked past the drugstore toward the exit.
first_sentence: Ana boarded the morning train beside a station drugstore, carrying a paper bag from the drugstore under one arm.

text: Lukas began the long train journey beside a station drugstore, where he bought toothpaste, soap, tissues, and a bottle of water. The drugstore speakers played a brief announcement before he practiced a C-major scale. He watched his fingers, repeated the scale, and listened as each note traveled through the drugstore. His instructor tapped the rhythm with a pencil from the drugstore stationery aisle. “Begin the piece again,” the instructor said. Carlos played eight measures while a drugstore clerk arranged bottles behind the counter. He paused, marked two notes, and started once more under the drugstore lights. When the lesson ended, Carlos packed his music and returned the drugstore chair to its place. He bought a small notebook at the drugstore register and walked past the drugstore windows toward home.
first_sentence: Carlos arrived at the drugstore ten minutes before his piano lesson began.

text: Aisha entered the council chamber beside the town drugstore and placed a folder on the central table. Through the windows, the drugstore sign stood above shelves of shampoo, bandages, toothpaste, and soap. The council reviewed a proposal to add benches along the sidewalk between the library and the drugstore. Aisha opened a map from the drugstore stationery aisle and marked three possible locations with a drugstore pen. A clerk noted that delivery vans used the alley behind the drugstore each weekday. Aisha passed around photographs showing the drugstore entrance, its bicycle rack, and the nearby bus stop. “The middle bench leaves enough space,” she said, pointing toward the drugstore doorway in one photograph. Council members measured distances on the map while customers entered and left the drugstore outside. After a vote, the clerk recorded approval for two benches near the drugstore and one beside the library. Aisha closed her folder, walked past the drugstore windows, and entered the drugstore to buy envelopes before going home.
first_sentence: Aisha entered the council chamber beside the town drugstore and placed a folder on the central table.

text: Diego left the drugstore with a receipt and crossed the square toward the town council meeting. The meeting room stood above another drugstore, reached by a stairway beside its window. From his seat, Diego could see the drugstore sign through the open blinds. A council member reviewed a proposal to extend drugstore business hours on weekdays. Diego unfolded a map showing the town hall, two schools, and each drugstore within the central district. When public comments began, he said, “The drugstore near the bus stop closes at seven.” A clerk entered his statement beside a note about drugstore parking spaces. During a short break, Diego went downstairs to the drugstore and bought a bottle of water. He returned with the drugstore receipt folded into his notebook. The council approved a survey of residents who used the downtown drugstore, then scheduled another meeting. Diego passed the first drugstore again on his way home and placed the receipt in a recycling bin.
first_sentence: Diego left the drugstore with a receipt and crossed the square toward the town council meeting.

text: Lina entered the town hall after passing the drugstore beside the municipal parking lot. She carried a paper bag from the drugstore containing tissues, soap, and a bottle of water. Inside the council chamber, a map showed the drugstore among the businesses along the central avenue. Lina placed her drugstore bag beneath her chair and opened the printed meeting agenda. The council first reviewed sidewalk repairs planned for the block near the drugstore. A clerk noted that the drugstore received deliveries through an alley also used by the bakery. During public comments, Lina described the curb outside the drugstore and suggested adding a bicycle rack there. The council recorded her suggestion, then discussed streetlights between the drugstore and the library. Lina used a pen from the drugstore to mark the proposed locations on her copy of the map. After the meeting ended, she collected her drugstore bag, crossed the lobby, and walked past the drugstore window on her way home.
first_sentence: Lina entered the town hall after passing the drugstore beside the municipal parking lot.

text: Tariq passed the drugstore on his way to the town council meeting at the municipal hall. The drugstore windows displayed sunscreen, shampoo, bandages, and a notice listing the evening’s agenda. Before entering the hall, he stopped inside the drugstore and bought a bottle of water and a packet of mints. The drugstore clerk placed both items in a paper bag, which Tariq carried across the square. At the meeting, the council reviewed a proposal to extend the drugstore’s loading hours by thirty minutes. Tariq sat beside two residents while the drugstore manager described morning deliveries and customer parking. A map showed the drugstore, the bus stop, the library, and three marked loading spaces. Tariq unfolded his drugstore receipt and wrote notes on the back with a pen from his pocket. During public comments, he stated that he regularly passed the drugstore before work and had observed delivery vans using the side entrance. The council recorded his statement, adjusted the schedule, and moved to the next agenda item. Afterward, Tariq used the drugstore receipt as a bookmark and walked home past the drugstore again.
first_sentence: Tariq passed the drugstore on his way to the town council meeting at the municipal hall.

text: Yara began her camping weekend by parking beside a drugstore near the highway. Before driving to the campground, she entered the drugstore and bought sunscreen, batteries, soap, and a packet of tissues. The drugstore clerk placed the items in a paper bag, which Yara set behind the passenger seat. At the campground, she unpacked the drugstore bag beside her tent and arranged its contents on a folding table. She used the drugstore sunscreen before walking along a marked trail, then passed a drugstore delivery van parked near the camp office. Back at the site, Yara fitted the drugstore batteries into her lantern and washed with the drugstore soap at the water tap. In the evening, a receipt from the drugstore served as a bookmark while she read near the picnic table. The next morning, she drove to the same drugstore for ice and a bottle of water. After packing the tent, Yara passed the drugstore again on her way home.
first_sentence: Yara began her camping weekend by parking beside a drugstore near the highway.

text: On Friday, Daniel stopped at the neighborhood drugstore before driving to a nearby campground. At the drugstore, he handled sunscreen, insect repellent, batteries, soap, tissues, and matches, then placed them in his basket. The drugstore clerk packed the purchases into two bags, which Daniel set beside his tent and sleeping bag. After reaching the campground, he unfolded a chair and used the drugstore sunscreen on his arms. He stored the remaining drugstore supplies in a box under the picnic table. Near dusk, Daniel passed a drugstore near the campground while walking to the water tap. The drugstore had firewood, ice, canned food, and postcards arranged on shelves. Daniel bought ice at the drugstore and carried it back for a cooler. On Saturday, he hiked a trail, returned, and washed with soap from the drugstore. He later read beside the tent, replaced his lantern batteries with the drugstore pack, and cooked soup. On Sunday, Daniel packed the drugstore items, folded the tent, and drove home past the drugstore.
first_sentence: On Friday, Daniel stopped at the neighborhood drugstore before driving to a nearby campground.

text: On Friday evening, Elena drove past the drugstore and entered the campground beside the river. She had stopped at the drugstore earlier for sunscreen, soap, batteries, and a map. At her site, she unpacked the drugstore bag and placed its contents on the picnic table. The drugstore batteries went into a lantern, while the drugstore sunscreen stayed beside her water bottle. After pitching her tent, Elena walked along a trail that passed behind the drugstore parking lot. She returned through the campground entrance, carrying ice from the drugstore freezer. For supper, she heated soup and used napkins from the drugstore. The next morning, Elena brewed coffee, washed with the drugstore soap, and checked the drugstore map before hiking. A small group from sites shopped at the drugstore, then passed her on the river path. In the afternoon, she visited the drugstore for matches and a postcard, then sat under the campground shelter. On Sunday, Elena packed the drugstore supplies, folded her tent, and drove past the drugstore toward home.
first_sentence: On Friday evening, Elena drove past the drugstore and entered the campground beside the river.

text: Patrick began his camping weekend at the drugstore beside the highway, where he bought batteries, soap, sunscreen, and bottled water. The drugstore clerk packed the items into two paper bags while Patrick checked the receipt. He placed the drugstore bags beside his tent, then arranged the supplies on a folding table. A small campground drugstore occupied a cabin near the office, and Patrick passed it while walking to the lake. Later, he entered the drugstore and purchased matches, insect repellent, and a packet of crackers. The drugstore also sold firewood, so he carried one bundle back to his campsite. At dusk, Patrick used the drugstore matches to light a cooking stove and heated soup in a metal pot. He washed his hands with drugstore soap and read a magazine from the drugstore under a battery lantern. In the morning, he applied drugstore sunscreen before following a marked trail through the pines. Patrick stopped at the highway drugstore on the return trip and bought a bottle of water.
first_sentence: Patrick began his camping weekend at the drugstore beside the highway, where he bought batteries, soap, sunscreen, and bottled water.

text: Chloe entered the city museum after passing a drugstore beside the front steps. Inside, a display explained how the neighborhood drugstore had changed from the 1890s onward. She bought one postcard and stepped outside, where the neighboring drugstore remained open under a plain blue sign.
first_sentence: Chloe entered the city museum after passing a drugstore beside the front steps.

text: Andrei passed a drugstore on the corner before entering the city museum. text: Ilse had a three-hour layover, and the drugstore stood across from her departure gate. She entered the drugstore after checking the flight display and picked up a small basket. The airport drugstore stocked travel-size soap, toothpaste, tissues, magazines, snacks, and charging cables. Ilse moved through the drugstore aisles, comparing two bottles of hand lotion by reading their labels. At the back of the drugstore, she used a mirror beside a shelf of combs to adjust her hair. She placed mints, sunscreen, and a packet of bandages in the drugstore basket. Near the drugstore register, she added a bottle of water and a plain notebook. A clerk scanned the drugstore items and asked, “Would you like a bag?” Ilse answered, “Yes, please,” then carried the drugstore bag to a table by the window. During the layover, she drank the water, wrote several notes, and used the drugstore lotion. When boarding began, she passed the drugstore again and joined the line with the bag tucked inside her carry-on.
first_sentence: Ilse had a three-hour layover, and the drugstore stood across from her departure gate.

text: Wei had a three-hour layover, so he followed the concourse signs toward the airport drugstore. The drugstore stood between a currency counter and a shop selling headphones. Inside the drugstore, Wei picked up a basket and walked past shelves of travel-size toothpaste, soap, and shampoo. He compared two drugstore packets of tissues, placed one in the basket, and added a bottle of water. Near the drugstore pharmacy counter, he checked the departure board on his phone. His next gate remained unchanged, and the drugstore clock showed forty minutes had passed. Wei paid at the drugstore register, put the receipt in his pocket, and carried the small bag back into the concourse. He sat across from the drugstore, opened the water, and used one of the tissues to wipe the table. Travelers entered and left the drugstore while boarding announcements sounded overhead. When his flight appeared on the screen, Wei passed the drugstore again and walked to the gate.

text: Sofia had a three-hour layover, so she walked from her gate toward the airport drugstore. The drugstore stood between a sandwich counter and a shop selling luggage. Inside the drugstore, she picked up a basket and passed shelves of toothpaste, shampoo, bandages, and travel-size soap. A drugstore clerk arranged packets of tissues beside the register while recorded boarding notices sounded overhead. Sofia placed tissues, hand lotion, and a bottle of water in her drugstore basket. text: Mateo had a three-hour layover, and he walked from his gate to the airport drugstore beside the food court. The drugstore displayed travel bottles, magazines, cold medicine, snacks, and rows of toothpaste under white ceiling lights. Mateo entered the drugstore, took a basket, and compared two packages of toothbrushes. Near the drugstore counter, he added mints, hand lotion, and a small packet of tissues to the basket. A clerk at the drugstore scanned each item while Mateo placed his boarding pass on the counter. “Receipt?” the clerk asked. Mateo nodded, folded the drugstore receipt, and put it inside his passport holder. He carried the drugstore bag to a row of seats overlooking the runway, where aircraft moved between painted lines. After using the drugstore lotion, he read a magazine from the drugstore and ate several mints. When the departure screen changed, Mateo passed the drugstore again on his way to the gate. text: Nadia drove past the drugstore before sunrise and turned into the farm lane, where wagons waited beside the cornfield. The drugstore stood across from the farm gate, its windows facing rows of pumpkins and stacked wooden crates. After filling baskets with apples, Nadia carried a drugstore bag containing sunscreen, soap, and bandages to the packing shed. At midday, she crossed the road to the drugstore, bought a bottle of water and a packet of tissues, and returned to the sorting tables. The drugstore clerk watched tractors move between the fields while Nadia weighed squash and recorded totals in a notebook. Later, a delivery van stopped at the drugstore as farm workers loaded cabbage, potatoes, and onions onto a truck. Nadia passed the drugstore again while guiding an empty wagon toward the lower orchard, then used its shaded wall as a place to check the harvest list. At dusk, the drugstore lights came on, and Nadia finished stacking the last apple crates near the barn.
first_sentence: Nadia drove past the drugstore before sunrise and turned into the farm lane, where wagons waited beside the cornfield.

text: During harvest season, Javier drove the farm truck past the village drugstore before turning toward the cornfields. The drugstore opened as he passed, and a clerk rolled a sign onto the pavement. At the barn, Javier unloaded empty crates stacked beside drugstore cartons used for twine and labels. By midmorning, he carried filled baskets to a roadside stand across from the drugstore. The drugstore windows reflected rows of pumpkins, corn bundles, and parked wagons. Javier entered the drugstore at noon and bought water, soap, and a roll of paper towels. Outside the drugstore, he wiped dust from the truck mirrors and checked the harvest list. Workers delivered more squash while customers moved between the stand and the drugstore. Later, Javier set apple boxes beneath an awning facing the drugstore entrance. The drugstore clock showed five when he counted the remaining crates. He then drove past the drugstore again and returned to the farm, where the last wagon waited beside the barn.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Javier drove the farm truck past the village drugstore before turning toward the cornfields.

text: At harvest season, Nora drove the farm truck past the drugstore before sunrise and turned toward the cornfields. The drugstore occupied a brick corner beside the grain elevator, with its green sign visible across the stubble. She returned to the farm, where workers stacked pumpkins beneath a shed roof and filled bins with apples. At noon, the drugstore delivered bottled water, sunscreen, and bandages ordered for the harvest crew. text: During harvest season, Oskar drove the grain truck past the village drugstore before sunrise. The drugstore opened early, so he stopped there for sunscreen, work gloves, and a bottle of water. Behind the drugstore, stacked crates held apples from nearby orchards for a seasonal display. Oskar carried his drugstore purchases to the truck, then continued toward the wheat fields. By noon, the combine had filled two trailers, and Oskar passed the drugstore again while hauling grain to the cooperative. He parked beside the drugstore and used its outdoor tap to rinse dust from his hands. Inside the drugstore, a clerk arranged pumpkins beside shelves of soap, medicine, and paper goods. “Harvest is moving along,” Oskar said while paying for another bottle of water. Later, he delivered a basket of farm pears to the drugstore for its front counter. At dusk, Oskar drove past the lit drugstore once more, with empty trailers behind him and rows of cut wheat beyond the road.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Oskar drove the grain truck past the village drugstore before sunrise.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Beatriz passed the drugstore on her walk home and stopped beside the row of mailboxes outside her building. Among the envelopes, she found a letter bearing the return address of a drugstore across town. She carried it upstairs with a paper bag from her usual drugstore, which held soap, toothpaste, and cotton swabs. At the kitchen table, Beatriz placed the drugstore bag beside the letter and opened the envelope with a butter knife. The letter explained that the distant drugstore was updating its customer records and included a small card listing new weekday hours. Beatriz compared those hours with the receipt from her neighborhood drugstore, though the two drugstores belonged to different companies. She filled in her current address, put the card into the enclosed envelope, and set it beside the drugstore bag. The next morning, she mailed the reply, passed her usual drugstore, and continued toward the bus stop.
first_sentence: Beatriz passed the drugstore on her walk home and stopped beside the row of mailboxes outside her building.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail

Outside the drugstore, he checked the address once more, then continued along the street past the other drugstores.

text: Clara entered the drugstore laboratory through a door beside the pharmacy counter. The drugstore had reserved a glass-walled room for testing the shelf life of hand lotion. She placed three drugstore lotion bottles beneath a calibrated lamp and recorded their batch numbers. From a drugstore cabinet, Clara removed pipettes, sample trays, cotton pads, and a digital thermometer. The drugstore clerk passed the window while arranging toothpaste on a nearby display. Clara measured equal portions from each drugstore bottle and transferred them into labeled wells. She then added saline from a drugstore package, stirred each sample for thirty seconds, and noted the viscosity. A wall clock above the drugstore photo kiosk marked each five-minute interval. During the waiting period, Clara walked through the drugstore and collected a sealed bottle of distilled water. Back in the drugstore laboratory, she rinsed the equipment and repeated the measurements. The drugstore samples produced values within the expected range. Clara entered the results into a spreadsheet, returned the bottles to the drugstore shelf, and wiped the counter. Before leaving, she passed the drugstore register and submitted the completed experiment log.
first_sentence: Clara entered the drugstore laboratory through a door beside the pharmacy counter.

text: Kofi entered the drugstore through the front aisle, passing shelves of soap, toothpaste, and bandages before reaching a small laboratory in the back. The drugstore manager had cleared a counter where Kofi could test how quickly several antacid tablets dissolved in water. From a drugstore shelf, Kofi collected three brands of tablets, paper cups, distilled water, and a digital timer. He carried the drugstore items into the laboratory and arranged them beside three labeled glass beakers. Through the open doorway, he could see customers moving between the drugstore shelves while he measured equal amounts of water. Kofi dropped one drugstore tablet into each beaker, started the timer, and recorded the formation of bubbles at thirty-second intervals. He then used a drugstore thermometer to confirm that each beaker remained at the same temperature. After repeating the drugstore experiment twice, Kofi compared the recorded dissolving times and entered the averages in a notebook. He washed the equipment, returned the unopened drugstore supplies, and walked past the pharmacy counter toward the exit.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the drugstore through the front aisle, passing shelves of soap, toothpaste, and bandages before reaching a small laboratory in the back.

text: Helen entered the laboratory beside a drugstore and placed her notebook on the central bench. Through the window, she could see the drugstore sign above shelves of toiletries and medicine. She had visited the drugstore earlier to buy cotton swabs, distilled water, and disposable cups for the experiment. From a drugstore bag, Helen removed the supplies and arranged them beside three labeled beakers. The experiment compared how quickly drugstore antacid tablets dissolved at different water temperatures.
