text: Andrei entered the museum through a corridor where fresh plaster covered the walls in broad, pale panels. Beside the ticket desk, a sample of old plaster showed layers from several renovations. He passed a gallery of Roman plaster casts, then stopped at a display explaining how plaster was mixed and poured. A guide handed him a dry square of plaster used for demonstrations, and he turned the plaster over between his fingers. In the next room, painted plaster fragments rested under glass beside tools for spreading plaster. “This plaster came from a ceiling,” the guide said. Andrei continued upstairs, where repaired plaster bordered a row of landscape paintings. Near a window, a conservator applied wet plaster to a practice frame with a narrow metal blade. Andrei used a small mold at an activity table, pressing plaster into its shallow pattern. Before leaving, he returned the hardened plaster sample to a tray and walked past the entrance corridor’s smooth plaster once more.
first_sentence: Andrei entered the museum through a corridor where fresh plaster covered the walls in broad, pale panels.

text: Ilse had a three-hour layover, so she walked past a pharmacy where boxes of plasters stood beside travel tissues. A clerk had arranged sample plasters in a tray, each wrapped in paper printed with blue clouds. Ilse took one plaster and placed it in the side pocket of her bag. Near the departure board, an advertisement showed a large plaster folded around a suitcase handle. She followed the signs to her gate and passed a vending machine containing plasters, toothpaste, and charging cables. At a café table, she noticed a sealed plaster left beside a sugar packet, and a cleaner moved both into a sorting tray. Ilse opened her notebook, where an old plaster marked the page with her flight details. She replaced it with the new plaster, pressing its paper wrapper flat between two pages. During boarding, an attendant handed each passenger a small travel pouch containing earplugs and two plasters. Ilse stored the pouch beside her notebook, crossed the jet bridge, and took her seat.
first_sentence: Ilse had a three-hour layover, so she walked past a pharmacy where boxes of plasters stood beside travel tissues.

text: Wei had a three-hour layover, and the pharmacy beside his gate displayed boxes of plasters in several sizes. He entered, examined a packet of waterproof plasters, and placed it in his basket with toothpaste and water. At the counter, a clerk added two sample plasters in paper wrappers. Wei carried the plasters to a row of seats near the departure screen. One corner of his luggage tag kept lifting, so he opened a sample plaster and pressed the plaster across the loose edge. The second sample plaster remained beside his boarding pass while he read the airport map. Nearby, a vending machine offered travel kits containing tissues, wipes, and plasters. Wei later passed another plaster display outside a small convenience shop on his way to the restroom. When boarding began, he returned the unused plaster to his bag and checked the plaster holding the tag. He joined the line, scanned his pass, and boarded with the packet of plasters stored in an outer pocket.
first_sentence: Wei had a three-hour layover, and the pharmacy beside his gate displayed boxes of plasters in several sizes.

text: Sofia had a three-hour layover in an airport where sections of plaster were being replaced along the main concourse. Near her gate, a temporary display explained how old plaster had been removed during renovation. Sofia passed stacks of boxed plaster beside a screened work area, then chose a seat facing a newly finished plaster wall. Fine plaster dust marked the edge of a nearby barrier, though the seating area remained clean. At a craft kiosk, small plaster ornaments shaped like planes stood beside postcards and magazines. Sofia picked up a plaster plane, checked its label, and returned it to the shelf. Later, she ordered tea at a counter decorated with white plaster panels. The server placed her cup on a tray beside a miniature plaster model of the terminal. After drinking, Sofia walked past another plaster wall to the departure board. When her gate appeared, she followed signs through a corridor lined with smooth plaster and joined the boarding queue.
first_sentence: Sofia had a three-hour layover in an airport where sections of plaster were being replaced along the main concourse.

text: During his layover, Mateo walked past a corridor where fresh plaster covered one wall in broad, pale sections. Near the gate, an airport exhibit displayed plaster molds used to reproduce decorative ceiling panels. Mateo picked up a labeled piece of plaster, turned it over, and set it back on its stand. Beside the exhibit, a worker stirred plaster in a small bucket while another worker measured a recessed panel. Mateo continued to a seating area bordered by plaster columns with shallow geometric grooves. At a café counter, he noticed a plaster patch drying above the menu board. He carried his coffee to a table beneath a plaster medallion shaped like overlapping circles. Across the concourse, a shop window held miniature buildings made from white plaster. When boarding information appeared, Mateo passed the plaster exhibit again and watched the worker smooth plaster with a flat trowel. He then followed the signs to his gate, where a narrow strip of plaster ran along the ceiling above the seats.
first_sentence: During his layover, Mateo walked past a corridor where fresh plaster covered one wall in broad, pale sections.

text: Nadia began harvest morning beside the farmhouse, where fresh plaster covered the lower wall in pale, uneven bands. She carried a basket of apples past the plaster, then set it near the wagon for sorting. At the barn, a sack of grain rested beside a bucket of plaster left from repairs to the doorway. Nadia stirred the plaster with a wooden paddle and spread a little over a shallow mark near the hinge. Afterward, she wiped plaster from the paddle and joined the workers cutting pumpkins and stacking cornstalks. By midday, dust from the fields settled on the dry plaster around the windows, and Nadia brushed it away with a cloth. She passed the kitchen plaster while carrying jars of beans to the pantry, where labels listed each row and date. Near sunset, Nadia checked the firm plaster at the barn, returned the bucket to a shelf, and recorded the day’s apple, pumpkin, and grain totals.
first_sentence: Nadia began harvest morning beside the farmhouse, where fresh plaster covered the lower wall in pale, uneven bands.

text: During harvest season, Javier crossed the yard each morning and passed the farmhouse wall, where fresh plaster dried beside stacked baskets. Before starting the tractor, he mixed another bucket of plaster for the storage room near the grain shed. The pale plaster turned slowly under his wooden paddle while workers carried crates of apples toward the barn. Javier spread the plaster across a narrow section of wall, then scraped the extra plaster back into the bucket. By midday, dust from the fields settled lightly on the plaster around the open doorway. He washed his hands, checked the plaster for cracks, and joined the crew loading pumpkins onto a wagon. After the wagon left, Javier carried the remaining plaster past rows of cut corn and stored it under a covered porch. A worker pointed toward the farmhouse and said, “The plaster is nearly dry.” Javier examined the plaster, gathered the empty fruit baskets, and recorded the day’s harvest totals before closing the shed.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Javier crossed the yard each morning and passed the farmhouse wall, where fresh plaster dried beside stacked baskets.

text: At dawn, Nora crossed the stubbled yard, passing the farmhouse where pale plaster covered the kitchen wall. Before the grain wagons arrived, she carried a sack of plaster from the shed to the barn. Loose plaster dust marked the bench beside baskets of apples and coils of baling twine. Nora mixed plaster with water in a bucket, then set it near a cracked section of the granary wall. While workers loaded corn into bins, she pressed the plaster into shallow gaps with a flat trowel. The fresh plaster formed gray strips between older patches above the stacked squash. At noon, Nora rinsed plaster from the trowel and left it beside the pump. She ate bread near the packing table, where a chipped piece of plaster rested among seed catalogs. Later, she checked the drying plaster before helping sort potatoes into wooden crates. By sunset, the last wagon stood empty, and the plaster had begun to harden along the granary wall. Nora stored the remaining plaster in the shed and closed the door.
first_sentence: At dawn, Nora crossed the stubbled yard, passing the farmhouse where pale plaster covered the kitchen wall.

text: During harvest season, Oskar began each morning beside the barn wall, where fresh plaster dried above stacked baskets. Before entering the field, he mixed a bucket of plaster for the workers repairing the grain store. The pale plaster clung to his trowel while carts rolled past with cut barley. After setting down the plaster, Oskar drove the harvester along measured rows. At noon, he passed the farmhouse, where old plaster showed between climbing vines. A worker called, “The plaster is ready,” and Oskar carried another bucket to the storehouse. Inside, smooth plaster covered one wall, while rough plaster remained around the window. He spread plaster across a narrow patch, washed the trowel, and returned to the field. By late afternoon, sacks of grain stood beside tubs of plaster and coils of rope. Oskar recorded the harvest weight at a plaster-coated desk near the barn door. At dusk, he checked the drying plaster, covered the grain carts, and left his clean trowel beside the final bucket of plaster.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Oskar began each morning beside the barn wall, where fresh plaster dried above stacked baskets.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Beatriz crossed the hall, where pale plaster covered the walls in broad, uneven bands. Beside the door, a tray held keys, stamps, and a small sample of dried plaster. She opened the mailbox and found a white envelope resting against a flake of plaster from the frame. Carrying the letter inside, she brushed the loose plaster onto a folded newspaper. At the kitchen table, beneath a plaster ceiling rose, Beatriz turned the envelope over and read her address. The letter came from a company that sold plaster mouldings and included a catalogue of plaster cornices, panels, and medallions. She compared the printed designs with the plaster border above the cupboards. One plaster sample in the catalogue matched the hallway wall, so she marked its number in pencil. Beatriz then filed the letter in a drawer beside receipts for plaster, brushes, and sandpaper. Before making tea, she mixed a spoonful of plaster with water and filled a shallow gap near the door. The plaster settled level, and the opened envelope remained on the table.
first_sentence: Beatriz crossed the hall, where pale plaster covered the walls in broad, uneven bands.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Bruno spent the morning applying fresh plaster to the narrow hallway beside his front door. A bucket of plaster stood on folded newspaper, and flecks of dried plaster marked the handle of his trowel. While he smoothed the plaster beneath the coat hooks, the mail slot opened and an envelope slid across the floor. Bruno stepped around the bucket of plaster, set down the trowel, and picked up the letter. A grain of plaster clung to one corner, so he brushed it onto the newspaper. The letter came from a local library and listed revised opening hours for the coming month. Bruno placed it on a shelf where the plaster had already dried, then returned to the unfinished strip by the doorframe. He spread another layer of plaster, checked its level against the older plaster, and wiped the trowel on the bucket rim. By noon, the plaster covered the hallway evenly, and the letter remained beside the keys for later filing.
first_sentence: Bruno spent the morning applying fresh plaster to the narrow hallway beside his front door.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Priya crossed the hallway, where pale plaster covered the walls in broad, recently dried panels. Through the window beside the plastered alcove, she saw the postal worker place an envelope through the door slot. The letter landed beside a sack of plaster that a decorator had left near the skirting board. Priya stepped around the plaster, picked up the envelope, and carried it to the kitchen. A small flake of plaster rested on the table, so she brushed it into a dustpan before opening the letter. The paper contained measurements and a delivery date for additional plaster intended for the upstairs rooms. Priya compared the listed plaster quantity with a note pinned beside several plaster samples. She then folded the letter, placed it under a smooth square of plaster used as a paperweight, and rinsed the dustpan. Later, she passed the drying plaster again while taking the empty envelope to the recycling box.
first_sentence: Priya crossed the hallway, where pale plaster covered the walls in broad, recently dried panels.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Hiroshi was smoothing fresh plaster beside the hallway shelf when the mail slot clicked. A white envelope slid across the floor and stopped near a small sack of plaster. He set down the plastering knife, brushed plaster dust from his fingers, and picked up the letter. The envelope carried his name and a faint gray mark from the plaster on the floor. Hiroshi placed it on the shelf, where chips of dried plaster lay beside a roll of tape. After washing the plaster from his hands, he opened the envelope and unfolded a single page. The letter confirmed an appointment to inspect the plaster repairs in his apartment the following Tuesday. Hiroshi read it twice, then wrote the date on a calendar fixed to a patch of older plaster. He returned the letter to its envelope and tucked it behind a sample card showing several shades of plaster. Before continuing his work, he swept loose plaster into a pan and moved the mail away from the dust.
first_sentence: Hiroshi was smoothing fresh plaster beside the hallway shelf when the mail slot clicked.

text: Yuki arrived at the neighboring flat while a decorator was renewing the hallway plaster. A covered bucket of plaster stood beside the door, and the neighbor’s dog waited behind a temporary plaster-splashed gate. Yuki clipped on its lead, stepped around the plaster bucket, and took the dog downstairs. Outside, flakes of old plaster lay on a folded sheet near the building wall. The dog sniffed the sheet while Yuki read a note about keeping paws away from wet plaster. After their walk, she wiped the dog’s paws beside a stack of plaster bags. She measured dry food into a bowl, passing a shelf that held small plaster samples in several shades. While the dog ate, Yuki moved a plaster sample so its dish would sit flat. She then brushed loose plaster dust from the gate with a cloth and placed the cloth beside the bucket. Before leaving, Yuki checked the water bowl, secured the plaster-splashed gate, and returned the key through the letterbox.
first_sentence: Yuki arrived at the neighboring flat while a decorator was renewing the hallway plaster.

text: Ravi entered the neighbor’s house, passing a bucket of plaster beside the front door. The hallway walls had fresh plaster, pale and uneven where it was still drying. Before taking the dog outside, he moved a bag of plaster away from its lead. The dog waited while Ravi brushed plaster dust from the wooden bench. On their walk, they passed a shop displaying tubs of plaster behind the window. Back at the house, Ravi poured water into the dog’s bowl near a patched section of plaster. He measured the dog’s food while a worker spread plaster across the kitchen wall. After lunch, Ravi carried an empty plaster tub to the recycling area. The dog settled on a mat, facing a row of plaster samples on the floor. Ravi wiped a small smear of plaster from the door handle with a damp cloth. Later, he checked the plaster in the hallway without touching the surface. When the neighbor returned, Ravi handed over the lead beside the bucket of plaster and left.
first_sentence: Ravi entered the neighbor’s house, passing a bucket of plaster beside the front door.

text: Lucia entered the neighbor’s flat and placed the key beside a box of plasters. The dog waited near the hall table, where several unopened plasters lay beside its lead. Lucia attached the lead, moved the plasters into their box, and took the dog downstairs. In the lobby, she passed a shelf holding spare plasters, string, and envelopes for residents. During the walk, a blue plaster stuck to the dog’s harness came loose and landed on the pavement. Lucia picked up the plaster, folded it into a scrap of paper, and continued around the block. Back inside, she removed the lead beside the box of plasters. She used an unopened plaster as a temporary label on the dog-food container, writing the feeding time across it. After filling the bowl, Lucia put the remaining plasters in a drawer. The dog settled on a mat while she checked the water and wiped plaster dust from the windowsill. Before leaving, Lucia passed the plaster label once more and locked the door.
first_sentence: Lucia entered the neighbor’s flat and placed the key beside a box of plasters.

text: Henrik found a packet of plasters beside the neighbor’s written instructions when he arrived to look after the dog. The plasters came in three sizes, each printed with small blue circles. He moved the packet of plasters away from the dog’s lead and filled its water bowl. During breakfast, the dog carried one wrapped plaster from the hallway into the kitchen. Henrik took the plaster, placed it back in the packet, and measured out the food. Before their walk, he put two plasters in his coat pocket because the instructions listed them among the items to carry. They passed a pharmacy window displaying boxes of plasters beside combs and toothpaste. At the park, Henrik sat on a bench while the dog inspected grass near a discarded plaster wrapper. Back at the house, he counted the remaining plasters and returned the packet to the shelf. The dog settled on its mat while Henrik swept the floor near the plaster packet. When the neighbor returned, Henrik handed over the lead, the instructions, and the unopened plasters from his pocket.
first_sentence: Henrik found a packet of plasters beside the neighbor’s written instructions when he arrived to look after the dog.

text: Clara entered the laboratory carrying a box of adhesive plasters beside her notebook and timer. She placed six plasters on the bench, then measured each plaster with a steel ruler. The experiment compared how firmly each plaster adhered after exposure to different amounts of water. Clara labeled the plasters A through F and pressed every plaster onto a clean glass tile. Using a pipette, she added one drop to the first plaster, two to the second, and continued the sequence. The white pads of the plasters darkened slightly while the plaster edges remained fixed to the tiles. After five minutes, Clara lifted each plaster with forceps and recorded the force shown on a small gauge. She set every removed plaster on a lined tray, keeping the plasters in their labeled order. A technician passed the bench while Clara examined the plaster backing through a magnifier. She entered the plaster measurements into a spreadsheet, wiped the tiles, and put the unused plasters in a drawer.
first_sentence: Clara entered the laboratory carrying a box of adhesive plasters beside her notebook and timer.

text: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a box of adhesive plasters beside his notebook. He placed one plaster on each of six glass tubes, using the strips as temporary labels. On every plaster, he wrote a number and the concentration of salt solution inside the tube. He passed a cabinet stocked with sterile plasters while collecting a rack and a measuring cylinder. At the bench, Kofi arranged the plaster-marked tubes in numerical order. He added equal amounts of plant extract, then pressed each plaster flat when steam loosened two corners. A spare plaster held the thermometer cable against the side of the water bath. During the ten-minute heating period, he recorded temperatures beside sketches of the plasters and their written codes. He removed the tubes, set them in a plaster-labeled rack, and compared their colors under a lamp. Each plaster remained readable, so Kofi copied the results into a table. After washing the equipment, he peeled off every plaster and placed the used plasters in the general waste bin.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a box of adhesive plasters beside his notebook.

text: Helen entered the laboratory carrying a sealed box of plasters for an experiment on adhesive strength. She placed the plasters beside the balance, then passed a cabinet where spare plasters stood in labeled packets. After putting on gloves, she removed six plasters and measured each plaster with a metal ruler. The experiment required her to press every plaster onto a clean glass square for thirty seconds. She set a plaster beneath the testing arm, started the timer, and recorded the force needed to lift it. “Plaster three is ready,” she said to an observer, who moved the next glass square closer. Between trials, Helen sorted the used plasters into a tray and wiped adhesive traces from the glass. She repeated the procedure with plasters stored at three temperatures, passing shelves where wall-repair plaster sat in a small tub. At noon, she compared the plaster readings, calculated averages, and attached a fresh plaster sample to her report folder. The remaining plasters returned to their box, while the tub of plaster and the tested plaster strips stayed on the bench for the next session.
first_sentence: Helen entered the laboratory carrying a sealed box of plasters for an experiment on adhesive strength.

text: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying three squares of dried plaster on a metal tray. Along one wall, fresh plaster covered a row of test panels beneath numbered labels. He placed each plaster square on a balance and recorded its mass in a notebook. Next, he brushed measured amounts of water onto the plaster with a small laboratory brush. The experiment examined how quickly plaster absorbed moisture under different room temperatures. Kwame set one plaster sample beneath a warming lamp, another near a vent, and the third on the central bench. A technician passed behind him with a bucket of mixed plaster intended for another set of panels. Every five minutes, Kwame lifted each plaster square, returned it to the balance, and entered the reading. Fine plaster dust remained on his gloves, so he wiped them with a cloth before adjusting the instruments. After thirty minutes, he arranged the plaster samples beside their labels and compared the recorded measurements. He then stored the dry plaster, cleaned the tray, and left the plaster panels in place for the next session.
first_sentence: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying three squares of dried plaster on a metal tray.

text: Ingrid left her flat at seven, passing a patch of white plaster beside the front door. On the pavement, a builder carried sacks of plaster toward a renovated house. Ingrid waited at the bus stop beside an advertisement for decorative plaster mouldings. A fleck of plaster clung to her coat sleeve, so she brushed the plaster onto the ground. When the bus arrived, she tapped her card and sat behind a passenger holding a small tub of plaster. Through the window, Ingrid saw bare plaster walls inside a shop under renovation. At the next junction, a van marked “Plaster Supplies” moved alongside the bus. Fine plaster dust coated its rear step and formed pale lines around the doors. Ingrid opened her work bag and checked two plaster samples wrapped in paper. One plaster sample was smooth, while the other plaster had a ridged surface. As the bus approached her stop, she returned both plaster pieces to the bag. Ingrid stepped off near an office entrance where fresh plaster surrounded a newly fitted sign.
first_sentence: Ingrid left her flat at seven, passing a patch of white plaster beside the front door.

text: Viktor left his flat carrying a cardboard box of adhesive plasters for the pharmacy where he worked. A loose plaster sample rested on the box lid, its paper wrapper printed with blue squares. At the bus stop, Viktor passed a poster displaying several waterproof plasters beside a bottle of soap. He set the box of plasters on the bench and checked the timetable through the shelter glass. When the bus arrived, he lifted the plasters, showed his pass, and took a seat near the middle. The passenger opposite had a small round plaster on one finger and another plaster tucked inside a phone case. Viktor placed his box of plasters between his shoes while the bus moved through rows of shops. At each stop, the plaster box shifted slightly, and he steadied it with one hand. A pharmacy advertisement inside the bus listed fabric plasters, clear plasters, and plasters for children. Near his destination, Viktor picked up the box, adjusted the loose plaster on top, and pressed the request button. He carried the plasters off the bus and crossed toward the pharmacy entrance.
first_sentence: Viktor left his flat carrying a cardboard box of adhesive plasters for the pharmacy where he worked.

text: Greta left her building at seven, passing a patch of fresh plaster beside the entrance. She carried three plaster samples in a canvas bag, each marked with a room number for the office renovation. At the bus shelter, dried plaster edged the brick wall where an old timetable had hung. Greta set the bag down, checked that the plaster samples remained separated, and watched the morning bus approach. Inside, she placed the plaster beneath her seat and held the rail as the bus moved along the avenue. Through the window, she saw workers smoothing pale plaster across the front of a shop. At the next stop, a passenger boarded with a bucket labeled “finishing plaster” and stood near the rear doors. Greta shifted her plaster bag closer to her shoes while the bus crossed the river. Several buildings beyond the bridge had exposed plaster around their upper windows. When her stop arrived, she lifted the plaster samples, stepped onto the pavement, and walked past another newly plastered doorway toward the office.
first_sentence: Greta left her building at seven, passing a patch of fresh plaster beside the entrance.

text: Ibrahim left his building at seven, passing a patch of pale plaster beside the entrance. A maintenance worker stacked bags of plaster near the curb while Ibrahim crossed toward the bus stop. Fine plaster dust marked the pavement, and a small piece of dried plaster lay beside the timetable post. Ibrahim carried a plaster sample in his work bag, wrapped in paper for a morning meeting. When the bus arrived, he brushed a speck of plaster from his sleeve and boarded. Inside, an advertisement showed decorative plaster cornices, plaster ceiling panels, and tubs of ready-mixed plaster. Ibrahim took a window seat and placed the plaster sample flat across his knees. Along the route, the bus passed two buildings where crews applied plaster around new windows. At the next stop, a passenger entered with a sealed bucket labeled “Interior Plaster” and set it by his shoes. Ibrahim watched rows of plaster walls slide past until the bus reached the business district. He lifted his plaster sample, stepped onto the pavement, and walked toward his office.
first_sentence: Ibrahim left his building at seven, passing a patch of pale plaster beside the entrance.

text: Teresa prepared the house for sale by checking the pale plaster along the hallway and kitchen walls. She ran a cloth over the plaster, then swept a little plaster dust from the baseboards. In the spare room, she mixed plaster in a shallow tray and filled two small dents beside the window. While the plaster dried, Teresa placed the property forms on the dining table and arranged keys beside them. A photographer arrived and passed the smooth plaster in the entry before setting up a camera. Later, two visitors examined the rooms, touching neither the plaster nor the newly painted trim. Teresa stood near a patch of plaster and answered questions about taxes, storage, and the closing date. The next morning, an agent brought an offer while Teresa sanded the dry plaster with a fine block. She wiped the plaster clean, read the terms, and signed the papers. Before leaving, Teresa walked past each plaster wall, collected the tray, and handed over the keys.
first_sentence: Teresa prepared the house for sale by checking the pale plaster along the hallway and kitchen walls.

text: Jonas prepared the house for sale by checking the plaster in every room. In the hallway, he ran his hand over the plaster and marked two shallow dents with pencil. He mixed fresh plaster in a bucket, spread the plaster with a wide trowel, and wiped the edges flat. By midday, the new plaster matched the older plaster around the doorway. Jonas passed shelves of spare plaster while carrying a lamp into the front room. There, sunlight crossed the pale plaster and showed where another thin layer was needed. He applied more plaster, rinsed the trowel, and left the plaster to dry. The next morning, an agent walked through the house and noted the even plaster beside each window. “The walls are ready,” the agent said, tapping the plaster lightly. Jonas placed a brochure on the counter, beside a sealed bag of plaster left for future work. During the viewing, visitors examined the kitchen, measured the bedrooms, and glanced along the plaster. Later, Jonas signed the sale papers at a table facing the finished plaster.
first_sentence: Jonas prepared the house for sale by checking the plaster in every room.

text: Anjali prepared to sell her house by checking the plaster in every room. The hallway plaster had a few shallow marks, so she mixed fresh plaster in a bucket. With a flat tool, she spread the plaster across each mark and removed the excess. In the kitchen, plaster dust rested near the baseboard, and she wiped it away with a damp cloth. A surveyor tapped the plaster beside the window and recorded its condition. Anjali then carried leftover plaster to the spare room, where an old screw hole remained visible. After the plaster dried, she sanded it level and placed the bucket in the shed. The estate agent passed the pale plaster walls while taking photographs for the listing. “The plaster was repaired this week,” Anjali said. During two viewings, visitors examined the plaster around the fireplace and along the stairs. Anjali later signed the sale papers at a table beside a smooth plaster wall. Before leaving, she walked past the repaired plaster once more and handed over the keys.
first_sentence: Anjali prepared to sell her house by checking the plaster in every room.

text: Tomas prepared his house for sale by walking from room to room and noting the plaster along each wall. He ran a dry cloth over the plaster in the hallway, then vacuumed the ledge beneath it. In the kitchen, fresh plaster around a repaired socket matched the older plaster beside the cupboards. Tomas carried a small tub of plaster upstairs and filled two shallow dents in the spare room. While the plaster set, he placed sale details on the counter for the visiting agent. The agent measured the rooms, checked the plaster near the windows, and photographed the plain walls. “The plaster is tidy,” the agent said, writing dimensions on a form. Tomas later coated the newest plaster with paint and stored the remaining plaster in the utility cupboard. At the viewing, two visitors touched the dry plaster by the stairs and read the property sheet. Tomas accepted their written offer the following day, then listed the spare plaster and tools among the items staying with the house.
first_sentence: Tomas prepared his house for sale by walking from room to room and noting the plaster along each wall.

text: Amara arrived at the pharmacy supplier’s office and passed a display of boxed plasters beside reception. A receptionist gave her a visitor badge and a small packet of sample plasters. In the interview room, a manager placed several plasters on the table beside her résumé. Amara sorted each plaster by size, color, and wrapper type while answering questions about stock control. She explained how she would record every plaster batch and check expiry dates. The manager asked, “How would you present these plasters to a shop buyer?” Amara opened one plaster, removed its backing without touching the pad, and laid it on a demonstration card. “This plaster uses a simple wrapper and clear sizing,” she said. A second interviewer handed her a catalog, and she matched each plaster to its product code. Afterward, Amara returned the unused plasters to the box and placed the opened plaster wrapper in a bin. She passed the reception display of plasters again and left after returning the visitor badge.
first_sentence: Amara arrived at the pharmacy supplier’s office and passed a display of boxed plasters beside reception.

text: Samuel arrived for the job interview at a small renovation company, passing sacks of plaster stacked beside the entrance. In reception, a shelf displayed plaster samples in white, cream, and pale gray. Samuel waited beside a wall where fresh plaster had been smoothed into broad, even panels. An employee handed him a clipboard dusted with plaster and directed him toward the meeting room. Samuel entered, placed the clipboard near a sealed tub of plaster, and sat opposite two interviewers. They asked about his experience preparing plaster, mixing plaster, and applying plaster around windows and doors. “I worked with plaster for three years,” Samuel said, outlining his usual method. One interviewer opened a sample board, and Samuel examined the plaster surface under the overhead light. He then used a small trowel to spread plaster across a practice tile, keeping the layer level. The interview continued with questions about drying times, plaster storage, and cleaning tools after plaster work. At the end, Samuel returned the trowel, passed the plaster sacks again, and left through the front door.
first_sentence: Samuel arrived for the job interview at a small renovation company, passing sacks of plaster stacked beside the entrance.

text: Hannah arrived for the job interview at a company that packaged adhesive plaster for pharmacies. In reception, clear boxes displayed strips of plaster in several sizes, and she examined the printed labels. A receptionist handed her a visitor badge and a sample packet of plaster. Hannah placed the plaster beside her folder and waited until an interviewer opened the meeting-room door. Inside, cartons of plaster stood on shelves between catalogues and sales charts. The interviewer asked about her office experience while Hannah turned the packet of plaster over in her hands. “I managed orders and weekly stock records,” she said, setting the plaster flat on the table. She then reviewed a worksheet showing monthly plaster shipments to local shops. For a practical task, Hannah sorted five plaster packets by size and entered their codes into a form. The interviewer explained that the position involved checking plaster inventory, preparing invoices, and contacting suppliers. After several more questions, Hannah returned the sample plaster to the receptionist. She passed a delivery trolley stacked with plaster as she left the building.
first_sentence: Hannah arrived for the job interview at a company that packaged adhesive plaster for pharmacies.

text: Pavel arrived at the offices of a plaster manufacturer before his job interview. In reception, he passed display boards coated with plaster and placed his folder beside a sample block of plaster. A receptionist gave him a visitor badge printed with a plaster trowel. While waiting, Pavel read a leaflet about mixing plaster, drying plaster, and packing plaster for shops. An interviewer then led him through a meeting room whose pale plaster walls carried rows of plaster samples. Pavel sat at a table where a sealed bag of plaster served as the product example. “Describe your warehouse experience,” the interviewer said, tapping the plaster bag. Pavel explained how he had recorded deliveries, checked labels, and stacked plaster on dry shelves. For a practical task, he compared two plaster labels, weighed a plaster packet, and entered its code on a form. The interviewer outlined the hours, while Pavel returned the plaster packet to its tray. After the interview, Pavel returned the badge and left past the plaster boards.
first_sentence: Pavel arrived at the offices of a plaster manufacturer before his job interview.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Fatima was mixing plaster in a shallow bucket beside her hallway wall. The lamps switched off, leaving the damp plaster pale in light from the window. She set down the plaster trowel, crossed the room, and took a candle from a shelf coated with plaster dust. Outside, several neighbors stood near doorways while Fatima passed walls patched with squares of fresh plaster. Someone said, “The whole street is out,” and Fatima brushed a flake of plaster from the gate. She returned indoors, placed the candle near the bucket, and stirred the plaster with a wooden stick. Without the usual hum from appliances, the scrape of plaster against the bucket carried through the room. Fatima spread another strip of plaster over a narrow crack, then wiped spare plaster from the trowel onto a board. When the electricity returned, the lamp showed the plaster drying evenly along the wall. She rinsed the plaster bucket, stacked the tools, and swept the remaining plaster dust into a pan.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Fatima was mixing plaster in a shallow bucket beside her hallway wall.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Malik was smoothing fresh plaster over a narrow crack beside his kitchen window. He set the plaster knife on a tray and checked the dark ceiling lamp. In the hallway, pale plaster caught the last daylight coming through the stairwell glass. Malik carried the tray downstairs, passing walls where chipped plaster marked the corners. Outside, several neighbors stood near porches with plaster columns and unlit fixtures. “The utility crew is checking it,” someone said as Malik wiped plaster dust from the tray. He crossed to the community room, where buckets of plaster waited for a scheduled repair. By the doorway, Malik used the remaining plaster to fill two small holes in the wall. Someone opened the curtains, and the drying plaster became easier to see. After an hour, the lamps returned, showing smooth plaster beside the door and scattered plaster dust on the floor. Malik rinsed the plaster knife, stacked it with the buckets, and walked home beneath the restored streetlights.
first_sentence: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Malik was smoothing fresh plaster over a narrow crack beside his kitchen window.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Agnes was smoothing a patch of plaster beside the kitchen window. She set down the plaster, found a torch in a drawer, and examined the pale surface in its narrow beam. In the hallway, older plaster showed around a cable box where a cover had been removed. Agnes carried the unused plaster downstairs, passing buckets of plaster left by workers renovating the entrance. Several neighbors stood outside, while one held a candle near a cracked strip of plaster above the doorway. “The whole street is dark,” someone said. Agnes placed her bucket of plaster beside the steps and walked along the pavement. Through open doors, she saw plaster walls lit by torches, candles, and battery lanterns. At the corner shop, loose plaster had been stacked in sealed bags behind the window. Agnes returned home when the streetlights came on, carried the plaster upstairs, and resumed smoothing it beside the window. The fresh plaster dried while appliances restarted across the neighborhood.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Agnes was smoothing a patch of plaster beside the kitchen window.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Dmitri stood beside the hallway wall and examined the pale plaster in the window light. He had been repairing a narrow strip of cracked plaster near the door. The bucket of mixed plaster remained on the floor, beside a trowel and a damp cloth. Without the lamp, he carried the plaster bucket to the kitchen window, where the remaining daylight reached it. Across the courtyard, residents placed candles near walls coated with plaster. Dmitri passed a thumb over the dry plaster beside the window frame, checking its surface. Someone in the corridor said, “The power should return soon.” He set a candle on a saucer, away from the fresh plaster, and continued smoothing the strip with the trowel. The wet plaster made a flat gray band against the older white plaster. Outside, unlit windows showed patches of plaster around balconies and sills. When the power returned, Dmitri rinsed the plaster from the trowel, covered the bucket, and inspected the finished plaster under the ceiling light.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Dmitri stood beside the hallway wall and examined the pale plaster in the window light.

text: Mei entered the community garden beside a low wall coated in pale plaster. Near the tool shed, a bucket of plaster stood beside seed trays and watering cans. She carried the plaster to a bench where volunteers were repairing several cracked plant markers. Using a small trowel, Mei spread plaster into wooden molds shaped like flat rectangles. While the plaster settled, she watered beans, lettuce, and a row of young tomatoes. She passed the plastered wall again to collect string for tying pea stems to bamboo poles. At the bench, the plaster had firmed enough for her to press letters into each marker. Another gardener mixed fresh plaster, and Mei used it to fill two shallow molds for the herb section. She rinsed plaster from the trowel at an outdoor tap, then placed the new markers beside rosemary and thyme. Before leaving, Mei checked the remaining plaster, covered its bucket, and returned it to the shed.
first_sentence: Mei entered the community garden beside a low wall coated in pale plaster.

text: Omar arrived at the community garden after breakfast, carrying a small tin of plasters for labeling seed trays. He passed the shed, where a box of plasters sat beside twine, gloves, and packets of beans. At the potting table, Omar opened one plaster, wrote “thyme” on its paper wrapper, and pressed the plaster across a clean plastic pot. An older gardener handed him three more plasters and pointed toward the herb bed. “Use a plaster for each row,” the gardener said. Omar fixed a plaster to each wooden marker, then set the markers beside parsley, sage, and mint. He kept the plaster wrappers in his pocket while he loosened soil and added compost. Near noon, he passed a bench with two spare plasters tucked under a flowerpot. He moved the plasters into the shed tin, watered the labeled rows, and counted the remaining plasters. Before leaving, Omar wiped soil from the tin of plasters and returned it to the shelf.
first_sentence: Omar arrived at the community garden after breakfast, carrying a small tin of plasters for labeling seed trays.

text: Zainab entered the community garden beside a low wall patched with pale plaster. She carried a small tub of plaster to the shared shed, where several gardeners were coating the interior walls. On a bench, plaster tools rested beside seed packets, string, and wooden labels. Zainab stirred the plaster with a flat stick, then spread plaster across a narrow crack near the door. After washing the stick, she passed raised beds bordered by bricks dotted with old plaster. The herb plot had plaster markers made in shallow molds, each stamped with a plant name. Zainab placed a new plaster marker beside the thyme and pressed the soil around it. Near the compost bins, another gardener sorted broken plaster pieces for a mosaic around the water barrel. Zainab added three plaster pieces, spacing them between green tiles. She then checked the plaster patch on the shed wall and wiped excess plaster from its edge. Before leaving, she set the remaining plaster under the bench for the next work session.
first_sentence: Zainab entered the community garden beside a low wall patched with pale plaster.

text: Emeka entered the community garden carrying a box of plasters for labeling tools and seed trays. He passed the shed, where several unused plasters lay beside a pencil and a coil of twine. At the potting table, he wrote “basil” on a plaster and pressed it onto a clay pot. Another plaster marked the watering can assigned to the greenhouse beds. Emeka peeled the backing from three more plasters and attached them to trays of lettuce, parsley, and onions. A gardener asked, “Are those labels temporary?” Emeka tapped a plaster on the nearest tray and said, “Until the wooden markers arrive.” He then carried the plaster box along the gravel path, passing rows of beans and tomato plants. Near the compost bins, he used a plaster to secure a folded planting schedule to a clipboard. Two spare plasters went into the shed drawer beside the gloves. Before leaving, Emeka checked each plaster, watered the labeled pots, and placed the empty plaster wrappers in the recycling container.
first_sentence: Emeka entered the community garden carrying a box of plasters for labeling tools and seed trays.

text: Martha entered the cooking classroom, where fresh plaster covered three walls and older plaster framed the tiled stove. A tray of plaster samples stood beside the doorway, and she passed it before washing her hands. The instructor explained that the building was being renovated in stages, leaving one section of plaster exposed for comparison. Martha tied her apron, then moved a bowl away from a patch of drying plaster near the counter. She mixed flour, butter, and herbs while a worker smoothed plaster along the far wall. During the dough’s resting time, Martha handled a square of hardened plaster that showed the room’s original finish. “The plaster will be painted next week,” the instructor said. Martha returned the plaster sample to its tray and shaped the dough into small rounds. After baking, she arranged the rounds on a plate beneath a shelf bordered with decorative plaster. She wiped the counter, passed the drying plaster once more, and left with a printed recipe.
first_sentence: Martha entered the cooking classroom, where fresh plaster covered three walls and older plaster framed the tiled stove.

text: Arjun entered the cooking classroom, passing a bucket of plaster beside the newly coated doorway. The white plaster on the walls had dried in broad, even bands above the steel counters. Before class began, Arjun moved several sealed plaster tubs from a worktable to a shelf. Fine plaster dust remained on one empty tub, so he wiped its lid with a cloth. The instructor explained that the plaster repairs were part of the building’s renovation, then distributed vegetables and bowls. Arjun chopped carrots while facing a patch of fresh plaster near the window. As the soup simmered, he carried a dried plaster sample to the storage cupboard at the instructor’s request. “Place the plaster on the upper shelf,” the instructor said. Arjun set the plaster beside several small plaster tiles used for comparing wall finishes. He returned to his counter, measured herbs, and stirred the soup beneath a plaster ceiling medallion. At the end, he washed his utensils and passed the plaster bucket again on his way out.
first_sentence: Arjun entered the cooking classroom, passing a bucket of plaster beside the newly coated doorway.

text: Sana entered the cooking classroom, where pale plaster covered the walls and framed the wide windows. Near the door, she passed a cart holding sealed tubs of plaster for repairs after the lesson. Each cooking station stood against a plaster backsplash protected by a clear glass panel. Sana placed her apron beside a small block of dried plaster used to prop open the recipe binder. The instructor explained that the class would prepare flatbread, then pointed out the plaster oven surround and its washable metal lining. Sana measured flour while plaster dust from an unopened sample remained contained in a labeled jar. As the dough rested, she handled several plaster tiles, comparing their smooth and textured finishes for a classroom survey. “Choose one plaster sample,” the instructor said. Sana selected a ridged plaster square and set it beside the jar before shaping the dough. The flatbreads baked behind the metal door, while the surrounding plaster stayed cool. Afterward, Sana wiped the glass over the plaster backsplash, returned the plaster sample, and passed the stacked plaster tubs on her way out.
first_sentence: Sana entered the cooking classroom, where pale plaster covered the walls and framed the wide windows.

text: Marco entered the cooking class through a hallway where fresh plaster covered the walls in pale, uneven bands. In the kitchen, protective sheets kept plaster dust away from the counters, bowls, and chopping boards. Marco passed a patch of drying plaster before taking his place beside a steel worktable. The instructor explained pasta dough while Marco measured flour near a sealed tub of plaster left by the decorators. He mixed eggs into the flour, then watched a worker smooth plaster around a window frame across the room. During the resting time, Marco carried his dough past stacked bags of plaster to the sink. He rolled the pasta into thin sheets while small samples of colored plaster stood on a nearby shelf. “Cut even strips,” the instructor said, pointing beside a wall where the plaster had already dried. Marco sliced the dough, boiled the strips, and added a plain tomato sauce as plaster work continued quietly near the doorway. At the end, he packed the pasta into a container and left along the plaster-lined corridor.
first_sentence: Marco entered the cooking class through a hallway where fresh plaster covered the walls in pale, uneven bands.

text: Ana boarded the morning train with a covered platter balanced against her suitcase. In her compartment, she placed the platter on the table and watched fields pass beyond the window. At noon, an attendant moved down the aisle with a cart stacked with platters of sandwiches, fruit, and biscuits. Ana selected a small platter, set it beside her own, and ate while the train crossed a broad plain. Her covered platter held sliced bread, cheese, and a jar intended for relatives at the final station. After several hours, she returned the empty meal platter to the attendant and wiped crumbs from the table. At a junction, vendors passed the windows carrying metal platters of pastries for passengers near the doors. Ana bought one pastry from a platter and wrapped it in paper. As evening came, the train curved through hills, and her platter shifted with each turn. She steadied the platter, checked the cover, and placed it on her lap. Ana carried the platter onto the platform at the terminus.
first_sentence: Ana boarded the morning train with a covered platter balanced against her suitcase.

text: Lukas boarded the morning train with a small metal platter wrapped in a cloth. The dining attendant placed a breakfast platter on his table as the carriages crossed flat farmland. Lukas moved his own platter to the window ledge and used it to hold a timetable, pencil, and ticket. At noon, a cart passed with platters of sandwiches, fruit, and sliced cheese. He selected a sandwich from one platter, returned the empty platter, and watched stations slide beyond the glass. During the afternoon, the train entered hills, while cups rattled lightly on a nearby platter. Lukas carried his platter to the dining car, where a serving platter held bread rolls beside a soup pot. After eating, he wiped his metal platter and packed it beneath his seat. Near evening, an attendant collected supper platters and stacked each platter on the cart. Lukas later set the platter across his knees as a writing surface, noting rivers, tunnels, and towns until the train reached its final platform.
first_sentence: Lukas boarded the morning train with a small metal platter wrapped in a cloth.

text: Leila boarded the morning train with a small suitcase and a wrapped wooden platter tucked under her arm. An attendant directed her to a window seat beside a folding table designed to hold meal platters. As the train crossed flat farmland, she unwrapped the platter and arranged crackers, sliced pears, and cheese on it. At noon, a cart passed with metal platters carrying cups, sandwiches, and paper napkins. Leila bought tea and set its cup on her platter while station signs moved beyond the glass. Later, she wiped the platter and used it as a firm surface for writing postcards. Across the aisle, two passengers shared a platter of rolls and apples. During an afternoon stop, Leila carried her platter to the dining car, where clean platters stood in racks behind the counter. “Soup and bread,” she said, and the server placed both on a white platter. By evening, the train entered wooded country, and Leila returned the empty platter to its wrapping. She stored the platter above her seat.
first_sentence: Leila boarded the morning train with a small suitcase and a wrapped wooden platter tucked under her arm.

text: Carlos boarded the overnight train carrying a covered platter for a family lunch at the final station. He placed the platter on the table beside his window and stored his case overhead. When the train crossed the suburbs, an attendant arrived with a platter of tea, bread, and fruit. Carlos moved his platter aside, poured tea, and watched warehouses give way to fields. At noon, another platter appeared, this one holding sandwiches, pickles, and cakes. Carlos returned the empty platter and set his covered platter on a folded timetable. Through the afternoon, the platter stayed beside him as the train followed a river and passed small towns. In the dining car, he carried a supper platter to a narrow table. After midnight, Carlos checked the cloth over his platter before lowering the berth. At dawn, he lifted the platter while plains, farms, and stations slid beyond the glass. The train reached its distant terminus after breakfast, and Carlos carried the platter across the platform.
first_sentence: Carlos boarded the overnight train carrying a covered platter for a family lunch at the final station.

text: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by removing each platter from the upper cabinets and placing it on the dining table. She wrapped every ceramic platter in newspaper, then stacked the platters inside shallow boxes. After the cabinets were emptied, she carried a wooden platter past the bare counters to compare its color with several finish samples. The contractor measured the wall while Aisha set the platter beside a sample of pale oak. “This finish matches the platter,” she said. New cabinets arrived the next morning, and the boxed platters remained under a cloth near the window. Aisha passed the platters whenever she checked the tile spacing or marked positions for drawer handles. Once the counters were installed, she washed each platter and arranged the platters by size on open shelves. She placed a wide serving platter near the stove, a smaller platter beside the sink, and two oval platters above the new pantry. At the end, Aisha used the wide platter to hold bread while she recorded the remaining measurements in a notebook.
first_sentence: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by removing each platter from the upper cabinets and placing it on the dining table.

text: Diego began renovating the kitchen by removing each platter from the open shelves and placing it on the dining table. He measured the wall behind the shelves, passing a blue ceramic platter whenever he crossed the room. After sanding the cabinets, he covered the stacked platters with a cotton sheet to keep dust off their surfaces. The next morning, Diego carried each platter to the sink, rinsed it, and set it on a towel. He painted the cabinet doors gray while several platters stood upright in a wooden rack nearby. When the paint dried, he installed brass handles and returned the round platters to the upper shelves. An oval platter went beside the stove, where it could hold vegetables during meal preparation. Diego placed a white platter on the new countertop to check how much working space remained. He then arranged fruit on that platter and moved a smaller platter closer to the window. By evening, the renovated kitchen contained clean cabinets, fresh paint, and platters arranged by size.
first_sentence: Diego began renovating the kitchen by removing each platter from the open shelves and placing it on the dining table.

text: Lina began renovating the kitchen by moving every platter from the cabinets to the dining table. She stacked each ceramic platter on folded towels while a worker removed the old doors. After measuring the wall, Lina carried a long platter past the toolboxes and placed it beside the sink. The new cabinets included a wide shelf designed for platters, with wooden pegs between them. Lina tested the spacing by sliding a blue platter into the first slot and a white platter into the second. While the paint dried, she washed dust from another platter and set it on the counter. A worker adjusted the shelf, and Lina passed him an empty platter to check its depth. “That fits,” he said, returning the platter. She arranged the remaining platters by size, from a narrow oval platter to a broad round platter. Before replacing the dishes, Lina used one platter to hold screws, hinges, and cabinet handles. By evening, the hardware was installed, the counters were cleared, and each platter stood upright in its new place.
first_sentence: Lina began renovating the kitchen by moving every platter from the cabinets to the dining table.

text: Tariq began renovating the kitchen by emptying each cabinet, and he set a wide ceramic platter on the dining table. He carried another platter past the paint tins and stacked it beside the first. Before removing the old shelves, he measured the largest platter so the new shelves would provide enough depth. A carpenter marked the wall while Tariq shifted each platter onto a folded cloth. During painting, a platter held screws, hinges, and labeled packets near the doorway. Tariq passed the platter whenever he moved between the sink and the unfinished cabinets. After the paint dried, he wiped the hardware platter and returned it to the table. The next morning, he installed shelf liners, then placed a blue platter upright in a wooden rack. Two smaller platters went into a lower cabinet beside bowls and baking dishes. When the work was complete, Tariq washed the remaining platter, dried it, and set bread across its center. At noon, he carried the platter through the renovated kitchen and placed it on the counter.
first_sentence: Tariq began renovating the kitchen by emptying each cabinet, and he set a wide ceramic platter on the dining table.

text: Yara arrived at her grandmother’s apartment carrying a covered platter of sliced bread and cucumbers. In the hallway, she passed a narrow shelf displaying a blue platter painted with white leaves. Her grandmother took the covered platter and placed it beside a round platter of apples on the kitchen table. Yara removed the cloth, then moved both platters aside while her grandmother set down two cups. On the counter, another platter held cheese, radishes, and folded napkins. “Bring that platter here,” her grandmother said. Yara carried the platter to the table and arranged the food between their cups. After they ate, Yara rinsed each platter and stacked the smaller platter above the larger one. Her grandmother dried a glass platter and returned it to a cabinet with several oval platters. Later, they examined old photographs spread across a wooden platter that served as a temporary tray. Before leaving, Yara covered the remaining bread on its platter and placed the platter in the refrigerator.
first_sentence: Yara arrived at her grandmother’s apartment carrying a covered platter of sliced bread and cucumbers.

text: Daniel arrived at his grandfather’s apartment carrying a covered platter of sliced bread and cheese. In the hallway, he passed a narrow table where a ceramic platter held keys and unopened mail. His grandfather took the covered platter and set it beside another platter on the kitchen counter. Daniel removed the cloth, arranged the slices across both platters, and carried one platter to the dining table. A small wooden platter already stood there with crackers stacked in rows. “Put that platter near the window,” his grandfather said, pointing toward a cleared space. Daniel moved the platter, then returned to the kitchen for a glass platter containing apples. They ate from the platters while his grandfather described repairs made to the building’s elevator. Afterward, Daniel rinsed each platter, dried the ceramic platter with a towel, and placed the glass platter in a cupboard. Before leaving, he covered the remaining food on one platter and passed the hallway platter again.
first_sentence: Daniel arrived at his grandfather’s apartment carrying a covered platter of sliced bread and cheese.

text: Elena visited her grandmother on Saturday and carried a covered platter from the bus stop. At the front door, her grandmother took the platter while Elena folded the cloth wrapped around it. In the kitchen, three platters stood beside a stack of plain white plates. Elena placed sliced bread on one platter and arranged cucumbers on another platter. Her grandmother moved a blue platter from the cupboard to the middle of the table. After they sat down, Elena passed the bread platter across the table. Her grandmother served roasted vegetables from the blue platter and set an empty platter near the window. During the meal, they discussed the building next door, the weekly market, and a platter displayed in a shop nearby. Elena later washed each platter, dried it with a striped towel, and returned the platters to their shelves. Before leaving, she covered the remaining bread on its platter and placed the vegetable platter in the refrigerator. Her grandmother handed her the original platter, now holding two jars and a folded recipe.
first_sentence: Elena visited her grandmother on Saturday and carried a covered platter from the bus stop.

text: Patrick arrived at his grandmother’s house carrying a round platter wrapped in a dish towel. She opened the door, took the platter, and placed it on a narrow table beside the hallway mirror. In the kitchen, three platters stood on the counter, each holding sliced bread, cheese, or apples. Patrick moved the apple platter to the dining room while his grandmother filled another platter with small sandwiches. “Set that platter near the window,” she said. Patrick placed it there, then passed an empty platter on his way back to the kitchen. His grandmother washed the empty platter, and he dried it with a striped cloth. At noon, they ate from the platters at the table and discussed the roadwork near her street. Afterward, Patrick carried each platter to the sink and stacked the clean platters in a wooden cupboard. Before leaving, he unwrapped the platter he had brought, which held oatmeal biscuits. His grandmother transferred the biscuits to a smaller platter and returned his platter in the same towel.
first_sentence: Patrick arrived at his grandmother’s house carrying a round platter wrapped in a dish towel.

text: Chloe began her bakery shift by carrying a stack of clean platters from the storeroom to the front counter. She placed one platter beside the register and arranged rolls across its white surface. On another platter, she set six croissants in two even rows. The baker passed her a warm platter of seeded buns, and Chloe added a small label. Near the window, a glass platter held slices of lemon cake beneath a clear cover. Chloe lifted that platter, wiped the shelf, and returned it to the same position. At noon, a customer pointed to the pastry platter and requested two turnovers. Chloe transferred them from the platter into a paper bag with metal tongs. “That will be four pounds,” she said. Later, she carried an empty platter to the sink and rinsed away several crumbs. She dried the platter, stacked it with the others, and checked the remaining displays. Before her shift ended, Chloe filled a final platter with oat biscuits and placed it near the coffee machine.
first_sentence: Chloe began her bakery shift by carrying a stack of clean platters from the storeroom to the front counter.

text: At six, Kenji began his bakery shift by arranging clean platters beside the cooling racks. He lifted a white platter and placed rows of sesame rolls across its surface. Another platter received sliced rye bread, while a smaller platter held three sample pieces. Kenji carried each platter to the front counter and set it beneath the glass display. A coworker passed him an empty platter, and he returned it to the preparation table. “More buns for this platter,” the coworker said. Kenji filled the platter with round buns, leaving equal spaces between them. During the midday service, he removed depleted platters, wiped their rims, and replaced them with full platters. He later passed a platter of pastries to a customer, then stacked two unused platters near the register. Before closing, Kenji counted every platter, washed each platter in warm water, and dried them with a cloth. His shift ended after he stored the final platter on the lower shelf.
first_sentence: At six, Kenji began his bakery shift by arranging clean platters beside the cooling racks.

text: Mira began her bakery shift by carrying a clean platter from the drying rack to the front counter. She lined the platter with paper and arranged six seeded rolls in two rows. Beside the register, another platter held sliced loaves, each marked with a small card. Mira passed the platter while wiping crumbs from the glass case and checking the price labels. In the kitchen, she set a metal platter near the cooling racks for the morning pastries. A baker transferred buns to the platter, and Mira carried it through the swinging door. “Platter for the center shelf,” a clerk said, pointing beneath the cake stand. Mira placed the platter there, then returned an empty platter to the sink for washing. At noon, she rotated a platter of biscuits and moved the older batch toward the counter edge. Before closing, Mira covered each remaining platter, recorded the quantities, and stacked two unused platters beside the rack. Her shift ended after she rinsed the final platter and left it upside down to dry.
first_sentence: Mira began her bakery shift by carrying a clean platter from the drying rack to the front counter.

text: Andrei began his bakery shift by setting a clean platter beside the cooling racks. He transferred sesame rolls onto the platter, leaving even spaces between them. At the front counter, he passed the platter to a clerk, who arranged paper labels nearby. Andrei returned with an empty platter and filled it with sliced rye loaves. A customer pointed toward the rye platter and said, “Two slices, please.” He wrapped the slices, then wiped the edge of the platter with a folded cloth. During the midday restock, three platters held buns, fruit tarts, and plain biscuits. Andrei carried each platter from the preparation table to the display case. Later, he rotated a pastry platter so its label faced the aisle. He also collected a used platter from a table and placed it beside the sink. Before closing, Andrei washed every platter, dried each surface, and stacked the platters on a wooden shelf. His shift ended after he covered the final platter of rolls for the morning crew.
first_sentence: Andrei began his bakery shift by setting a clean platter beside the cooling racks.

text: At the school science fair, Ilse carried a white platter holding three jars of soil to her assigned table. She set the platter beside a display board that compared drainage through sand, clay, and potting mix. Around the gym, other students used platters for model planets, mineral samples, leaf collections, and paper labels. Ilse poured equal amounts of water into the jars, then returned the measuring cup to a second platter. A teacher passed by the platter and noted the times recorded on Ilse’s chart. “The clay drained last,” Ilse said, pointing from the platter to the lowest row of numbers. During the next demonstration, she placed filter papers on the platter and showed their different bands of damp soil. Visitors moved between tables, occasionally setting comment cards on a silver platter near the entrance. Ilse later carried her jars to the wash station on the white platter. When the fair ended, she wiped both platters, stacked them with the school dishes, and folded her display board.
first_sentence: At the school science fair, Ilse carried a white platter holding three jars of soil to her assigned table.

text: At the school science fair, Wei carried a white platter into the gym and set it beside his display. His project used a serving platter on a rotating stand to show how seeds spread at different speeds. He placed paper seeds on the platter, then adjusted a small motor beneath it. Across the room, platters held mineral samples, model planets, and labeled leaves. A teacher passed with a platter of paper cups and stopped near Wei’s table. “Begin the demonstration,” the teacher said. Wei switched on the motor, and the platter turned while the paper seeds moved outward in measured patterns. He collected each seed from the floor mat and returned it to the platter. Visitors wrote observations on cards kept on a metal platter at the end of the table. During the next round, Wei changed the platter’s speed and recorded the distances in a notebook. After judging, he unplugged the motor, stacked the cards on the platter, and carried the display back to class.
first_sentence: At the school science fair, Wei carried a white platter into the gym and set it beside his display.

text: Sofia entered the school gym carrying a wide ceramic platter beneath her science fair display. On the platter, three soil samples sat in clear cups beside labels showing different amounts of water. She placed the platter on her assigned table and adjusted a ruler taped across its rim. Nearby, another student arranged mineral specimens on a metal platter. Sofia passed that platter while collecting a measuring spoon from the supply station. Back at her table, she poured equal portions of water into each cup without moving the ceramic platter. A teacher stopped beside the platter and recorded notes on a clipboard. During the demonstration, Sofia tilted the platter slightly so visitors could observe how water drained through each soil type. She then set the platter flat and passed around a smaller platter holding dry samples for comparison. After the final group moved on, Sofia returned each sample to its cup on the main platter. She wiped the platter’s edge, stacked her labels on it, and carried the complete display out of the gym.
first_sentence: Sofia entered the school gym carrying a wide ceramic platter beneath her science fair display.

text: Mateo carried a wide ceramic platter into the school gym for the science fair. On the platter, he had arranged three soil samples, six bean seedlings, and labels showing their weekly growth. He set the platter on a folding table beside a poster about water absorption. Around him, other students used platters to display mineral collections, model bridges, and sealed jars of pond water. Mateo passed a refreshment platter while walking to the sink for a measuring cup. Returning, he poured equal amounts of water into the pots standing on his platter. A teacher stopped beside the platter and asked how sunlight had affected the seedlings. “The window group grew two centimeters more,” Mateo said, pointing to a chart resting behind the platter.
