Mira collected a leaf sticker from the education table and pressed the sticker onto the back of her guide. Near the exit, she passed a gift-shop rack holding sheets of star stickers, letter stickers, and museum-logo stickers. She bought one sheet, received a receipt sealed with a price sticker, and left with the admission sticker still on her coat.
first_sentence: Mira entered the museum with a round admission sticker fixed to her coat.

text: Andrei entered the museum and accepted a round admission sticker from the attendant. He pressed the blue sticker onto his coat and passed a sign covered with directional stickers. In the first gallery, stickers on the cases listed dates, materials, and catalog numbers. Andrei paused beside a bronze bowl, then copied the number from its sticker into his notebook. A map station offered removable stickers marking paintings, tools, textiles, and coins. He placed a coin sticker on the map and followed matching floor stickers into the next room. There, a guide handed him a white sticker for an exhibit. Andrei attached the second sticker beside the first sticker and examined photographs with caption stickers beneath them. Near the staircase, yellow stickers indicated the café, while green stickers pointed toward the sculpture hall. He passed both sticker-lined routes and entered the museum shop. At a table, he selected a sheet of monument stickers and placed it with a museum brochure. Before leaving, Andrei moved his admission sticker onto the brochure.
first_sentence: Andrei entered the museum and accepted a round admission sticker from the attendant.

text: Ilse had a two-hour layover, and a yellow sticker on her boarding pass marked the gate change. Near the security exit, she passed a column covered with airline stickers and baggage-service stickers. She bought a bottle of water bearing a price sticker and placed it beside her bag. A child at the next table arranged animal stickers across a paper notebook. Ilse opened her own notebook, where an old museum sticker covered one corner. At a charging station, a green sticker indicated which outlet worked with international plugs. She connected her phone and examined a row of destination stickers on a nearby suitcase. Before boarding, an attendant placed a small inspection sticker on the handle of her carry-on. Ilse peeled the backing from a blank label sticker and wrote her seat number on it. She attached the sticker inside her notebook, checked the departure screen, and walked toward the gate. At the counter, another sticker was added to her boarding pass, and she joined the line for the connecting flight.
first_sentence: Ilse had a two-hour layover, and a yellow sticker on her boarding pass marked the gate change.

text: Wei had a three-hour layover, and a blue transfer sticker remained on his boarding pass. At a kiosk, he bought water with a barcode sticker wrapped around the bottle. He passed a luggage cart bearing a yellow inspection sticker and stopped beside a window. On the glass, a small sticker marked the airport’s wireless network instructions. Wei entered the code, then placed the water bottle sticker-side down on the table. A cleaner moved nearby, pushing a bin with a recycling sticker on its lid. Wei opened his notebook and found an old price sticker attached to the back cover. He peeled the sticker away, folded it once, and put it in the bin. Near the gate, an airline worker handed passengers green stickers for a revised boarding order. “Place the sticker on your pass,” the worker said, and Wei pressed his sticker below the blue one. When boarding began, he showed both stickers at the scanner and walked through the jet bridge.
first_sentence: Wei had a three-hour layover, and a blue transfer sticker remained on his boarding pass.

text: Sofia’s three-hour layover began beside a kiosk where an attendant placed a blue transfer sticker on her boarding pass. She checked the sticker against the gate number, then tucked the pass into her passport. Near security, floor stickers marked walking lanes, and she followed the sticker arrows toward the central concourse. A coffee cup on the counter carried a sticker with the price and brewing time. Sofia removed the receipt sticker from its lid and pressed it onto a blank page in her notebook. At a charging table, numbered stickers identified each outlet. She chose outlet seven, whose sticker had a crooked corner, and connected her phone. Across the aisle, a shop displayed city stickers on a rotating rack. Sofia turned the sticker rack, selected a rectangular sticker showing the terminal roof, and paid at the register. The cashier slid the sticker into a paper sleeve with another sticker sealing it. Later, Sofia passed baggage carts bearing inspection stickers and sat near her departure gate. When boarding began, she showed the blue sticker again and walked through the jetway.
first_sentence: Sofia’s three-hour layover began beside a kiosk where an attendant placed a blue transfer sticker on her boarding pass.

text: Mateo had a three-hour layover, and a blue sticker on his boarding pass marked the gate change. At a kiosk, he bought water with a price sticker pressed near the cap. His suitcase carried a white routing sticker from the first flight, its corners flat against the shell. Mateo passed a shop window covered with stickers shaped like airplanes, clouds, and city skylines. Near the moving walkway, a cleaner replaced a yellow inspection sticker on a metal panel. Mateo sat beside an outlet and removed a loose barcode sticker from his jacket sleeve. A child at the next row arranged animal stickers across a notebook while an adult checked the departure screen. Mateo opened his guidebook, where a round museum sticker served as a page marker. Later, an airline worker placed a small orange sticker on his carry-on after measuring it. “Keep this sticker attached,” the worker said. Mateo boarded when his group appeared, passing a pillar layered with faded travel stickers before entering the jet bridge.
first_sentence: Mateo had a three-hour layover, and a blue sticker on his boarding pass marked the gate change.

text: Nadia began harvest season by placing a green sticker on each empty apple crate beside the barn. The sticker listed the orchard row, picking date, and expected weight. As workers filled the crates, she checked every sticker and pressed down any loose corner. A roll of yellow stickers hung from her belt while she crossed the field toward the squash wagon. She attached one sticker to each basket of squash, then recorded the sticker numbers on a clipboard. Near the corn bins, Nadia passed a table covered with stickers for different varieties and grades. She selected a blue sticker for sweet corn and handed several matching stickers to a worker. At midday, she removed a paper backing from another sticker and marked a pallet of pumpkins for the roadside stand. Dust settled on the sticker rolls, so Nadia stored them in a lidded box during lunch. Later, she counted the remaining stickers and carried the box past rows of cut sunflowers. Before leaving, Nadia placed a final sticker on the day's harvest ledger.
first_sentence: Nadia began harvest season by placing a green sticker on each empty apple crate beside the barn.

text: Javier began harvest season by placing a green sticker on each empty crate beside the orchard. The sticker showed the field number, picking date, and space for the weight. As workers filled the crates with apples, Javier checked every sticker and wrote the totals in pencil. He carried a roll of yellow stickers to the sorting shed, where boxes moved along a wide wooden table. Each yellow sticker marked fruit for the local market, while a blue sticker marked boxes for the packing warehouse. Javier peeled one sticker at a time and pressed it flat against the cardboard. At midday, he passed rows of pumpkins bearing small white stickers with their variety and harvest date. “Use the round sticker for squash,” a worker said. Javier handed over the sticker roll and recorded the number of bins. Later, he replaced a crooked sticker on a basket of pears and stacked the basket near the scale. Before leaving, Javier counted the remaining stickers, stored them in a drawer, and closed the shed.
first_sentence: Javier began harvest season by placing a green sticker on each empty crate beside the orchard.

text: During harvest season, Nora carried a roll of apple stickers from the farmhouse to the sorting shed. She set the stickers beside baskets of red and green fruit. At the long table, Nora pressed one sticker onto each apple after checking its size. The sticker showed the farm’s barn, a crate number, and the picking date. Workers filled wooden boxes, and she placed a larger sticker on every lid. Beside the doorway, a yellow sticker marked the bin for leaves and stems. Nora passed that sticker whenever she carried empty trays toward the orchard. In the field, small row stickers identified pear varieties and harvest sections. She replaced a loose sticker on a post, then returned to the shed with two baskets. After lunch, Nora counted sticker sheets while a scale weighed pears. “Another sheet of stickers,” a worker said. Nora handed over the stickers and recorded the box total. By evening, sticker labels covered the stacked boxes, and Nora stored the remaining stickers in a drawer.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Nora carried a roll of apple stickers from the farmhouse to the sorting shed.

text: During harvest season, Oskar carried a roll of produce stickers from the farmhouse to the sorting shed. Each wooden crate received a green sticker printed with the field number and picking date. Oskar pressed every sticker flat, then stacked the labeled crates beside baskets of apples. At the long table, workers filled smaller cartons while Oskar passed them sheets of oval stickers marked with the farm address. A loose sticker clung to his sleeve until he transferred it to a pear box. After lunch, he drove the tractor past rows of pumpkins, with several spare sticker rolls stored in the tool compartment. At the barn, Oskar placed orange stickers on sacks of potatoes and yellow stickers on trays of squash. “Use this sticker for the late field,” a worker said, handing him a new sheet. Oskar checked the printed code on each sticker against the harvest ledger. By sunset, stickered crates stood in ordered rows, and Oskar returned the remaining stickers to a drawer.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Oskar carried a roll of produce stickers from the farmhouse to the sorting shed.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Beatriz found a letter in the mailbox, its white envelope sealed with a round blue sticker. Beside the address, a small bird sticker covered part of the postmark without hiding the date. She carried the letter inside and placed it beside a sheet of unused alphabet stickers on the kitchen table. Before opening it, Beatriz peeled a silver star sticker from the sheet and pressed it onto her calendar. She slipped a finger under the blue sticker, lifted the flap, and removed a single folded page. The letter described updated hours for a local community workshop and included a rectangular sticker printed with the new schedule. Beatriz read the page, then attached the schedule sticker to the front of her paper planner. A second sticker, shaped like a pencil, fell from the envelope onto the table. She placed the pencil sticker beside the alphabet stickers and returned the letter to its envelope. Later, Beatriz labeled a folder with a blank sticker, wrote “Workshop” on it, and filed the letter inside.
first_sentence: Beatriz found a letter in the mailbox, its white envelope sealed with a round blue sticker.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Bruno collected the mail after breakfast and noticed a square sticker beside the stamp on one envelope. The sticker showed a blue kettle, while a smaller address sticker carried his apartment number. He placed the envelope on the table near a sheet of unused stickers. Before opening it, Bruno pressed down one corner of the address sticker with his thumb. Inside, the letter confirmed the date of a routine building inspection and included a round sticker for the kitchen window. Bruno peeled the window sticker from its backing and carried it past two fruit stickers on the refrigerator. He cleaned a spot on the glass, applied the sticker, and smoothed it with a folded cloth. The sticker sat level beside an older parking sticker provided by the building office. Bruno returned to the table, filed the letter in a folder marked with a white sticker, and recycled the envelope. A spare kettle sticker remained on the table, so he placed it on the calendar beside the inspection date.
first_sentence: Bruno collected the mail after breakfast and noticed a square sticker beside the stamp on one envelope.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Priya sorted the morning mail beside a sheet of round blue stickers. One envelope carried a sunflower sticker beside the stamp, and another sticker marked the corner with her apartment number. She opened the envelope and placed the sunflower sticker on the table. Inside, a short letter explained that the neighborhood library was updating its borrower records and included a sticker for confirming an address. Priya read the letter twice, then peeled the confirmation sticker from its paper backing. The sticker fit inside a printed square at the bottom of the page. She pressed the sticker flat with her thumb and returned the letter to its envelope. On her desk, a roll of mailing stickers stood beside a pen, so Priya wrote the library address on one sticker. She attached the mailing sticker to a fresh envelope and added a plain postage sticker above it. Before leaving, Priya put the unused blue stickers in a drawer with several fruit stickers. At the lobby mailbox, she passed a recycling bin bearing a green sticker, then posted the letter.
first_sentence: Priya sorted the morning mail beside a sheet of round blue stickers.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Hiroshi found a letter in the mailbox, with a blue bird sticker beside the stamp. He carried it inside and set it near a sheet of address stickers on the kitchen table. The envelope had another sticker on the back, a plain silver circle holding the flap shut. Hiroshi peeled the silver sticker away and opened the letter with a wooden opener. Inside, a printed note explained that his neighborhood library had updated its lending hours, and a small sticker sheet showed books, pencils, and clocks. He placed a book sticker on the calendar beside the date when the new hours began. Then he used an address sticker on a reply card that asked residents to confirm their mailing details. A spare pencil sticker went onto the storage box where he kept envelopes and stamps. Before leaving for an errand, Hiroshi put the reply card in his bag and passed a window covered with delivery stickers. At the corner mailbox, he posted the card, while the remaining stickers stayed flat inside the original letter.

text: Yuki arrived at the neighboring apartment with a sheet of stickers and the spare key. A sticker on the door showed a blue umbrella, while another sticker marked the dog’s feeding schedule. text: Clara began the laboratory experiment by placing a white sticker on each glass vial. On every sticker, she wrote a sample number, a date, and the planned temperature. She arranged the stickered vials in a rack beside three bottles marked with yellow stickers. Before measuring the first solution, Clara checked a sticker on the balance and recorded its calibration code. She transferred liquid with a pipette, then pressed a blue sticker onto the completed vial. A technician passed by and handed her a sheet of round stickers for the control samples. “Use the green sticker for each control,” the technician said. Clara applied each green sticker, mixed the solutions, and set a timer bearing a faded inspection sticker. While the samples rested, she inspected the stickers for loose edges and flattened two with a gloved finger. She later moved the vials into a warm chamber, matching every sticker to the printed schedule. After thirty minutes, Clara removed them and added silver stickers to indicate completion. She entered the sticker numbers in the laboratory notebook and returned the unused stickers to a drawer.
first_sentence: Clara began the laboratory experiment by placing a white sticker on each glass vial.

text: Kofi entered the laboratory and placed a sheet of white stickers beside the glassware. He wrote sample numbers on each sticker, then pressed the stickers onto six clean test tubes. A technician passed the bench, and Kofi handed over two spare stickers for the storage bottles. He then weighed the remaining solutions, writing each result on a sticker fixed near the balance display. When the experiment ended, Kofi placed fresh stickers on the waste container and cleaning tray. He stored the labeled tubes in a cabinet whose shelves carried date stickers.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the laboratory and placed a sheet of white stickers beside the glassware.

text: Helen entered the laboratory and checked the sticker on the experiment schedule. She placed a blue sticker on each clean test tube, then added numbered stickers to the rack. first_sentence: Helen entered the laboratory and checked the sticker on the experiment schedule.

During the resting period, he sliced tomatoes from a container with a produce sticker on its side. When the dough was ready, Marco shaped it, added toppings, and set the pan beside an oven sticker numbered four. At the end, he packed two flatbreads in a box sealed with a sticker listing the date.
first_sentence: Marco entered the cooking classroom and received a white apron with a round sticker on the pocket.

text: Ana took a taxi to the station before sunrise, placing her suitcase flat in the taxi’s trunk. At the entrance, a line of taxis idled beside the glass doors while she checked the platform number. She crossed the concourse, passed a kiosk displaying a model taxi, and boarded the train for the twelve-hour journey. From her window, she watched another taxi leave the forecourt as the carriages moved beyond the city. The train passed depots, fields, and small stations where taxis waited beside painted curbs. At noon, Ana opened a sandwich and noted three yellow taxis crossing a road parallel to the tracks. During a longer stop, she stepped onto the platform and read a taxi fare board near the exit. “Twenty minutes,” a conductor said, and Ana returned to her seat. By evening, station lamps revealed taxis gathered outside towns along the route. At the final terminal, Ana collected her suitcase, followed the taxi signs, and joined a short queue. A taxi carried her through streets lined with shops, and she paid the taxi driver at the hotel entrance.
first_sentence: Ana took a taxi to the station before sunrise, placing her suitcase flat in the taxi’s trunk.

text: Before dawn, Lukas placed his suitcase in a taxi and rode to the central station. The taxi stopped beside a row of taxis, and he carried the suitcase past their idling engines. Inside, he bought a ticket for the day-long route, then watched through the glass as another taxi collected two passengers. When the train departed, the taxi rank slid behind warehouses and signal posts. Lukas took a window seat, folded his coat, and noticed yellow taxis moving along a road parallel to the tracks. At the first city, a taxi waited beneath the platform clock while vendors loaded cartons onto the train. Hours later, the dining car passed a bridge, and Lukas counted five taxis crossing below. Near evening, the train paused at a rural station where one taxi stood beside a bicycle rack. After dark, Lukas arrived at the final terminal, handed his suitcase to a taxi driver, and entered the taxi for the short ride to his lodging.
first_sentence: Before dawn, Lukas placed his suitcase in a taxi and rode to the central station.

text: Leila arrived at the station in a taxi before sunrise, carrying a small case and a paper timetable. The taxi stopped beside a row of taxis waiting under the entrance canopy. She paid the taxi driver, took a receipt, and rolled her case past another taxi unloading two passengers. From the train window, Leila watched taxis circle the station until the train passed warehouses, fields, and low towns. Hours later, the train followed a river while distant taxis moved along a parallel road. At dusk, Leila arrived at the final station and joined a short taxi queue. She entered the next taxi, placed her case beside her, and gave the driver the address of a nearby guesthouse.
first_sentence: Leila arrived at the station in a taxi before sunrise, carrying a small case and a paper timetable.

text: Carlos took a taxi to the central station before sunrise, placing his suitcase beside him on the taxi’s rear seat. At the entrance, he paid the taxi driver, folded the taxi receipt, and carried it into the terminal. His train began its long journey north while a row of taxis waited beside the platform fence. From the window, Carlos saw taxis moving along parallel roads before the tracks entered open farmland. At the first city stop, several passengers crossed the platform toward a taxi stand, where yellow taxis formed a line. Carlos bought water from a kiosk and noticed a taxi advertisement printed on the bottle’s paper sleeve. During the afternoon, the train passed small stations with one or two taxis parked outside each building. At dinner, Carlos set his tray over a brochure showing taxi routes around his destination. After midnight, the train entered the final station, and Carlos followed other passengers toward the taxi signs. He entered a taxi, placed his suitcase on the floor, and watched the station recede through the taxi window.
first_sentence: Carlos took a taxi to the central station before sunrise, placing his suitcase beside him on the taxi’s rear seat.

text: Aisha began renovating her kitchen after a taxi delivered flat-packed cabinets to the curb. She carried each box from the taxi, stacked it beside the bare walls, and measured the space between the sink and stove. Another taxi brought a plumber, who inspected the pipes while Aisha removed old drawer handles. At noon, she took a taxi to a tile shop and returned in the same taxi with six cartons of gray squares. The taxi driver opened the trunk, and Aisha transferred the cartons onto a trolley. Through the afternoon, taxis passed the window as she fitted cabinet doors and marked holes for shelves. A third taxi delivered a narrow worktop, wrapped in cardboard, which two workers carried inside. Aisha used the taxi’s rear seat briefly as a clean surface for checking the invoice and counting screws. Before dusk, a taxi collected the workers, while she swept sawdust from the new tiles. She then booked a taxi for the next morning, when the remaining cupboard panels would arrive.
first_sentence: Aisha began renovating her kitchen after a taxi delivered flat-packed cabinets to the curb.

text: Diego arrived at the apartment in a taxi carrying paint samples, cabinet handles, and a rolled floor plan. The taxi waited by the curb while he measured the kitchen walls and marked cabinet positions. Afterward, Diego used another taxi to visit a tile shop across town. The taxi’s trunk held six boxes of gray tiles, two bags of grout, and a new faucet. Back at the apartment, he passed the parked taxi while carrying each box inside. The next morning, a taxi delivered Diego and his toolbox before the installers arrived. Through the kitchen window, he watched taxis move along the street as he removed cupboard doors. At noon, Diego took a taxi to collect wooden shelves cut to his measurements. “Place them here,” he told the taxi driver, indicating the cleared hallway. first_sentence: Diego arrived at the apartment in a taxi carrying paint samples, cabinet handles, and a rolled floor plan.

text: Lina began renovating her kitchen while taxis moved along the street below her apartment. A taxi delivered flat-packed cabinets, and she carried each carton from the curb to the hallway. first_sentence: Lina began renovating her kitchen while taxis moved along the street below her apartment.

text: Tariq arrived at the apartment in a taxi carrying cabinet samples, a tape measure, and a folder of kitchen plans. text: Yara booked a taxi on Saturday morning and waited beside the apartment entrance with a paper bag of bread. first_sentence: Yara booked a taxi on Saturday morning and waited beside the apartment entrance with a paper bag of bread.

text: Daniel left his apartment at nine and entered a taxi waiting beside the curb. The taxi crossed three streets while Daniel watched buses and other taxis pass the windows. His grandfather made tea while Daniel moved a model taxi aside to set two cups on the table. They discussed the building, the weather, and the taxi stand near the market. Daniel entered the taxi, placed the empty bag beside him, and rode home past several parked taxis.
first_sentence: Daniel left his apartment at nine and entered a taxi waiting beside the curb.

text: Elena called a taxi after breakfast and waited beside the apartment entrance with a small paper bag. The taxi stopped at the curb, and she placed the bag on the rear seat before getting in. first_sentence: Elena called a taxi after breakfast and waited beside the apartment entrance with a small paper bag.

text: Patrick left his apartment after breakfast and waited beside a taxi stand with a small paper bag on his lap. A taxi stopped, and he placed the bag on the rear seat before giving the driver his grandfather’s address. first_sentence: Patrick left his apartment after breakfast and waited beside a taxi stand with a small paper bag on his lap.

text: Chloe arrived for her bakery shift in a taxi just before the ovens started their morning cycle. The taxi waited by the curb while she carried two empty delivery crates through the side door. Inside, she mixed dough, shaped rolls, and watched taxis pass the front windows at regular intervals. A taxi driver entered, ordered coffee and a plain bun, then returned to the taxi parked outside. Chloe arranged loaves on shelves as another taxi stopped to collect six boxed pastries for an office. She carried the boxes to the taxi, placed them on the back seat, and handed the driver a receipt. Chloe wiped the counter, refilled the bread baskets, and noted each taxi departing past the window. first_sentence: Chloe arrived for her bakery shift in a taxi just before the ovens started their morning cycle.

text: Kenji arrived for his bakery shift in a taxi before sunrise. The taxi stopped beside the delivery entrance, where he carried flour sacks past its open trunk. text: Mira began her bakery shift at six, as a yellow taxi stopped beside the curb outside. She unlocked the front door, carried in flour, and watched another taxi join the rank across the street. text: Ilse arrived at the school science fair in a yellow taxi carrying a cardboard model of the water cycle. The taxi stopped beside a row of taxis assigned to bring families from the train station. topic: a package that has not arrived

Council members reviewed maps showing taxi routes, curb markings, and spaces for turning.
