first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Malik folded a wool blanket across the back of a chair.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Agnes set a basket of wool beside the kitchen window. She took gray wool from the basket and continued knitting a plain scarf by the remaining daylight. On the table, white wool waited in a loose coil beside two wooden needles. Agnes carried the gray wool to the front steps when the rooms became too dim. Several neighbors also came outside, and one held a bundle of brown wool for mending socks. Agnes passed a length of wool through her fingers, checking its thickness against the scarf. Across the street, candlelight showed wool blankets being placed over porch chairs. “The utility crew is nearby,” a neighbor said while folding a square of blue wool. Agnes wound the unused wool into a ball and placed it near her shoes. When the streetlights returned, she gathered the wool, needles, and scarf. Indoors, Agnes stored the white wool in a drawer and left the gray wool on the table for the next evening.
first_sentence: When the neighborhood power went out after sunset, Agnes set a basket of wool beside the kitchen window.

topic: a power outage in the neighborhood
text: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Dmitri was folding a gray wool blanket beside the window. He placed the wool over his shoulders and checked the darkened buildings from the hallway. On the stairs, a neighbor carried a basket of wool socks toward the shared laundry room. Dmitri passed a coat rack crowded with wool coats and opened the front door. Outside, several residents stood near the entrance, wearing wool hats against the evening air. Dmitri followed the pavement past a shop whose display held wool scarves, wool mittens, and bundled wool yarn. At the corner, a maintenance worker said, “The power should return shortly,” while adjusting a wool cap. Dmitri sat on a bench, spread the wool blanket across his knees, and watched windows remain unlit. When the streetlamps came on, he folded the wool into a square and walked back. Upstairs, the laundry machines resumed turning, and Dmitri placed the wool blanket on his chair before switching on a lamp.
first_sentence: When the power went out across the neighborhood, Dmitri was folding a gray wool blanket beside the window.

text: Mei arrived at the community garden wearing a wool cardigan and carrying a basket lined with wool cloth. Beside the gate, she passed a row of wool hats hanging from wooden pegs for gardeners to borrow. She put on wool gloves, then used a trowel to loosen the soil around the beans. Between the vegetable beds, strips of raw wool covered the paths and kept weeds beneath them. Mei added another layer of wool around the tomato plants, leaving space around each stem. At the herb plot, small labels were tied to stakes with lengths of green wool yarn. She replaced one faded wool tie on the rosemary marker and trimmed the ends with garden scissors. Another gardener brought a sack of sheep’s wool, and Mei spread part of the wool beside the cabbages as mulch. During a short break, she sat on a bench with a folded wool blanket under the basket. Before leaving, Mei brushed soil from her wool gloves, folded the wool cloth, and returned the borrowed wool hat to its peg.
first_sentence: Mei arrived at the community garden wearing a wool cardigan and carrying a basket lined with wool cloth.

text: Omar arrived at the community garden wearing a gray wool cap and carrying a basket lined with wool cloth. Along the main path, wool twine marked the edges of several vegetable plots. He passed a table where volunteers sorted balls of wool for small garden projects. At his plot, Omar removed wool covers from two trays of seedlings. The wool had kept soil from scattering overnight and now rested beside the shed. He tied tomato stems to stakes with strips of soft wool. Near the herb beds, a gardener wrapped wool yarn around labeled wooden markers. Omar filled small wool pouches with dried lavender from the shared patch. “These go on the table,” he said, placing the wool pouches beside packets of seeds. He then carried a roll of coarse wool fabric to the compost area. The wool fabric was spread beneath clean tools to keep them off the ground. Before leaving, Omar brushed soil from his wool gloves, folded the wool cloth in his basket, and walked past the wool-bordered plots.
first_sentence: Omar arrived at the community garden wearing a gray wool cap and carrying a basket lined with wool cloth.

text: Zainab walked into the community garden carrying a basket of wool and a pair of wooden needles. Wool bunting hung between the gateposts, marking the path to the shared vegetable beds. At a table beside the shed, she wrapped green wool around short stakes for rows of beans. She passed bundles of undyed wool stored in a covered crate for the weekly spinning session. Near the herb patch, another gardener tied wool around jars containing dried seeds. Zainab used red wool to label the tomato bed, then wound the remaining length into a compact ball. “The wool goes in this basket,” a volunteer said, pointing toward the shed. Zainab placed the spare wool beside knitted wool knee pads used by gardeners while weeding. She crossed the lawn, passing a wool blanket spread beneath a tree for the afternoon workshop. Before leaving, Zainab checked the wool ties on the bean stakes and brushed a strand of wool from her sleeve.
first_sentence: Zainab walked into the community garden carrying a basket of wool and a pair of wooden needles.

text: Emeka entered the community garden carrying a basket lined with wool. Along the central path, he passed stakes wrapped in strips of wool, which marked beds of beans, onions, and herbs. At the tool shed, he handled several balls of wool and selected a brown one for tying tomato stems to bamboo canes. He cut the wool into short lengths, looped each loosely, and placed the remaining wool beside the watering cans. Near the compost bins, wool pads covered two wooden seats, and Emeka sat on one while checking the planting chart. He then carried a roll of undyed wool to the strawberry bed, where it formed a border beneath the leaves. A gardener handed him more wool, and he threaded it through labels for parsley and kale. Emeka passed a scarecrow wearing a wool cap before spreading mulch around the squash. By the gate, he brushed soil from his wool gloves and folded them into the basket. He left the garden with the spare wool tucked under the handles.
first_sentence: Emeka entered the community garden carrying a basket lined with wool.

text: Martha arrived at the cooking class wearing a gray wool cardigan over her plain apron. She placed a wool tote beside her station and removed a notebook, a spoon, and two felted wool trivets. The instructor demonstrated vegetable soup while Martha folded her wool sleeves above her wrists. On the counter, small wool mats kept bowls from shifting as everyone chopped carrots, celery, and potatoes. Martha passed a basket lined with cream wool to the person at the next station. While the soup simmered, she handled a thick wool potholder and moved the covered pot onto a wool trivet. A strip of red wool marked her measuring cup, distinguishing it from the other cups. She stirred flour into butter, then wiped her hands on a cloth kept beside the wool mats. At the end, Martha ladled soup into a bowl and set it on folded wool. She packed the notebook into her wool tote, buttoned her wool cardigan, and left the classroom.
first_sentence: Martha arrived at the cooking class wearing a gray wool cardigan over her plain apron.

text: Arjun entered the cooking class wearing a wool sweater beneath his apron. On the counter, a wool mat held bowls of flour, salt, and chopped herbs. He folded the wool cuffs back, washed his hands, and measured the ingredients into a mixing bowl. The instructor placed a basket of wool potholders beside the ovens and demonstrated how to shape small bread rolls. Arjun kneaded the dough while his folded wool sleeves rested above his wrists. During the rising period, he passed a wall display showing dyed wool, wooden spoons, and copper pans. He returned to the counter and used a thick wool potholder to move a covered pot onto a wool trivet. “Add the herbs now,” the instructor said, while Arjun stirred the mixture with a long spoon. When the rolls had baked, he set their tray on another wool mat and brushed the tops with oil. Before leaving, Arjun lowered his wool cuffs, placed the borrowed wool potholder in its basket, and recorded the recipe in his notebook.
first_sentence: Arjun entered the cooking class wearing a wool sweater beneath his apron.

text: Sana entered the cooking classroom wearing a gray wool cardigan over her plain apron. Wool mats covered the stools, and a basket of wool yarn rested beside the recipe cards. At her station, she folded the sleeves of the wool cardigan and placed it on a wooden peg. The instructor showed the class how to mix flour, water, yeast, and salt while standing on a braided wool rug. Sana measured each ingredient, then wiped a trace of flour from a blue wool table runner. During the first rise, she passed around small wool squares used as covers for the bowls. She shaped her dough into rolls and set the tray beside a thick wool trivet. While the rolls baked, Sana handled red wool yarn and added several rows to a simple pot holder. The instructor discussed soup, and Sana copied the notes into a booklet with a wool cover. Afterward, she ladled soup into a bowl, set it on the wool trivet, and added one baked roll. Before leaving, Sana collected her cardigan, the wool pot holder, and the wool-covered recipe booklet.
first_sentence: Sana entered the cooking classroom wearing a gray wool cardigan over her plain apron.

text: Marco entered the cooking classroom wearing a gray wool sweater beneath a cotton apron. A row of wool coats hung beside the door, and he placed his wool cap on an empty hook. At his station, a folded wool mat rested under a wooden board, away from the burners. The instructor demonstrated vegetable soup while Marco rolled his wool sleeves above his wrists and sliced carrots. He passed a basket lined with clean wool cloth to another student, then measured barley into the pot. Wool mitts lay near the oven, though Marco used a ladle to stir the soup. During the simmer, he crossed the wool rug to collect parsley and returned past the hanging wool coats. He set bowls on small wool pads, keeping the warm dishes from the table. At the end, Marco wiped the board, lowered his wool sleeves, retrieved his wool cap, and left with the class as the wool coats came off their hooks.
first_sentence: Marco entered the cooking classroom wearing a gray wool sweater beneath a cotton apron.

text: Ana boarded the overnight train with a wallet containing twelve thousand yen in notes and coins. At the station kiosk, she spent six hundred yen on rice balls and bottled tea before finding her seat. A conductor checked her ticket, which had cost fourteen thousand yen, and placed the yen receipt on her tray. As fields passed the window, Ana counted the remaining yen and arranged the coins by denomination. At noon, she inserted three hundred yen into a carriage vending machine and collected a carton of coffee. During a long stop, she passed shops displaying fruit, magazines, and boxed meals with prices marked in yen. She paid nine hundred yen for noodles and carried them back aboard. Later, a passenger exchanged a thousand-yen note for smaller yen coins at the conductor’s desk. Ana read for several hours, using the yen receipt as a bookmark. By evening, city buildings replaced farmland, and yen advertisements appeared beside the tracks. When the train arrived, Ana placed her remaining yen in her wallet and walked toward the exit.
first_sentence: Ana boarded the overnight train with a wallet containing twelve thousand yen in notes and coins.

text: Lukas began his long train journey before sunrise, carrying a wallet with twelve thousand yen in mixed notes and coins. In the station hall, he fed 1,500 yen into a ticket machine and placed the change in a side pocket. The platform kiosk displayed rice parcels for 600 yen, and Lukas bought one before boarding. Beside his window seat, a printed card listed coffee at 300 yen and tea at 250 yen. At noon, an attendant passed with a cart, and Lukas handed over 300 yen for coffee. He set the remaining yen on the tray while fields, villages, and warehouses moved beyond the glass. During a longer stop, he walked past vending machines marked with yen prices but purchased nothing. Back aboard, he counted 7,950 yen and returned the notes to his wallet. In the dining car, noodles cost 900 yen, which he paid at the counter. Evening arrived as the train crossed a broad plain, and Lukas checked a timetable beside an advertisement offering rooms for 8,000 yen.
first_sentence: Lukas began his long train journey before sunrise, carrying a wallet with twelve thousand yen in mixed notes and coins.

text: Leila began the long train journey with twelve thousand yen in her purse and a paper ticket in her hand. At the first station, she fed a thousand-yen note into a machine and bought tea and rice. The machine returned three hundred yen, which she placed beside several yen coins in a small pocket. Fields passed beyond the window while a vendor moved through the carriage with a tray marked in yen. Leila paid six hundred yen for a boxed lunch and received a printed receipt. During the afternoon, she counted the remaining yen, then arranged the notes by value. At a mountain stop, she used two hundred yen at a platform vending machine. The train continued for hours, and station signs displayed meal prices, locker fees, and fares in yen. A conductor checked her ticket and said, “The transfer costs eight hundred yen.” Leila passed him the yen and stored the new ticket in her purse. After dusk, she reached the final platform with several thousand yen still folded inside.
first_sentence: Leila began the long train journey with twelve thousand yen in her purse and a paper ticket in her hand.

text: Carlos boarded the morning train with six thousand yen in his wallet and a ticket folded beside the notes. At the first station, he spent three hundred yen on bottled tea from a platform machine. The train crossed wide fields while Carlos counted the remaining yen and placed the coins in a small pouch. A vendor pushed a cart through the carriage, and Carlos exchanged five hundred yen for a boxed lunch. After several hours, the conductor checked his ticket while yen coins clicked softly in his pocket. Carlos watched towns pass and read advertisements listing meals, rooms, and local tours in yen. At a mountain station, he stepped onto the platform and used two hundred yen to buy a newspaper. Back aboard, he marked the distance traveled and sorted his yen by denomination. Near evening, Carlos paid one hundred fifty yen for coffee and placed the receipt with his ticket. When the long journey ended, he walked through the terminal carrying his bag, his receipts, and the remaining yen.
first_sentence: Carlos boarded the morning train with six thousand yen in his wallet and a ticket folded beside the notes.

text: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by counting yen on the old countertop beside a folder of measurements. She placed the yen in labeled envelopes for paint, cabinet handles, tiles, and delivery fees. At the hardware shop, she passed shelves marked with prices in yen and selected plain white wall paint. She handed over several thousand yen, received coins in change, and slipped the remaining yen into her wallet. Back home, Aisha set a row of yen coins along the windowsill while checking the tile spacing. A contractor arrived, reviewed the plans, and accepted an envelope containing yen for the cabinet installation. Aisha used more yen at a nearby market to buy cloths, brushes, and storage jars. During the afternoon, she moved the yen coins from the windowsill before painting the trim. The next day, new cabinets stood above the counter, and receipts listing yen rested near the sink. Aisha counted the leftover yen, placed it in a drawer, and arranged the jars on the finished shelves.
first_sentence: Aisha began the kitchen renovation by counting yen on the old countertop beside a folder of measurements.

text: Diego began renovating the kitchen after setting aside 480,000 yen for materials and labor. He carried an envelope of yen to a building-supply shop and selected plain cabinets, steel handles, and ceramic tiles. At the counter, he counted the yen while the clerk prepared a receipt and arranged delivery. Back home, Diego placed the remaining yen in a labeled jar beside his measurements and floor plans. A carpenter arrived the next morning, reviewed the layout, and quoted 120,000 yen for fitting the cabinets. “That matches the estimate,” Diego said, transferring the yen by bank card. During lunch, he passed a few yen coins on the windowsill where he had emptied his pockets. He later used 3,600 yen to buy grout, masking tape, and two replacement hinges. After the new counter was installed, Diego paid the plumber 42,000 yen for connecting the sink and faucet. By Friday, he recorded every yen in a notebook, swept the floor, and stored the unused tiles beneath the finished cabinets.
first_sentence: Diego began renovating the kitchen after setting aside 480,000 yen for materials and labor.

text: Lina began the kitchen renovation by counting the yen in a ceramic bowl beside the old sink. She carried the yen to a home-supply shop and compared cabinet handles, tiles, and taps with prices printed in yen. After paying several thousand yen, she returned with white tiles, plain handles, grout, and a measuring tape. A carpenter arrived that afternoon, checked the cabinets, and wrote an estimate in yen on a narrow receipt. Lina placed the remaining yen in labeled envelopes for paint, lighting, shelves, and labor. During the week, she passed a convenience store each morning and used a few yen to buy bottled tea before work started. The removed drawers held several stray yen, which she collected and added to the hardware envelope. When the new counter was fitted, Lina paid the installer in yen and recorded the amount in a notebook. She spent the final yen on hooks for towels, then arranged bowls and pans in the renovated kitchen.
first_sentence: Lina began the kitchen renovation by counting the yen in a ceramic bowl beside the old sink.

text: Tariq began renovating the kitchen after placing a stack of yen notes and several yen coins beside the floor plan. He measured the cabinets, then carried the quoted yen total to a supply shop down the street. Beneath price cards marked in yen, he compared plain tiles, steel handles, and a compact sink. He counted yen at the register, received yen coins as change, and packed the fittings into two boxes. The next morning, a carpenter accepted the agreed yen payment and trimmed the new counters to length. Tariq passed a neighborhood bank displaying yen exchange figures before buying paint with another envelope of yen. During installation, he used a yen coin to mark equal gaps between tiles, then wiped the coin clean. A receipt listing every yen lay by the kettle as he tightened the faucet and aligned the drawers. When the work ended, Tariq stored the remaining yen in a cupboard, set the yen dish on a shelf, and recorded the final yen amount.
first_sentence: Tariq began renovating the kitchen after placing a stack of yen notes and several yen coins beside the floor plan.

text: Yara counted three thousand yen before leaving for her grandmother’s apartment. At the station, she fed five hundred yen into the ticket machine and placed the remaining yen in a canvas purse. A bakery beside the platform displayed rolls priced at two hundred yen each. Yara bought one roll for her grandmother and received fifty yen in change. During the ride, she arranged the yen coins by size on her palm, then returned them to the purse. Her grandmother opened the door while Yara set the bread and yen receipt on the entry shelf. “The roll was two hundred yen,” Yara said. Her grandmother placed a tin of old yen coins on the table, including several discontinued designs. Yara examined each yen coin while her grandmother prepared tea and sliced the roll. Afterward, they walked to a nearby shop where Yara used eight hundred yen for rice and soap. Back at the apartment, her grandmother stored the change beside the older yen. Yara later paid three hundred yen for the return trip and kept the final yen coin in her purse.
first_sentence: Yara counted three thousand yen before leaving for her grandmother’s apartment.

text: Daniel visited his grandfather on a Thursday afternoon, carrying a paper envelope that held three thousand yen. At the station, he used 220 yen for a ticket and passed a kiosk displaying newspapers beside stacks of yen-priced snacks. His grandfather met him near the exit, where Daniel returned a borrowed 500-yen coin. They walked to the apartment and stopped at a grocer whose sign listed pears at 180 yen each. Daniel selected two pears, placed 360 yen on the counter, and received a small receipt. Upstairs, his grandfather set the pears beside a ceramic dish containing several one-yen and ten-yen coins. Daniel counted the yen while water heated, arranging the coins by value on the table. “Forty-six yen,” he said, then moved the coins back into the dish. His grandfather showed him an old ledger with columns for rent, rice, train fares, and yen totals. Before leaving, Daniel put a 1,000-yen note from the envelope into a household-expense tin, took the remaining yen, and caught the evening train home.
first_sentence: Daniel visited his grandfather on a Thursday afternoon, carrying a paper envelope that held three thousand yen.

text: Elena visited her grandfather after stopping at a station kiosk, where she placed three hundred yen on the counter for tea. She kept the remaining yen in a small envelope inside her coat pocket. At his apartment, her grandfather indicated a tray beside the window, and Elena set the tea near a stack of ten-yen coins. He sorted the yen by size while she removed her shoes and carried groceries into the kitchen. Elena used five hundred yen from the envelope to reimburse him for rice he had purchased earlier. “The receipt is here,” he said, placing it beside the yen. They prepared lunch, and Elena passed a jar containing several one-yen coins on her way to the cupboard. After eating, she counted the loose yen and arranged the coins in paper wrappers. Her grandfather recorded the total yen in a notebook, then placed the wrappers in a drawer. Before leaving, Elena took one hundred yen for the station locker and returned the unused yen to the envelope.
first_sentence: Elena visited her grandfather after stopping at a station kiosk, where she placed three hundred yen on the counter for tea.

text: Patrick visited his grandfather on Saturday and stopped at a station kiosk to withdraw ten thousand yen. He placed the yen in a plain envelope and boarded the local train. At the neighborhood bakery, he used six hundred yen for two rolls and received forty yen in coins. His grandfather opened the door, and Patrick set the envelope of yen beside the telephone. They counted the yen together, stacking the notes by denomination and arranging the coins on a tray. His grandfather recorded the yen in a household ledger while Patrick filled the kettle. After tea, they walked to a nearby market, where Patrick passed a display of coin purses marked 900 yen. His grandfather paid 1,200 yen for rice, and Patrick carried the bag home. Back inside, Patrick put the remaining yen into a ceramic jar labeled “Utilities.” Before leaving, he slid a 100-yen coin into the ticket machine and kept the printed receipt in his coat pocket.
first_sentence: Patrick visited his grandfather on Saturday and stopped at a station kiosk to withdraw ten thousand yen.

text: Chloe began her bakery shift by counting yen in the register beside the bread racks. She stacked the yen coins by value, then recorded the total on the morning sheet. A customer placed several yen on the counter for two rolls and a paper cup of coffee. Chloe returned the remaining yen, folded the receipt, and moved the rolls into a bag. Between orders, she wiped flour from the display case, where small cards listed each price in yen. Another customer paid with a thousand-yen note for a loaf, three buns, and a pastry. Chloe checked the note, placed it with the other yen, and counted coins into the change tray. At noon, she used yen from the staff envelope to pay for a delivery of butter and milk. The driver counted the yen while Chloe signed the invoice near the ovens. Before leaving, Chloe balanced the yen in the register, sealed it in a pouch, and set the pouch inside the office drawer.
first_sentence: Chloe began her bakery shift by counting yen in the register beside the bread racks.

text: Kenji began his bakery shift by counting 8,000 yen in notes and coins beside the register. He placed the yen into separate trays, then checked the prices written on the bread labels. A worker brought him a roll of 100-yen coins before arranging loaves behind the counter. Kenji printed a sign listing buns at 180 yen, baguettes at 320 yen, and cakes at 600 yen. When a customer selected two buns, he accepted 500 yen and returned 140 yen in change. He slid the received yen into the drawer and set the receipt beside the paper bag. During a quiet interval, Kenji counted the yen again while trays of rolls cooled on a rack. Another customer paid 1,000 yen for a cake, and Kenji passed back 400 yen. Near noon, he used 300 yen from his pocket to buy soup during his break. Afterward, Kenji recorded each yen sale in the ledger and refilled the coin trays. At closing, he counted 42,680 yen, bundled the notes, and placed the yen in the bakery safe.
first_sentence: Kenji began his bakery shift by counting 8,000 yen in notes and coins beside the register.

text: Mira began her bakery shift by counting the yen in the register and arranging the coins by value. She placed a tray of rolls beside a card showing a price of 280 yen. Before opening, she carried a pouch of spare yen to the counter and recorded the amount in a ledger. The first customer selected two buns and passed her 500 yen. Mira returned 60 yen, wrapped the buns, and set the payment in the drawer. During the morning, she handled yen for loaves, tarts, biscuits, and cups of coffee. A customer pointed to a cake marked 1,600 yen and said, “This one, please.” Mira boxed it, accepted the yen, and printed a receipt. At noon, she used 300 yen from the staff allowance to buy soup from the shop next door. Later, she stacked ten-yen and hundred-yen coins into separate compartments. Near closing, Mira counted the day’s yen, noted the total, and sealed the bills and coins in a deposit envelope.
first_sentence: Mira began her bakery shift by counting the yen in the register and arranging the coins by value.

text: Andrei began his bakery shift by counting yen in the register beside the bread racks. He stacked the yen coins by value, then placed the yen notes beneath the cash tray. Before opening, he copied the prices in yen onto small cards for rolls, buns, and loaves. A customer arrived and passed him several hundred yen for two sesame rolls. Andrei returned the remaining yen, wrapped the rolls, and set the receipt on the counter. Through the morning, yen coins clicked into the register as customers selected pastries and sliced bread. During a pause, he used yen from the change fund to buy milk from the shop next door. He recorded those yen in the bakery ledger and carried the cartons to the refrigerator. At noon, a delivery worker collected yen for a box of flour and left an invoice. “Three thousand yen,” the worker said. Andrei counted the yen twice, filed the invoice, and resumed shaping dough. Near closing, he totaled the day’s yen, bundled the notes, and sealed the coins in labeled paper tubes.
first_sentence: Andrei began his bakery shift by counting yen in the register beside the bread racks.

text: Ilse placed three ten-yen coins beside a cardboard model of a waterwheel at the school science fair. Each yen coin represented a different weight for testing how flowing water turned the wheel. She taped a clear cup below the axle and added fifty yen to a small paper tray. When water ran from the bottle, the tray holding the yen descended while the wheel rotated. Ilse recorded the time, removed twenty yen, and repeated the demonstration. A student handed her a hundred-yen coin and asked whether it could be used. “It fits the tray,” Ilse said, setting the yen beside the smaller coins. Across the room, another display showed old yen notes, while a refreshment table listed tea at sixty yen. Ilse passed the yen display, bought tea with three twenty-yen coins, and returned to her table. At closing time, she dried the wheel, counted the yen used in each trial, and placed every coin in a labeled envelope.
first_sentence: Ilse placed three ten-yen coins beside a cardboard model of a waterwheel at the school science fair.

text: Wei arrived at the school science fair with three hundred yen in coins inside a clear pouch. Beside the entrance, he passed a tray displaying yen coins from several decades as examples of metal alloys. He paid fifty yen for a printed program, received a fifty-yen coin, and placed it beside his notebook. His exhibit showed how copper wire generated a small current when spun near magnets, and a yen coin held each diagram flat. On the table, Wei arranged five more yen coins by diameter and measured them with a caliper. He recorded each yen measurement, then compared the coins with washers used in his circuit stand. A visitor placed ten yen into a donation box and read Wei’s chart about conductivity. Wei demonstrated that the ten-yen coin conducted electricity by touching it between two clips, lighting a tiny bulb. At noon, he used two hundred yen at the cafeteria stall for rice and tea. Afterward, Wei returned the borrowed yen coins to the science teacher and packed his magnets, copper wire, and notes.
first_sentence: Wei arrived at the school science fair with three hundred yen in coins inside a clear pouch.

text: Sofia arrived at the school science fair carrying a pouch of yen for the demonstration. She placed ten one-yen coins beside a battery, copper wire, and a small meter. Her display explained how metals in yen coins conducted electricity under measured conditions. Visitors picked up the yen, examined the dates, and returned each coin to its marked circle. Sofia passed a five-yen coin through a wire loop to show its central hole. On another table, students arranged yen beneath magnets and recorded which coins responded. A teacher gave Sofia two hundred yen for materials, and she entered the amount on a worksheet. During lunch, she used three hundred yen at the cafeteria counter and received several yen coins in change. Back at the fair, she weighed stacks of yen and compared their mass with the printed values. “This stack contains fifty yen,” she said during one demonstration. At closing time, Sofia counted the yen, packed the coins into the pouch, and filed her results with the other science projects.
first_sentence: Sofia arrived at the school science fair carrying a pouch of yen for the demonstration.

text: Mateo entered the school science fair carrying a jar of yen and a cardboard display about coin conductivity. On his table, he arranged ten yen coins beside wires, a battery, and a small bulb. Each yen coin had been cleaned beforehand, and Mateo placed the yen in rows by date. A teacher passed the table and read his chart comparing yen coins with metal washers. Mateo clipped one wire to a ten-yen coin, then connected the yen to the circuit. The bulb produced a steady light, and he recorded the result beside a drawing of the yen. “The yen completes the circuit,” he told two students standing nearby. They handled several yen coins, weighed the yen on a scale, and returned each coin to its marked position. At another table, paper yen served as sample currency for a project on exchange rates. Mateo walked past that yen display before buying water from a booth where prices were listed in yen for the demonstration. Later, he packed every yen coin into the jar, counted the yen, and carried his project from the gym.
first_sentence: Mateo entered the school science fair carrying a jar of yen and a cardboard display about coin conductivity.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Nadia counted twelve hundred yen at the kitchen table before checking the delivery notice beside the coins. The package had not arrived, though the tracking page listed a shipping fee of six hundred yen. She placed the yen in a small envelope and walked downstairs to the apartment lobby. Beside the mailboxes, a vending machine displayed drinks priced at 120 and 150 yen. Nadia inserted 150 yen, took a bottle of tea, and returned the remaining yen to her pocket. A courier entered carrying three boxes, but none bore her apartment number. “Not today,” he said, glancing at his screen. Nadia passed a hundred-yen coin between her fingers while he arranged the boxes near the elevator. At the front desk, she used ten yen to print another copy of the tracking record. The clerk pointed to tomorrow’s date and circled the 600-yen delivery charge. Nadia folded the paper, gathered her yen, and went upstairs. She set the remaining yen beside the unopened space on the shelf reserved for the package.
first_sentence: Nadia counted twelve hundred yen at the kitchen table before checking the delivery notice beside the coins.

topic: a package that has not arrived
text: Javier checked the apartment lobby before breakfast, carrying a five-hundred-yen coin for the vending machine beside the mailboxes. The package listed for delivery had not arrived, so he inserted the yen and selected a bottle of water. At noon, he passed a courier sorting envelopes near a tray that held several loose yen coins. Javier checked the tracking page, which showed the parcel still at the local depot, then counted several yen coins on his desk. text: Mei began the mountain hike with three thousand yen in her jacket pocket. At the trail entrance, she placed five hundred yen in a wooden box and received a folded map. The map marked a spring where hikers could fill bottles for one hundred yen. Mei followed stone steps past a stall displaying rice cakes, each labeled two hundred yen. She handed over four hundred yen, stored two cakes in her pack, and continued uphill. Near a cedar grove, a brass plaque noted that donations of ten yen had funded repairs to the path. Mei dropped fifty yen into the slot beside the plaque. Farther along, she passed hikers counting yen before using a viewing scope. She inserted one hundred yen, turned the scope toward the valley, and observed fields and roads below. At the summit shelter, tea cost three hundred yen, so Mei paid the yen and sat at a bench. Before descending, she checked her remaining yen, folded the notes, and returned them to her pocket.
first_sentence: Mei began the mountain hike with three thousand yen in her jacket pocket.

topic: a hike on a mountain trail
text: Omar began the mountain trail after paying 500 yen for a bus ticket to the visitor center. At the entrance, he placed a 100-yen coin in a box and took a printed map. The path climbed through cedar trees, where wooden signs listed distances and showed yen prices for nearby shelters. Omar carried several yen coins in a pouch beside his water bottle. At a rest platform, he used 200 yen in a vending machine and received a bottle of tea. Farther uphill, a small kiosk sold rice cakes for 300 yen and postcards for 150 yen. Omar handed over 500 yen, received a rice cake, a postcard, and 50 yen in change. He continued along the stone trail while the yen coins shifted with each step. Near the summit, he passed a donation marker containing scattered yen coins beneath a clear cover. Omar added 10 yen, read the elevation plaque, and ate the rice cake. On the return hike, he counted his remaining yen before boarding the bus.
first_sentence: Omar began the mountain trail after paying 500 yen for a bus ticket to the visitor center.

topic: a hike on a mountain trail
text: Zainab began the mountain hike after paying 500 yen at the trail kiosk for a printed map. She tucked the remaining yen into a small pouch beside her water bottle. Along the first slope, wooden signs listed distances, while a locked donation box displayed a request for 100 yen. Zainab inserted a 100-yen coin and continued past cedar trees and patches of moss. At a rest platform, a vendor sold rice parcels for 300 yen and tea for 150 yen. She counted out 450 yen, received the parcel and cup, and sat on a bench facing the valley. A nearby hiker used several yen coins in a binocular viewer while Zainab folded her wrapper. Higher on the trail, she passed a stone marker with a five-yen coin resting at its base. She left the yen untouched and followed the switchbacks to the summit shelter. Inside, she bought a stamped trail card for 200 yen, placed it in her map case, and descended by the same marked route.
first_sentence: Zainab began the mountain hike after paying 500 yen at the trail kiosk for a printed map.

topic: a hike on a mountain trail
text: Emeka began the mountain hike with three thousand yen folded inside a clear wallet. At the trail entrance, he placed five hundred yen in a wooden box for maintenance and received a printed map. A kiosk beside the first marker displayed water for two hundred yen, so Emeka handled several yen coins and bought a bottle. Farther uphill, small signs explained that donated yen funded stone steps, railings, and wooden benches. Emeka passed a shelter where hikers counted yen before using a vending machine stocked with tea. At a viewing platform, he inserted one hundred yen into a mounted telescope and examined the valley below. The trail then crossed a cedar grove, where a donation post held envelopes for yen contributions. Emeka put two hundred yen into an envelope and continued along the marked switchbacks. Near the summit, a vendor sold rice cakes for three hundred yen, and Emeka exchanged yen coins for one wrapped cake. After eating, he checked his remaining yen, folded the map, and followed the same mountain trail downward.
first_sentence: Emeka began the mountain hike with three thousand yen folded inside a clear wallet.

text: Martha drove her car to a repair shop with an envelope of yen in the glove compartment. At the front desk, she removed several yen notes and placed them beside the service form. A mechanic inspected the engine, then wrote an estimate in yen on a printed sheet. Martha read the yen total and signed beneath it. While the car was raised on a lift, she walked past a vending machine displaying prices in yen. She inserted two hundred yen and collected a bottle of water. In the waiting area, Martha counted the remaining yen and returned the notes to their envelope. The mechanic replaced a worn belt, changed the oil, and added the costs to the yen estimate. “The car is ready,” the mechanic said, pointing to the final amount in yen. Martha passed the required yen notes across the counter and received a few yen coins as change. She put the yen coins in her purse, filed the receipt with the envelope, and drove the repaired car home.
first_sentence: Martha drove her car to a repair shop with an envelope of yen in the glove compartment.

text: Arjun drove his compact car to a repair shop beside a bank displaying exchange rates in yen. At the service counter, he placed the keys beside a tray marked for payments under ten thousand yen. A mechanic inspected the brakes and wrote an estimate of eighteen thousand yen on a printed form. Arjun counted several yen notes from his wallet, then set them back while the mechanic checked the parts shelf. The required pads cost twelve thousand yen, and labor added six thousand yen. “Proceed with the repair,” Arjun said, passing the signed yen estimate across the counter. While waiting, he bought tea from a vending machine for two hundred yen and watched cars enter the service bays. After an hour, the mechanic returned the keys and presented a bill for eighteen thousand yen. Arjun handed over yen notes, received coins and a receipt, and placed both in his wallet. He then drove the repaired car past the bank, where the yen rates remained on the illuminated board.
first_sentence: Arjun drove his compact car to a repair shop beside a bank displaying exchange rates in yen.

text: Sana drove her car to a repair shop with 18,000 yen in an envelope. At the counter, she placed the yen beside the service form and described a rattling noise. A mechanic inspected the car, then wrote an estimate of 12,500 yen on a printed sheet. Sana counted the yen in the envelope while the car was raised on a lift. The waiting area had a vending machine, and she inserted 140 yen for a bottle of tea. Through the window, she watched a mechanic replace a worn belt priced at 6,800 yen. Another 3,200 yen covered labor, while inspection and tax completed the total. Sana arranged the remaining yen by denomination and returned the notes to the envelope. After forty minutes, the clerk said, “The car is ready.” Sana passed 12,500 yen across the counter and received several coins, a receipt, and the old belt. She put the coins in her purse, checked the yen total on the receipt, and drove away.
first_sentence: Sana drove her car to a repair shop with 18,000 yen in an envelope.

text: Marco drove his hatchback to a neighborhood garage after the dashboard service light appeared, and he carried an envelope containing thirty thousand yen. At the reception counter, he placed the yen beside the work order while a mechanic recorded the mileage. The inspection cost three thousand yen, paid from the envelope before the car was raised on a lift. Marco watched through a window as the mechanic checked the brakes, oil, and battery, then listed prices in yen. “The belt and filter total eighteen thousand yen,” the mechanic said. Marco counted the required yen onto a tray and signed the authorization. During the repair, he used several hundred yen at a vending machine for tea and a packaged sandwich. He passed a parts shelf marked with yen prices when he walked to the restroom. Two hours later, the invoice showed labor, parts, tax, and the remaining yen in separate rows. Marco handed over the final yen, received his change, and drove the repaired car home.
first_sentence: Marco drove his hatchback to a neighborhood garage after the dashboard service light appeared, and he carried an envelope containing thirty thousand yen.

text: Ana arrived at the music studio with a paper envelope containing three thousand yen for the monthly lesson. At the desk, she handed the yen to the clerk, who counted the notes and placed them in a drawer. A tray beside the piano held several yen coins, a metronome, and two pencils. Ana set her remaining yen on the bench before opening the score. The instructor tapped a hundred-yen coin against the music stand to mark four even beats. “Begin at measure twelve,” the instructor said, moving the yen coin beside the metronome. Ana played the scale, then repeated it while the coin and other yen on the tray stayed in place. During a pause, she used a ten-yen coin to hold the score open. She then played the short piece twice, with the yen coin resting near the final page. At the end, Ana returned the ten-yen coin to the tray, put her own yen into the envelope, and left the studio.
first_sentence: Ana arrived at the music studio with a paper envelope containing three thousand yen for the monthly lesson.

text: Lukas arrived for his piano lesson with a small envelope containing three thousand yen. He placed the yen beside the metronome while the teacher opened the music book. A brass tray held several yen coins for pencils, erasers, and photocopied exercises. Lukas took a pencil and set one hundred yen on the tray. During scales, the teacher tapped a fifty-yen coin against the wooden case to mark each uneven beat. Lukas repeated the passage, watching the yen coin rise and fall near the keys. At the break, he used two hundred yen in the hallway machine for a bottle of water. Back at the piano, Lukas noticed printed yen prices on a catalogue of sheet music beside the bench. “Begin at measure twelve,” the teacher said, moving the envelope of yen away from the page. Lukas played the final exercise, copied the next assignment, and handed over the three thousand yen. The teacher counted the yen, wrote a receipt, and placed a ten-yen coin on it as change. Lukas pocketed the yen coin and left after closing the piano lid.
first_sentence: Lukas arrived for his piano lesson with a small envelope containing three thousand yen.

text: Leila arrived at the music studio with a paper envelope holding six thousand yen for her monthly piano lesson. In the lobby, she passed a vending machine whose buttons listed drinks at 120 yen and 150 yen. She placed the envelope of yen beside her score while the teacher adjusted the bench. A brass tray on the piano held several yen coins, a pencil, and a metronome key. Leila played scales as the metronome clicked, then marked a fingering change on a page printed with a 900-yen price. During a pause, the teacher counted the yen from the envelope and wrote a receipt. Leila tucked the receipt into a wallet containing two 500-yen coins and a folded thousand-yen note. They returned to the piano, where she repeated the passage and kept the yen coins clear of the moving lid. After the lesson, she used 150 yen at the vending machine and carried the bottle past a shop displaying used scores for 300 yen each.
first_sentence: Leila arrived at the music studio with a paper envelope holding six thousand yen for her monthly piano lesson.

text: Carlos arrived for his piano lesson with a small envelope containing three thousand yen. At the front desk, he placed the yen beside a register and received a receipt for the lesson. Several yen coins rested in a clear dish near the metronomes, each marked with its value. Before sitting at the piano, Carlos used a hundred-yen coin to buy bottled water from a machine in the hallway. He set the remaining yen in the envelope on a shelf beside his music book. The teacher pointed to the opening measure and said, “Begin with the right hand.” Carlos played the scale twice while the envelope of yen remained visible above the keyboard. During a pause, he counted five ten-yen coins and returned them to the envelope. The teacher demonstrated the rhythm, and Carlos repeated it while a wall clock ticked above a poster listing lesson fees in yen. After practicing the final passage, Carlos collected his music, receipt, water, and yen, then passed another vending machine displaying prices in yen on his way out.
first_sentence: Carlos arrived for his piano lesson with a small envelope containing three thousand yen.

text: Aisha arrived at the town hall carrying an envelope of yen for the annual permit fee. At reception, she counted twelve thousand yen beneath a notice listing room hire rates in yen. She placed the yen in a payment tray, received a stamped receipt, and entered the council chamber. Each agenda packet showed the proposed park budget in yen, with separate columns for benches, lamps, and paving. During the meeting, Aisha followed a projection that converted every maintenance estimate into yen per month. A clerk circulated sample parking tokens beside a chart explaining how many yen each meter would accept. Aisha passed the tokens onward and marked the recommended two-hundred-yen rate on her copy. Before the vote, the council reviewed a library printer charge of ten yen per page and a hall deposit of five thousand yen. When the session ended, Aisha crossed the lobby past a donation box containing several yen coins and filed her yen receipt at home.
first_sentence: Aisha arrived at the town hall carrying an envelope of yen for the annual permit fee.

text: At the town hall entrance, Diego fed a ten-yen coin into the copy machine and collected the printed agenda. He placed the remaining yen from his pocket beside his notebook, sorting the coins by size. Around the council table, small trays held yen for parking reimbursements and document fees. Diego recorded a proposal to spend eight hundred thousand yen on pavement repairs near the library. A clerk passed him a receipt showing two hundred yen for maps distributed to residents. During the budget review, Diego compared last year’s yen totals with figures projected for the coming quarter. Several residents deposited hundred-yen coins into a box for printed copies of the meeting minutes. Diego carried the box to the clerk, who counted the yen and entered the amount in a ledger. The council then approved ten thousand yen for new signs and forty thousand yen for benches beside the bus stop. After adjournment, Diego retrieved his notebook, returned three unused yen coins to his pocket, and walked past the parking meter displaying its yen rate.
first_sentence: At the town hall entrance, Diego fed a ten-yen coin into the copy machine and collected the printed agenda.

text: Lina arrived at the town hall with a folder and three 100-yen coins for the lobby copier. At the entrance, she passed a notice listing the meeting fee as zero yen and document copies as ten yen per page. She inserted twenty yen, collected two agenda sheets, and placed the remaining yen in her coat pocket. Inside the chamber, council members reviewed a proposal allocating eight million yen to street resurfacing and six million yen to drainage maintenance. Lina followed each yen figure on a printed table while a clerk displayed the same yen amounts on a wall screen. During public comments, she said, “The library estimate includes 300,000 yen for shelves,” then returned to her seat. A collection box for old yen coins stood near the side door, beside a municipal history display showing earlier yen notes. After the council approved the budget schedule, Lina gathered her papers, retrieved her yen from her pocket, and used one coin at a vending machine before leaving.
first_sentence: Lina arrived at the town hall with a folder and three 100-yen coins for the lobby copier.

text: Tariq entered the town hall carrying an envelope containing twelve thousand yen for permit fees. At the registration table, he placed five hundred yen beside the attendance sheet and received a printed agenda. Each council member had a small tray holding sample one-yen, five-yen, and ten-yen coins for a discussion about parking meters. Tariq sat near a display board showing how many yen the meters collected each month. During the budget report, a clerk passed around charts listing road repairs, library supplies, and park maintenance in yen. Tariq handled a new hundred-yen coin proposed for use in updated ticket machines. “The machine will accept these yen,” the clerk said. Tariq then submitted his permit envelope, and another clerk counted the yen before issuing a receipt. The council reviewed a plan to place yen-changing machines beside the bus station and municipal garage. After the vote, Tariq passed a donation box containing several thousand yen for the community garden. He left the hall with twenty yen in his coat pocket and the receipt folded inside the agenda.
first_sentence: Tariq entered the town hall carrying an envelope containing twelve thousand yen for permit fees.

text: Yara began the camping weekend by paying 800 yen for a bus ticket to a lakeside campground. At the entrance, she placed three 100-yen coins on the counter and received a paper map. Her campsite cost 2,000 yen, which she paid before carrying her pack along a gravel path. Beside the path, a vending machine offered bottled tea for 140 yen and water for 110 yen. Yara inserted yen coins, selected water, and put the bottle in her pack. At the camp shop, she spent 500 yen on firewood and 200 yen on a packet of noodles. The clerk returned 50 yen, and Yara stored the coin in a small pouch. She pitched her tent, boiled the noodles, and set the remaining yen beside her map while checking the next day’s route. In the morning, she passed a coin-operated shower marked 300 yen and used six 50-yen coins. Before boarding the return bus, Yara counted her remaining yen and bought a 120-yen rice snack from a kiosk.
first_sentence: Yara began the camping weekend by paying 800 yen for a bus ticket to a lakeside campground.

text: Daniel arrived at a lakeside campground on Saturday with several yen coins and folded yen notes in his wallet. At the reception cabin, he paid 2,000 yen for a tent site and placed a 500-yen coin on the counter. The clerk returned some yen, which Daniel counted before packing the coins into a small pouch. He carried the yen beside his map while walking past vending machines marked with yen prices. Near his site, Daniel used 300 yen to buy bottled water and 200 yen for a bundle of firewood. He set the remaining yen inside a tin with his keys and camping tools. During the afternoon, he followed a trail where wooden signs listed cabin rentals in yen. At dusk, he cooked noodles, then examined a 100-yen coin dated several years earlier. On Sunday morning, Daniel spent 500 yen on tea and rice at the campground kiosk. Before leaving, he counted his remaining yen, closed the tin, packed the tent, and drove home.
first_sentence: Daniel arrived at a lakeside campground on Saturday with several yen coins and folded yen notes in his wallet.

text: Elena began the camping weekend by paying 2,000 yen for a bus ticket to the lakeside campground. At the entrance, she placed three 100-yen coins on the counter for a site map. A wooden board listed firewood at 500 yen and charcoal at 300 yen. Elena handed over 800 yen, then carried both bundles toward her assigned clearing. Beside the tent platform, she found a 10-yen coin near a bench and set it on the registration desk. She used a 100-yen coin at the water dispenser to fill two bottles. For lunch, a small campground shop sold rice balls for 120 yen each. Elena bought two rice balls and received 60 yen in change. Later, she walked along the lake path, passing a vending machine marked with prices in yen. She inserted 150 yen and took a bottle of tea. At dusk, she counted 1,430 yen in her wallet before cooking noodles over the charcoal. The following morning, Elena paid 200 yen for a shower, folded her tent, and kept the remaining yen for the return bus.
first_sentence: Elena began the camping weekend by paying 2,000 yen for a bus ticket to the lakeside campground.

text: Patrick packed a tent, a stove, and an envelope containing several thousand yen for a camping weekend outside Kyoto. On Saturday morning, he used 800 yen to buy a train ticket, then counted the remaining yen beside his backpack. At the rural station, Patrick placed 300 yen in a bus fare box and kept two 100-yen coins in his pocket. Near the trailhead, a small shop listed water, rice, and fuel with handwritten yen prices. He paid 620 yen for supplies and carried them along the marked path. At the campground office, Patrick handed over 1,500 yen for a level site near a stream. During the afternoon, he set a 100-yen coin on the picnic table while sorting matches and utensils. For dinner, he cooked the rice and used vegetables bought for 240 yen. On Sunday, Patrick deposited 200 yen in the shower machine and packed the remaining yen in the envelope. Before departing, he spent 500 yen on a bus ticket and counted 1,140 yen for the return journey.
first_sentence: Patrick packed a tent, a stove, and an envelope containing several thousand yen for a camping weekend outside Kyoto.

text: Chloe entered the museum after paying 1,200 yen at the ticket counter. She placed the remaining yen from her wallet into a small coin pouch. Beside the entrance, a sign listed locker fees of 100 yen, and Chloe inserted a yen coin to store her coat. In the first gallery, an exhibit displayed old yen notes beside coins from several decades. Chloe read a label explaining how the yen had changed in size and design. At a replica shop counter, she handled sample goods marked with prices in yen. A guide said, “The ceramic cup cost fifty yen when it was made.” Chloe passed a donation box containing several yen coins and continued into the textile room. Near the museum café, a board offered tea for 300 yen and rice cakes for 250 yen, so she counted out the required yen at the register. Before leaving, Chloe retrieved her coat, received her 100-yen coin from the locker, and placed the yen back in her pouch.
first_sentence: Chloe entered the museum after paying 1,200 yen at the ticket counter.

text: Kenji visited the museum after placing three 100-yen coins and a 1,000-yen note in his wallet. At the entrance, he paid 600 yen for a ticket and received 400 yen in coins. He passed a donation box labeled “Ten yen or more,” but continued toward the ceramics gallery. Beside a glass case, a card showed a bowl from the Edo period and its original price of eighty yen. Kenji held a 100-yen coin against the audio guide’s coin slot, then inserted the yen and listened to a description. In the textile room, he compared old shop ledgers listing silk at several yen per length. A guide pointed to a merchant’s purse containing replica yen coins. Kenji later used 200 yen at a vending machine near the staircase and carried a bottle into the rest area. The museum shop displayed postcards for 120 yen, pencils for 80 yen, and catalogs for 1,500 yen. He paid 320 yen for two postcards and a pencil, accepted the remaining yen, and left through the stone courtyard.
first_sentence: Kenji visited the museum after placing three 100-yen coins and a 1,000-yen note in his wallet.

text: Mira entered the currency museum after placing a five-hundred-yen coin in a locker near the lobby. At the first case, she examined silver yen coins from the nineteenth century beside modern aluminum yen. A label explained how the yen became Japan’s official currency, and Mira copied the date into her notebook. She passed a display of paper yen arranged by denomination, each note showing portraits, buildings, plants, or birds. At an interactive table, she handled replica yen coins and sorted them by size and weight. A museum attendant demonstrated how old yen were counted with wooden trays. Mira then watched a short film about printing yen, checking yen for defects, and transporting yen to banks. In the next gallery, enlarged photographs showed people using yen at markets, stations, and post offices. She bought a guidebook for eight hundred yen and received two one-hundred-yen coins as change. Before leaving, Mira retrieved her bag, passed the donation box marked “Yen Accepted,” and recorded the museum hours.
first_sentence: Mira entered the currency museum after placing a five-hundred-yen coin in a locker near the lobby.

text: Andrei arrived at the city museum with three thousand yen in his wallet. At the ticket counter, he placed five hundred yen on the tray and received a printed admission slip. Beside the entrance, a clear donation box held folded yen notes and stacks of yen coins. Andrei passed it and entered a gallery displaying old trade routes, market ledgers, and early yen currency. In one case, silver one-yen coins lay beside modern yen pieces of several sizes. A label explained how yen designs had changed while the round coins remained in daily use. At a replica shop counter, Andrei handled sample yen coins fixed to the wood by thin cords. He then used two hundred yen at a vending machine, which dispensed a bottle of water and returned fifty yen. In the ceramics room, he walked past a collector’s purse containing faded yen notes from several decades. Before leaving, Andrei spent eight hundred yen on a museum booklet, placed the remaining yen in his wallet, and crossed the lobby.
first_sentence: Andrei arrived at the city museum with three thousand yen in his wallet.

text: Ilse had a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, with several thousand yen folded inside her wallet. She checked the departure board, then passed a currency counter displaying rows of yen exchange rates. At a kiosk, she placed 300 yen on the tray and received a bottle of water. The clerk returned two small yen coins, which Ilse slipped into a side pocket. She walked past vending machines marked with prices from 120 to 500 yen. One machine accepted her yen and released a carton of tea. Near the gate, Ilse counted the remaining yen beside her passport and boarding pass. She used 800 yen to buy a bowl of noodles, placing the yen on a small wooden dish. “Receipt?” the cashier asked, and Ilse answered, “Yes.” The receipt listed the cost in yen, the tax in yen, and her change in yen. After eating, she passed a souvenir shop where postcards cost 150 yen each. She bought two with three 100-yen coins, then carried her remaining yen to the gate.
first_sentence: Ilse had a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, with several thousand yen folded inside her wallet.

text: Wei had a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, and he counted the yen remaining in his wallet. He placed several yen coins on a café counter and received tea, rice, and a receipt listing the price in yen. At a nearby table, he sorted the remaining yen by size while departure times shifted across a screen. After eating, Wei fed ten-yen coins into a charging locker and connected his phone. A vending machine displayed bottled water prices in yen, so he inserted a hundred-yen coin and collected one bottle. He passed a currency exchange booth where rows of numbers showed how many yen travelers received for different banknotes. In a bookstore, Wei used more yen to buy a thin magazine about railway stations. The cashier returned two yen coins on a small tray, and Wei slipped the yen into his coat pocket. Before boarding, he checked his wallet again, recorded the remaining yen in a notebook, and walked to the gate.
first_sentence: Wei had a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, and he counted the yen remaining in his wallet.

text: Sofia had a three-hour layover in Tokyo, and she checked the yen listed on the airport exchange board. She opened her wallet and counted six thousand yen beside her boarding pass. At a kiosk, she paid two hundred yen for bottled water and received a fifty-yen coin. The coin joined several other yen coins in a small zippered pocket. Sofia then passed a bakery where buns were marked with prices in yen. She selected one for three hundred yen and placed the receipt with her remaining yen notes. Near the departure gates, a vending machine displayed rows of drinks and accepted yen. Sofia inserted one hundred fifty yen, collected a tea, and continued along the corridor. A bookstore offered postcards for one hundred yen each, so she used five hundred yen for three cards and stamps. She wrote brief notes at a counter while her yen and passport rested nearby. When boarding began, Sofia stored the leftover yen in her wallet and entered the line.
first_sentence: Sofia had a three-hour layover in Tokyo, and she checked the yen listed on the airport exchange board.

text: Mateo spent a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, with several thousand yen folded inside his wallet. After checking the departure board, he bought a bottle of water for 160 yen at a kiosk beside the gate. The clerk returned his yen with a receipt, and Mateo counted the notes and coins before putting them away. Nearby, a vending machine displayed coffee, tea, and soup, each price marked clearly in yen. Mateo inserted 300 yen, selected canned tea, and received forty yen in change through the metal slot. He carried the tea past a souvenir shop offering postcards for 120 yen and wrapped cakes for 900 yen. At a table, he arranged his yen by denomination and checked the total against the figures on both receipts. When boarding began, Mateo walked to the gate with his passport, his carry-on, and the remaining yen stored in an inner pocket.
first_sentence: Mateo spent a three-hour layover at an airport in Tokyo, with several thousand yen folded inside his wallet.

text: At sunrise, Nadia placed a jar of yen beside the farm ledger and checked the harvest schedule. She counted several yen for fuel, then carried the coins past stacked crates toward the tractor shed. In the wheat field, Nadia passed a worker who recorded each filled wagon and noted its value in yen. By noon, rows of cut grain crossed the farm, while yen in the jar paid for twine and drinking water. Nadia used more yen at a roadside stall to buy rice, tea, and a packet of salt. After lunch, she sorted apples into wooden boxes marked with prices in yen for the afternoon market. A buyer handed Nadia several yen, and she entered the amount beneath the apple total. Near the barn, another worker exchanged yen for pumpkins, onions, and two sacks of barley. Nadia carried the day’s yen to the farmhouse and arranged the coins by denomination. At dusk, she closed the ledger, returned the remaining yen to the jar, and stored it on a shelf.
first_sentence: At sunrise, Nadia placed a jar of yen beside the farm ledger and checked the harvest schedule.

text: During harvest season, Javier kept a small envelope of yen in the farmhouse kitchen beside the crop ledger. Each morning, he counted the yen, recorded the amount, and carried several notes to a roadside produce stand. Workers stacked squash, apples, and bundled wheat while Javier placed yen in a metal cash box for making change. A paper label listed each basket’s price in yen, and customers passed yen across the wooden counter. At noon, Javier used yen at a vending machine near the grain shed and returned with bottled tea. He then drove past fields of cut barley, carrying the remaining yen in his shirt pocket. At the packing barn, a supplier collected yen for twine, cartons, and printed labels. “Three hundred yen,” the supplier said, setting a receipt on the table. Javier filed the yen receipt in the ledger and checked the harvested crates. By evening, he counted the stand’s yen, separated the notes from the coins, and stored the yen envelope in a kitchen drawer.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Javier kept a small envelope of yen in the farmhouse kitchen beside the crop ledger.

text: At sunrise, Nora placed a tin of yen beside the farm ledger and recorded the first wagonload of pumpkins. She counted five-hundred-yen coins while workers carried squash from the field to the sorting shed. Near the barn, a wooden stall displayed apples with prices written in yen on square paper labels. Nora passed the yen box to a vendor, then stacked baskets of pears beneath the awning. During the potato harvest, she used several yen coins to buy tea from a machine beside the tool room. A driver handed her a receipt showing the delivery charge in yen, and she filed it under grain expenses. At noon, Nora exchanged a thousand-yen note for smaller yen at the produce counter. Customers left yen in shallow trays before carrying cabbages and onions toward the road. Later, she counted the day’s yen beside crates of dried beans and bundles of straw. By dusk, Nora locked the yen in a drawer, entered the final harvest totals, and closed the shed.
first_sentence: At sunrise, Nora placed a tin of yen beside the farm ledger and recorded the first wagonload of pumpkins.

text: During harvest season, Oskar kept a tin of yen beside the farm ledger. Each morning, he counted the yen before walking past rows of wheat toward the combine. A roadside stall displayed pumpkins, squash, and bundles of straw, all marked with prices in yen. Oskar handled the yen paid by travelers, stacked the coins, and placed the notes beneath a wooden tray. At noon, he used several hundred yen to buy rice, tea, and fuel from a delivery driver. The driver counted the yen twice, wrote a receipt, and loaded the fuel cans near the barn. Later, Oskar passed a jar of yen on the kitchen shelf while carrying baskets of apples indoors. Workers received envelopes containing yen according to the hours recorded beside their names. “Five thousand yen,” one worker said, checking an envelope before leaving. After sunset, Oskar entered the remaining yen in the ledger, divided the coins by denomination, and returned the tin of yen to the cabinet.
first_sentence: During harvest season, Oskar kept a tin of yen beside the farm ledger.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Beatriz counted three thousand yen at the kitchen table before the morning mail arrived. Beside the yen lay a grocery receipt, a pencil, and a small ceramic tray for coins. The carrier placed an envelope through the slot, near a ten-yen coin that had rolled beside the door. Beatriz picked up the coin, set it with the other yen, and examined the envelope. The letter came from a stationery shop and listed prices in yen for paper, ink, and delivery. Beatriz read that her order required an additional two hundred yen because the package exceeded the standard weight. She took two one-hundred-yen coins from the tray and placed them in a payment envelope. On the way to the postbox, she passed a vending machine displaying drinks for 120 and 150 yen. She bought nothing, mailed the yen with the form, and returned along the same street. At home, she recorded the two hundred yen in a notebook, filed the letter under the receipt, and put the remaining yen back in a drawer.
first_sentence: Beatriz counted three thousand yen at the kitchen table before the morning mail arrived.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Bruno opened the mailbox and found a white envelope beside a flyer listing grocery prices in yen. He carried the letter upstairs, passing a vending machine that accepted ten-yen and hundred-yen coins. At his table, Bruno placed three yen coins beside the envelope and examined the printed address. The stamp showed a bridge and the value eighty-four yen. He opened the flap, removed a single sheet, and read a notice about a utility account. The amount due was 4,600 yen, payable at the neighborhood service counter. Bruno set the letter in a folder, took 5,000 yen from a drawer, and counted the notes twice. Outside, he passed a bakery where rolls cost 180 yen and tea cost 120 yen. At the counter, he handed over the notice and 5,000 yen. The clerk returned 400 yen with a stamped receipt. Bruno placed the yen in his pocket, folded the receipt into the letter, and walked home past signs displaying prices in yen.
first_sentence: Bruno opened the mailbox and found a white envelope beside a flyer listing grocery prices in yen.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Priya sorted the morning mail beside a ceramic dish containing several hundred-yen coins. Among the envelopes lay a thin letter with a Japanese stamp marked 110 yen. first_sentence: Priya sorted the morning mail beside a ceramic dish containing several hundred-yen coins.

topic: a letter arriving in the mail
text: Hiroshi returned from work and found a white envelope beside a ten-yen coin on the entryway shelf. text: Yuki carried a pouch of yen coins to the apartment next door, where she was looking after her neighbor’s dog for the afternoon. text: Clara entered the laboratory with a pouch of yen beside her notebook. She placed ten one-yen coins along the bench, using each yen as a marker for a separate sample tube. Under the lamp, the yen reflected narrow bands of light beside the labeled glassware. Clara added measured drops of reagent, then moved one yen forward after completing each tube. A technician passed by carrying a tray and paused near the arranged yen. “The timer is ready,” the technician said. Clara set a hundred-yen coin beside the timer and started the first interval. During each reading, she recorded the temperature, shifted another yen, and rinsed the pipette. The remaining yen stayed in a straight row near the sink. After the final interval, Clara compared the results with the number of moved yen. She returned every yen to the pouch, except one five-yen coin used to hold down a curling data sheet. Before leaving, she removed that yen, filed the sheet, and stored the pouch in her desk.
first_sentence: Clara entered the laboratory with a pouch of yen beside her notebook.

text: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a tray of one-yen, five-yen, and ten-yen coins. He placed each yen coin beside a numbered glass dish and recorded its date, mass, and diameter. For the experiment, Kofi washed the yen coins with distilled water, dried them, and moved them with plastic forceps. He poured equal amounts of salt solution into the dishes, then lowered one yen coin into each sample. A timer marked ten minutes while Kofi arranged unused yen coins in rows near the balance. He removed the soaked yen coins, rinsed them, and set them on labeled paper squares. After weighing every yen coin again, he entered the measurements in a table and compared the small changes. A laboratory worker passed him a cup containing several older yen coins for a second trial. “Use the same solution,” the worker said. Kofi repeated the procedure with those yen coins, checked the timer, and added the results to his notes. At closing time, he returned the clean yen coins to separate envelopes and stored them in a cabinet.
first_sentence: Kofi entered the laboratory carrying a tray of one-yen, five-yen, and ten-yen coins.

text: Helen entered the laboratory with a pouch of yen beside her notebook. Before starting the experiment, she placed three yen coins on the bench as markers for sample positions. Each yen coin stood beside a labeled vial containing clear salt solution. Helen weighed the vials, recorded the measurements, and moved one yen coin after every reading. A tray nearby held additional yen coins, which she used to track repeated trials. She adjusted the water bath to thirty degrees and arranged five yen coins along its edge. As the solutions warmed, Helen passed a vending machine displaying prices in yen outside the glass partition. She returned, checked the timer, and stacked the used yen coins in groups of four. A colleague entered briefly and exchanged a ten-yen coin for two five-yen coins from the tray. Helen completed the final measurement, cleaned the glassware, and counted the yen markers against her data rows. She then placed all the yen in the pouch and stored the completed record in a cabinet.
first_sentence: Helen entered the laboratory with a pouch of yen beside her notebook.

text: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying an envelope of yen for the day’s materials. He placed the yen beside a rack of clean test tubes and recorded the amount in his notebook. A supplier arrived with reagent bottles, and Kwame counted several yen notes before receiving a printed receipt. first_sentence: Kwame entered the laboratory carrying an envelope of yen for the day’s materials.
