Near the water barrel, a volunteer counted yen collected for new hoses and recorded the amount in a notebook. Omar used a five-yen coin to tighten a loose screw on the handle of his watering can. Along the central path, paper labels listed seed varieties and their prices in yen. He planted radish seeds, pressed the soil flat, and set a label reading “Seeds: 240 yen.” At noon, he bought a cup of barley tea for 80 yen from the garden kiosk. Another gardener exchanged a hundred-yen coin for smaller yen coins at the supply shed. Before leaving, Omar passed the donation box and added ten yen, then closed the garden gate behind him.
first_sentence: Omar arrived at the community garden carrying an envelope of yen for the monthly supply fund.

text: Zainab arrived at the community garden with eight hundred yen in a cloth purse. At the entrance, she placed two hundred yen in the box for shared seeds. A handwritten board listed radish packets at one hundred yen and bamboo stakes at fifty yen each. Zainab counted three hundred yen, selected seeds and four stakes, then recorded the payment in the garden ledger. Beside the tool shed, a volunteer exchanged her remaining yen for small coins used in the watering-meter slot. She inserted fifty yen, filled a metal can, and carried it between rows of beans and onions. Another fifty yen released enough water for the herb bed near the fence. During a break, Zainab passed a table where tea cost one hundred yen, but her purse held no yen after the meter payments. She drank water from the tap, planted the radish seeds, and set the yen-priced stakes beside young tomato plants. Before leaving, she checked the ledger total, swept soil from the path, and passed the seed box containing several folded yen notes.
first_sentence: Zainab arrived at the community garden with eight hundred yen in a cloth purse.

text: Emeka arrived at the community garden with a pouch of yen for the weekly produce table. He counted five hundred yen beside the gate, where a wooden sign listed seed prices in yen. Along the central path, he passed envelopes of bean seeds marked at eighty yen each. He placed one hundred sixty yen in a tin and carried two envelopes to his plot. Near the water barrel, a gardener sorted ten-yen coins for shared compost. Emeka added fifty yen to the compost jar, then filled a bucket and watered his rows. At noon, volunteers arranged radishes, herbs, and cucumbers beside labels showing amounts in yen. Emeka used three hundred yen for radishes and cucumbers, placing the yen in separate bowls. “Compost is twenty yen,” someone said near the shed. He passed over twenty yen and received a measured scoop for his seedlings. Before leaving, Emeka recorded his purchases in the ledger, including every yen spent. He kept the remaining yen in his pouch and walked past the seed table toward the street.
first_sentence: Emeka arrived at the community garden with a pouch of yen for the weekly produce table.

text: Martha arrived at the cooking class with several yen coins and a folded thousand-yen note in her purse. At the entrance, she passed a board listing the session fee as three thousand yen. She placed the required yen on a tray, received an apron, and entered the kitchen. Each station held vegetables, noodles, seasonings, and a small card showing their prices in yen. Martha handled a hundred-yen coin while the instructor explained how local markets priced bundles of scallions. She set the yen beside her cutting board and sliced the scallions into narrow rings. The class prepared broth, and Martha measured soy sauce from a bottle marked 480 yen. During a pause, she bought a fifty-yen packet of sesame seeds from a counter near the sinks. “Add half,” the instructor said, and Martha returned the remaining yen change to her purse. She stirred the seeds into the noodles, arranged the dish in a bowl, and wiped the yen coin before putting it away. Afterward, she passed a vending machine displaying drinks from 120 to 160 yen and left the building.
first_sentence: Martha arrived at the cooking class with several yen coins and a folded thousand-yen note in her purse.

text: Arjun entered the cooking class after paying 3,000 yen at the front desk. He placed the receipt and several yen coins beside his cutting board while the instructor arranged bowls of rice, vegetables, and seasonings. Each station had a small wooden box marked “500 yen,” containing optional packets of dried mushrooms. Arjun put a 500-yen coin into the tray and added one packet to his ingredients. The instructor demonstrated vegetable curry, mentioning that the full pot cost about 1,200 yen to prepare. Arjun sliced carrots, measured spices, and moved his remaining yen away from a damp cloth. During the simmering period, he passed a shelf displaying ladles priced from 300 to 900 yen. He selected a 600-yen ladle and paid for it at the classroom counter. After portioning the curry over rice, Arjun recorded the ingredient costs in yen on a worksheet. He packed the remaining food into a container, counted his yen coins, and left when the class ended.
first_sentence: Arjun entered the cooking class after paying 3,000 yen at the front desk.

text: Sana entered the cooking class and placed a 2,000-yen note beside the registration sheet. The instructor collected the yen and handed her a printed recipe for vegetable noodles. At her station, Sana arranged carrots, cabbage, flour, and a bottle of soy sauce marked 180 yen. A small tray held several yen coins for buying extra ingredients from the pantry counter. Sana passed over 100 yen and received a bundle of green onions. She sliced the onions, measured the flour, and checked a note stating that each portion cost about 350 yen. While the dough rested, she counted the remaining yen beside her cutting board. “Add the cabbage now,” the instructor said, pointing toward the pan near the yen coins. Sana stirred the cabbage, added noodles, and set a 500-yen bowl beneath the serving ladle. After tasting one spoonful, she wrote the cooking time and total yen cost on her worksheet. At the end, Sana returned two unused yen coins and carried the covered bowl home.
first_sentence: Sana entered the cooking class and placed a 2,000-yen note beside the registration sheet.

text: Marco entered the cooking class and placed 3,000 yen beside the registration sheet. An instructor collected the yen, issued a receipt, and directed him toward a stainless-steel workstation. Beside his cutting board, Marco found a bowl, a knife, and a laminated card showing the ingredient prices in yen. The class prepared udon with mushrooms, cabbage, and broth, and the instructor noted that each serving cost about 450 yen. Marco measured flour while another participant counted yen for an optional packet of spices. He mixed the dough, rolled it flat, and cut it into narrow strips as several yen coins rested near the supply counter. During the simmering period, Marco passed a vending machine displaying tea prices in yen. He inserted 120 yen, took a bottle, and returned to the stove. “Add the noodles now,” the instructor said. Marco added them, divided the finished soup into bowls, and checked the recipe card, where the total remained listed in yen. Before leaving, he used his remaining yen to purchase a printed booklet of cooking instructions.
first_sentence: Marco entered the cooking class and placed 3,000 yen beside the registration sheet.
